albania-lalzit-rinia.description: A sandy shore on Lalzi Bay (Rinia area, Bisht-Palla beach), 20 minutes north of Durrës and 40 minutes from Tirana airport. Thigh-deep shallow water and a steady wind direction make it a good place to learn: southerly winds blow in spring, and a northerly thermal breeze in July–August. Albania is still an inexpensive, uncrowded kite destination.
albania-lalzit-rinia.rating_basis: Kitejungle lists Lalzi as one of Albania's two “popular” spots: shallow water and steady wind, “ideal for beginners”; Albania barely appears in international top lists yet
albania-lalzit-rinia.waves_note: “Thigh-deep” shallow water, mostly flat or choppy; small waves in strong southerly wind
albania-lalzit-rinia.hazards: Strong, gusty southerly winds in spring; minimal rescue infrastructure
albania-lalzit-rinia.gustiness_note: The summer northerly breeze is gentle and predictable; spring southerlies are stronger (30–40 kn at times) and less steady
albania-lalzit-rinia.crowd_note: The Kite Era school advertises “99% empty spots” — usually just a handful of kiters on the water
albania-lalzit-rinia.region: Lalzi Bay, north of Durrës, Adriatic
pros: Shallow flat water — good for beginners
Almost nobody on the water
Close to Tirana airport, inexpensive
cons: Summer wind is moderate and not daily
Few schools and little infrastructure
Spring southerlies can be too strong
albania-lalzit-rinia.wind_dir: May–June: S–SW–W; July–August: northerly thermal breeze

geraldton-point-moore.description: Point Moore is an exposed sandy point near Geraldton, a 6-hour drive north of Perth, and one of the windiest spots in Western Australia. From late November to early March a very strong southerly sea breeze blows, and a powerful left breaks on the reef. Nearby are Separation Point, Sunset Beach and Coronation Beach.
geraldton-point-moore.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: one of Australia's windiest spots, a 7 m kite most days; Point Moore is an exposed sandy point with powerful waves
geraldton-point-moore.waves_note: Powerful lefts on the Hell's Gates reef; flatter inside the reef, where local instructors teach
geraldton-point-moore.hazards: Reefs on both sides of the point, powerful waves, very strong wind and gusts, harsh sun
geraldton-point-moore.gustiness_note: The breeze builds through the day; a typical day is a 7 m kite, gusts up to ~50 kn
geraldton-point-moore.crowd_note: Uncrowded; Coronation Beach is getting more popular
pros: Very strong, reliable summer breeze
World-class waves
You can drive onto the beach
cons: Wind can be too strong — you need a 5–6 m kite
Heavy waves, reefs
Far from Perth
geraldton-point-moore.wind_dir: S–SSW (sea breeze), cross-onshore from the left
geraldton-point-moore.airport: GET — Geraldton, ~10 min; PER — Perth, ~6 h by car

gold-coast-broadwater.description: The Broadwater is a sheltered lagoon behind the Gold Coast spit with flat water and sandbanks. The Train spot is at the end of North St in Southport; nearby are KFC (Loaders Creek) and Shearwater Esplanade for beginners. The season is the warm months, when the afternoon sea breeze blows; it fades by March, and southerly winds dominate in winter.
gold-coast-broadwater.rating_basis: Locals on Seabreeze recommend the flat water opposite Sea World and The Train spot; the Broadwater is a training ground rather than a travel destination
gold-coast-broadwater.waves_note: Enclosed water with no waves; chop at high tide
gold-coast-broadwater.hazards: Boat traffic and moorings, 1–2 kn tidal current, an underwater obstacle at low tide (signposted), speed limits in channel zones
gold-coast-broadwater.gustiness_note: Best in a “clean” SE or NNW–NE; from other directions the wind is patchy because of buildings
gold-coast-broadwater.crowd_note: Few kiters, but lots of boats and moorings
pros: Flat water within the city
Good for training and freestyle
Warm water in summer
cons: Lots of boats and moorings
Gusty wind because of buildings
Current and shallows, tide-dependent
gold-coast-broadwater.wind_dir: NNW–NE (summer breeze) and SE; patchy and gusty from other directions
gold-coast-broadwater.airport: OOL — Gold Coast, ~30 min; BNE — Brisbane, ~1 h

lancelin.description: Lancelin is a fishing town 1.5–2 hours north of Perth and one of Western Australia's wind capitals. In summer a powerful southerly sea breeze blows almost daily; the lagoon behind Edward Island gives flat water, while the outer reefs offer quality left-handers. White dunes nearby, and an excellent downwinder along the coast.
lancelin.rating_basis: A legendary spot on Australia's west coast (Lancelin Ocean Classic); IKSURFMAG: breeze “almost every day” from December to February, a lagoon for everyone and reef waves; on Seabreeze it is recommended alongside Margaret River as the best for waves in WA
lancelin.waves_note: The lagoon behind the point and Edward Island is flat water; beyond the reef (~1 km) are Main Break (powerful lefts) and South Passage (long lefts); Back Beach has lefts and rights with shorebreak; the waves get blown out as the wind picks up
lancelin.hazards: Shallow reef in the lagoon at low tide, reef at Main Break if you go upwind, rocks and Lancelin Island at South Passage, shorebreak at Back Beach; if your gear breaks, the cross-onshore wind carries you far down the coast; strong sun; cars get stuck in the sand
lancelin.gustiness_note: From late November to early March the breeze blows almost every day: offshore in the morning, swinging cross-onshore by midday; windier than Perth — you need a smaller kite
lancelin.crowd_note: Lots of riders from Perth at weekends, quiet on weekdays; South Passage is popular with windsurfers, Back Beach is usually empty
lancelin.region: Western Australia, Turquoise Coast, ~1.5–2 h north of Perth
pros: Breeze almost daily December–February
Flat lagoon and reef waves in one place
A windsurf and kite classic (Lancelin Ocean Classic)
Close to Perth
cons: Shallow reef in the lagoon at low tide
Crowded at weekends
Few schools — a place for independent riders
Water cooler than in the tropics (19–23 °C)
lancelin.wind_dir: S–SSW sea breeze, cross-onshore from the left; offshore (E) in the morning

perth-woodman-point.description: Woodman Point, 10 minutes south of Fremantle, is Perth's classic spot for flat-water riding along a sandbank. In summer the “Fremantle Doctor” sea breeze blows almost daily. Launch from the car park at the western tip of the point.
perth-woodman-point.rating_basis: On the Seabreeze forum Woodman Point (“Woodies”) is called a “flat-water paradise” where international riders passing through Perth come to ride
perth-woodman-point.waves_note: Flat water along the bank/spit; heavy chop at the top of the run where you turn
perth-woodman-point.hazards: Offshore wind on the run (drifting back can take 2–3 h), weed beds, wind shadow near the bar, tugs and tankers — stay well clear of the shipping channel; you need a tide of ~0.8 m
perth-woodman-point.gustiness_note: The summer “Fremantle Doctor” sea breeze blows reliably in the afternoon; best at 20–25+ kn
perth-woodman-point.crowd_note: Usually 20–30 kiters on the run, riding right up against the bank
pros: Smooth water along the bank — speed and freestyle
Reliable summer breeze
Close to the city
cons: Offshore wind on the run — break gear and it's a long swim
Weed — you need a small fin
Crowded
Wind is irregular in winter
perth-woodman-point.wind_dir: SW–SSW (Fremantle Doctor); offshore on the main run

aruba-fishermans-huts.description: Hadicurari Beach by the fishermen's huts in Aruba's hotel zone is the island's main kite spot and the venue of an annual competition. Flat water over a shallow reef, warm sea and trade winds almost all year round. Advanced riders head to the waves at Boca Grandi in the southeast. Many schools (e.g. Armando's Kite Shack) operate right on the beach and offer boat rescue.
aruba-fishermans-huts.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG rates Aruba 5.0/5 in its guides: steady trade winds all year (usually 20–25 kn), warm turquoise water; Fishermans Huts is the island's main spot, where nearly all schools operate
aruba-fishermans-huts.waves_note: At Fishermans Huts — flat water over a large shallow reef covered in seagrass, no waves; 0.5–1 m waves in the bay and 1–2 m beyond the reef at the sports spot Boca Grandi in the island's southeast
aruba-fishermans-huts.hazards: Side-offshore wind (blows you away from shore — rescue beyond the reef is paid, ~$20), shallow reef with seagrass, windsurfers and swimmers
aruba-fishermans-huts.gustiness_note: The trade wind blows all day (strongest 11:00–15:00), but is gusty near shore because of buildings on land; further out (the “blue highway”) it's smooth
aruba-fishermans-huts.crowd_note: The island's main spot next to the hotels — schools, kiters and windsurfers share one small patch
aruba-fishermans-huts.region: Northwest coast, Noord (Palm Beach hotel zone)
pros: Trade winds almost all year, especially reliable December to August
Flat water and warm sea
Walking distance from the Noord and Palm Beach hotels
Outside the hurricane belt
cons: Side-offshore wind — don't go far beyond the reef without a school boat
Gusty near shore
Expensive

silver-rock-barbados.description: Silver Sands Beach at the southern tip of Barbados is the island's main kite and windsurf spot. The trade wind blows side-onshore, waves break on the reef, and inside there are small kickers for jumping. The wind season is December to July, with the best waves in December–February.
silver-rock-barbados.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: a famous reef break and the island's most popular kite spot; trade winds blow from December to July
silver-rock-barbados.waves_note: Reef break: waves on the reef, “kickers” inside; best waves December–February; shorebreak at high tide
silver-rock-barbados.crowd_note: The island's main spot — most kiters and windsurfers gather here
pros: Steady trade winds most of the year
Reef waves and kickers inside
Warm water all year, 15 min from the airport
cons: Reef and shorebreak — not for total beginners
Weaker wind August–October, hurricane season
Expensive island
silver-rock-barbados.wind_dir: E (trade wind), cross-onshore from the left

bulgaria-krapets-durankulak.description: Long sandy beaches in Bulgaria's far northeast — from the village of Krapets to Lake Durankulak and the Romanian border (6 km north, with Vama Veche beyond it). The Shabla and Durankulak lakes are separated from the sea by dunes, and the coast is almost undeveloped. The wind is synoptic, from the northeast; the swimming and kite season is June–September.
bulgaria-krapets-durankulak.rating_basis: The most northeasterly and least developed stretch of the Bulgarian coast — long wild beaches between Krapets and Durankulak; known mainly to Bulgarian and Romanian kiters, absent from international top lists
bulgaria-krapets-durankulak.waves_note: Open Black Sea: chop and short wind waves in northeasterly wind; calm water when there's no wind
bulgaria-krapets-durankulak.hazards: Onshore waves and surf in strong NE; no lifeguards on the wild stretches
bulgaria-krapets-durankulak.gustiness_note: Synoptic wind with no reliable summer thermal: windy days alternate with calm ones
bulgaria-krapets-durankulak.crowd_note: The beaches are long and quiet even in summer
bulgaria-krapets-durankulak.region: Shabla municipality, Dobrich, northern Black Sea coast
pros: Long wild beaches and plenty of room on the water
Inexpensive, Romania's Vama Veche close by
Warm water in summer (up to 24 °C)
cons: No reliable summer thermal — wind is irregular
Minimal infrastructure and few schools
Cold water outside summer
bulgaria-krapets-durankulak.wind_dir: NE–E (onshore / side-onshore); also N in spring and autumn
bulgaria-krapets-durankulak.airport: VAR — Varna, ~1.5 h; CND — Constanța (Romania), ~1.5 h

atins.description: A quiet village on the Preguiças River delta at the entrance to Lençóis Maranhenses National Park, with its white dunes and freshwater lagoons. The river forms a huge shallow lagoon with warm flat water — ideal for learning and freestyle — and there are waves in the ocean beyond the sandbanks. There are no roads, only boats and licensed jeeps, so people come here for wild nature and space.
atins.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG calls Atins one of the best places in Brazil: a huge shallow river-mouth lagoon for all levels and wind “almost guaranteed” from July to mid-January; Brazilian press calls it “Maranhão's kitesurfing paradise”
atins.waves_note: Knee-deep flat water in the river-mouth lagoon; chop and waves in the ocean beyond the sandbanks
atins.hazards: Shifting sandbanks and current in the river mouth on the ebb/flood tide; far from medical help
atins.gustiness_note: Trade wind with almost no breaks: windless days in season are rare
atins.crowd_note: The beaches are huge and empty, plenty of room even at the peak of the season
atins.region: Maranhão, mouth of the Preguiças River by Lençóis Maranhenses National Park
pros: Huge shallow flat-water lagoon
Few people
Unique nature: the Lençóis dunes and lagoons
Steady wind July to December
cons: Tricky logistics: ~5 h from São Luís, then a boat or jeep
Deep sand, spread-out village
Little entertainment, weak internet
atins.wind_dir: E–ENE, cross-onshore (from the right at the lagoon launch)
atins.airport: SLZ — São Luís, ~5 h (via Barreirinhas); PHB — Parnaíba, ~5 h

barra-grande-piaui.description: A former fishing village on Piauí state's short coastline between Jeri and the Parnaíba delta. The main draw is the tides: at low tide a huge shallow flat-water lagoon forms along the beach, ideal for learning and freestyle, and there's another big lagoon downwind. Schools: Buena Onda Brasil (the first in the village), BGKite, Ventos do Mar, Barra Grande Kite Camp.
barra-grande-piaui.rating_basis: Wannakitesurf — “Great” for all levels; season July–January with 20–30 kn wind; the whole village has rebuilt itself around kite tourism (UFMG research) but remains calmer and cheaper than Jeri
barra-grande-piaui.waves_note: At low tide a huge shallow flat-water “pool”, chop at high tide; no big waves. A big flat lagoon 3 km downwind
barra-grande-piaui.hazards: Shallow water at low tide (risk of hitting the bottom when you fall), fishing nets and posts near the shore
barra-grande-piaui.gustiness_note: Steady trade wind, strongest in the afternoon
barra-grande-piaui.crowd_note: Almost empty on weekdays, a bit busier at weekends; the beach is 4 km long — plenty of room
pros: Shallow flat water at low tide
Few people and a relaxed atmosphere
Steady trade wind July–January
Reachable without a jeep (45 min from Parnaíba)
cons: Very tide-dependent: sometimes too shallow
Less infrastructure and nightlife than Jeri
January–May is the rainy season
barra-grande-piaui.airport: PHB — Parnaíba, ~45 min; JJD — Jijoca de Jericoacoara, ~3 h by jeep

cumbuco.description: A fishing village 35 km from Fortaleza that has become one of Brazil's main kite hubs. A wide sandy beach with a steady side-onshore trade wind, and 6 km downwind the freshwater Cauípe lagoon with flat water for learning and freestyle. A handy starting point for downwinders and kite safaris along the Ceará coast.
cumbuco.rating_basis: One of Brazil's best-known kite resorts: Wannakitesurf — “Great” for all levels, wind almost every day from August to December; features in Russian-language top lists (kiteteam.ru) alongside Jericoacoara
cumbuco.waves_note: On the ocean — chop and small surf (bump-and-jump); flat water in the Cauípe (6 km downwind) and Tabuba lagoons
cumbuco.hazards: Surf and a 1–2 knot current on the ocean, jangada fishing boats and other craft; petty theft in Fortaleza
cumbuco.gustiness_note: Trade wind boosted by thermals off the dunes: steady, picks up in the afternoon, dies down by night
cumbuco.crowd_note: Plenty of room on weekdays, crowded at weekends; the main crowd is by the Eco Paradise hotel — 150 m up- or downwind it's already spacious; the Cauípe lagoon fills up by midday
pros: Wind almost every day from July to January
Warm water all year — no wetsuit needed
Flat-water lagoons Cauípe and Tabuba nearby
Close to Fortaleza airport, well-developed infrastructure
cons: Crowded at weekends
Surf on the ocean — harder for beginners than the lagoon
Fortaleza is unsafe at night

jericoacoara.description: A trendy village among the dunes in a national park in northwest Ceará — the poster child of Brazilian kiting. The beach by the point itself is mostly used by windsurfers and advanced kiters in the waves, while most kiters head to the wide neighbouring Preá, the Paraíso and Azul lagoons, and downwinders to Guriú and Tatajuba. Great social scene, restaurants and sunsets from the dune.
jericoacoara.rating_basis: Brazil's iconic spot and a stop on the GKA Kite-Surf World Cup (2024); features in Russian-language world top lists; the country's best-known surf resort, with lagoons and downwinders nearby
jericoacoara.waves_note: A 1–2 m right-hander at the point (claimed by windsurfers), chop and small waves on the beach; flat water in the Paraíso and Azul lagoons and on downwinders to Guriú
jericoacoara.hazards: Waves and rocks at the point, windsurfers in the waves, buggies and boats at the lagoons; strong sun
jericoacoara.gustiness_note: Steady trade wind “day and night”; right by the shore under the point the wind is weaker and choppy in the waves
jericoacoara.crowd_note: The resort is busy, with lots of windsurfers on the wave at the point; kiters head to Preá (12 km) and the lagoons, where buggies converge by midday
jericoacoara.vibe_note: Famous nightlife: sunset on the dune, caipirinha bars on the main street, forró parties.
pros: Steady trade wind from July to January
Downwinders and flat-water lagoons nearby
Lively resort atmosphere, plenty of accommodation and restaurants
Warm water, no wetsuit
cons: Crowded and expensive
Long journey: ~4–5 h from Fortaleza over sand, or a flight to Jijoca
Waves and crowds at the point — not for beginners
jericoacoara.airport: JJD — Jijoca de Jericoacoara, ~30 min; FOR — Fortaleza, ~4–5 h

paracuru.description: A reef wave spot 3 km from the town of Paracuru, about 1.5 h west of Fortaleza. The trade wind blows side-shore from the right, and the wave breaks on the reef and suits down-the-line riding. The reliable wind season is July to January, strongest in September–October.
paracuru.rating_basis: Surf-Magazin: the area's best-known windsurf/kite spot with the biggest waves in Ceará, today “firmly in kiters' hands”; kitejungle — ~325 windy days a year
paracuru.waves_note: The wave breaks on the reef further out — one of the biggest in Ceará, up to 2 (occasionally 3) m; chop inside the reef, increasing with the tide
paracuru.hazards: Rocks just below the surface at low tide, fish traps (currais) downwind, shorebreak from 2 h before to 2 h after high tide
paracuru.gustiness_note: The trade wind is steady and half a Beaufort force to a full force stronger than in Cumbuco
paracuru.crowd_note: Noticeably quieter than Cumbuco and Jericoacoara
pros: One of the best waves in Ceará
Very steady, strong trade wind July–January
Fewer people than at neighbouring spots
cons: Not for beginners
Submerged rocks at low tide, strong shorebreak at high tide
Little infrastructure right at the spot
paracuru.wind_dir: ESE–SE (trade wind), side-shore from the right

prea.description: A former fishing village 12 km from Jericoacoara that has become the area's kite capital, with kite hotels and schools lining the beach. A wide beach with a steady side-shore trade wind, shallow water at low tide and kickers further out suits all levels. Downwinders to Jeri and Guriú start here, and there are flat-water lagoons nearby.
prea.rating_basis: The main kite base of the Jeri area: a wide beach with side-shore wind, according to locals over 300 windy days a year; Unplug rates the spot as beginner-friendly; dozens of schools and kite hotels
prea.waves_note: Wide beach: flat and shallow near shore at low tide, further out chop and 1–1.5 m waves — kickers for jumping; shallow lagoons nearby (Riacho Doce, Lagoa Azul)
prea.hazards: Waves and current at high tide, rocks in some parts of the beach, buggies on the beach
prea.gustiness_note: Steady side-shore trade wind with no obstructions; picks up in the afternoon
prea.crowd_note: The beach is long and wide — noticeably more room than in Jeri, though it gets busy by the kite hotels at peak season
prea.region: Ceará, Cruz (12 km east of Jericoacoara)
pros: Plenty of room on the water
Suits everyone from beginners to freestylers
Downwinders and lagoons nearby
Wind almost every day July–January
cons: Pricey, accommodation is mostly kite hotels
Far from Fortaleza
February–May is the rainy, light-wind season
prea.airport: JJD — Jijoca de Jericoacoara, ~20 min; FOR — Fortaleza, ~4 h

sao-miguel-do-gostoso.description: A laid-back resort town on the north coast of Rio Grande do Norte, known as “Ceará without the crowds”. The main spot is Ponta do Santo Cristo: a sandbank gives flat water, and waves appear at high tide and on the reef. Nearby are the natural pools of Monte Alegre, the Tourinhos and Lagoa do Sal waves, a 30 km downwinder to Maracajaú and the Parrachos reef pools near Perobas. Schools include Idilico Kite Club.
sao-miguel-do-gostoso.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: “the best wind conditions in Brazil, but without the crowds”, 90–100% rideable days from September to February; a varied set of spots from flat water to waves
sao-miguel-do-gostoso.waves_note: At Ponta do Santo Cristo a sandbank ~300 m offshore gives flat water, with waves at high tide and on the outer reef; at Monte Alegre waist-deep natural pools form at low tide; Tourinhos and Lagoa do Sal have waves
sao-miguel-do-gostoso.hazards: Coral on the Tourinhos downwinder (instructor needed), reef at Santo Cristo, sea turtles near Monte Alegre; the ~30 km downwinder to Maracajaú requires good fitness
sao-miguel-do-gostoso.gustiness_note: Very consistent trade wind blowing along the shore; almost no rain in season
sao-miguel-do-gostoso.crowd_note: Quiet and spacious — the main difference from Ceará
sao-miguel-do-gostoso.region: Rio Grande do Norte, north coast (≈100 km from Natal)
pros: Wind almost every day from September to February
Few people
Variety: flat water, waves, reef pools, downwinders
Only ~1.5 h from Natal airport
cons: Less choice of schools and accommodation than in Ceará
Quiet nightlife
Some spots need transport (buggy)
sao-miguel-do-gostoso.wind_dir: E–SE, cross-onshore from the right (parallel to the shore)
sao-miguel-do-gostoso.airport: NAT — Natal (São Gonçalo do Amarante), ~1 h 20 min

taiba.description: A village an hour's drive north of Cumbuco, world-famous for its lagoon of perfectly flat water, where the freestyle elite train and GKA finals are held. The lagoon is narrow and elongated and gets shallow at its downwind end — it's a place for confident riders, while beginners are more comfortable at Cauípe. On the ocean by the Tramuntana pousada there are waves for bump-and-jump and wave riding.
taiba.rating_basis: The Taíba lagoon is “Brazil's main freestyle arena”: it hosted GKA Freestyle-Kite World Cup finals (2022, 2025); Wannakitesurf rates the ocean spot as “Great”
taiba.waves_note: A narrow, elongated lagoon on the northern edge of the village — benchmark flat water with no chop; on the ocean by the Tramuntana pousada, waves ~1 m, sometimes bigger
taiba.hazards: Rocks in the middle and shallows at the downwind end of the lagoon; heavy freestyle traffic
taiba.gustiness_note: Steady trade wind, slightly stronger than in Cumbuco/Cauípe; smooth wind in the lagoon
taiba.crowd_note: The lagoon is small and packed with pro freestylers who don't give way much; almost empty in the morning. The ocean spot is quiet on weekdays
taiba.region: Ceará, São Gonçalo do Amarante (65 km from Fortaleza)
pros: One of the world's best freestyle lagoons
Wind a bit stronger than in Cumbuco
Ocean waves as well
Easy to combine with Cumbuco and Paracuru (downwinder)
cons: The lagoon is small and crowded
Little infrastructure — one barraca by the lagoon
You need a buggy or 4×4 to reach the northern part

lake-silvaplana.description: The high-altitude Lake Silvaplana (1790 m) near St. Moritz is one of the best-known kite spots in the Alps. From June to September the Maloja thermal wind blows almost daily at 20–25 knots, peaking in the afternoon. In winter the lake freezes over and snowkiters and skiers ride on it.
lake-silvaplana.rating_basis: A classic of Alpine kiting: in summer ~80% windy days thanks to the Maloja wind, in winter snowkiting on the frozen lake; downsides are cold water, thin air and Swiss prices
lake-silvaplana.waves_note: In summer — chop, no waves or shorebreak; in winter the lake freezes and becomes a snowkite playground
lake-silvaplana.hazards: Cold water and cool evenings; ride no closer than 50 m to shore, one permitted entry point; in winter only on confirmed ice
lake-silvaplana.gustiness_note: The Maloja wind is a reliable valley thermal: starts around 11:00–13:00, peaks 15:00–17:00 (20–25 kn), dies down by 18:00–19:00
lake-silvaplana.crowd_note: In the summer season lots of kiters and windsurfers on the water in the afternoon; one official water entry point
lake-silvaplana.region: Graubünden, Upper Engadine, ~1790 m, near St. Moritz
pros: Very reliable summer thermal (~80% of days)
Snowkiting on the ice in winter
Incredible Alpine views
No shorebreak
cons: Cold water (max ~18 °C in early August)
Thin air — you need kites one size bigger
Expensive Switzerland
Crowded at peak season
lake-silvaplana.wind_dir: SW (Maloja wind) — cross-onshore from the right
lake-silvaplana.airport: ZRH — Zurich ~2 h (up to 3 h) / MXP — Milan Malpensa ~2 h

antofagasta-playa-amarilla.description: A city beach in the south of Antofagasta, a large port city on the edge of the Atacama Desert. Riding is best in the southern summer (December–February), when a steady daytime breeze blows in from the ocean. The water is cold because of the Humboldt Current.
antofagasta-playa-amarilla.rating_basis: A local spot without wide international fame; kitejungle notes ~157 windy days, with December–February the best months; travellers on Seabreeze rode here on 10–12 m kites
antofagasta-playa-amarilla.waves_note: Pacific coast: chop and waves, nothing outstanding for wave riding
antofagasta-playa-amarilla.hazards: Cold water, rocky stretches of shore, waves
antofagasta-playa-amarilla.gustiness_note: Mostly a daytime breeze, more reliable in summer
pros: Empty water
Dry, sunny climate
A city with infrastructure close by
cons: Cold water 16–22 °C
Short season
Little information and few schools

salinas-del-rey.description: An up-and-coming spot on Colombia's Caribbean coast, an hour's drive from Barranquilla and Cartagena. Strong trade winds from December to April and waves have made it a stop on the GKA kite-surf world tour. Infrastructure is modest (a kite hostel and a few camps), but cities with entertainment are close by; for flat water there's neighbouring Puerto Velero.
salinas-del-rey.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: prime season December–March with average wind of 20–25 kn; the spot hosted GKA Kite-Surf World Tour events in 2022 and 2023; chosen over Cabo de la Vela, which is remote and, according to the guide, “gusty, full stop”
salinas-del-rey.waves_note: An open beach with waves — a wave and strapless spot (GKA Kite-Surf stop); no flat water — for that, head to the bay at Puerto Velero (light chop) or to Cabo de la Vela
salinas-del-rey.hazards: Waves and currents; unregistered moto-taxis are dangerous on the roads; the last kilometre to Puerto Velero is sand and scrub
salinas-del-rey.gustiness_note: Strong, dry trade wind (often over 25 kn in season); steadier than gusty Cabo de la Vela
salinas-del-rey.crowd_note: Wide, spacious beaches; riders come from all over the world in season, but it never feels crowded
salinas-del-rey.region: Atlántico, Caribbean coast between Barranquilla and Cartagena
pros: Strong, steady wind from December to March
Good waves for wave riding
Close to Cartagena and Barranquilla
Few people
cons: No flat water — not for beginners
Modest infrastructure, occasional power cuts
Off-season from August to November
salinas-del-rey.airport: BAQ — Barranquilla, ~45 min–1 h; CTG — Cartagena, ~1 h 20 min

boa-vista-praia-chaves.description: Praia de Chaves by the Iberostar hotel south of Sal Rei is the main teaching spot on Boa Vista; when there are waves, lessons move to a boat. The northeast trade wind blows from November to May. The island has other spots too: Morabeza near town (flat water), the Rio lagoon and the wave spot Varandinha for experienced riders.
boa-vista-praia-chaves.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: 15–30 kn trade wind in high season (November–May), a variety of spots from flat water to waves; kitejungle — ~330 windy days a year
boa-vista-praia-chaves.waves_note: December–February — waves (lessons from a boat); neighbouring beaches range from flat water to waves of ~2 m
boa-vista-praia-chaves.hazards: Shorebreak and waves in winter; at Varandinha — open ocean downwind and volcanic rocks, no lifeguards; gusty offshore wind at Morabeza and Rio
boa-vista-praia-chaves.gustiness_note: The trade wind is steady; gusty offshore at Morabeza and the Rio lagoon
pros: Strong, steady trade wind November–May
Variety: flat water, waves, downwinders
Warm all year, airport nearby
cons: In winter the main beach can have waves and shorebreak
You need a 4x4 for the remote spots
Noticeably lighter wind in summer

sal-kite-beach.description: A flat desert island with the resort town of Santa Maria and steady trade winds all winter. Most schools operate at Kite Beach, a 20-minute taxi ride from town: side-onshore wind, chop and small waves. For advanced riders there's the legendary Ponta Preta wave and Ponta Leme. Nightlife, diving and direct charters from Europe.
sal-kite-beach.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: Cape Verde's most popular kite destination — steady, strong trade wind from late October to April, almost no windless days in winter; Ponta Preta is an iconic world-tour wave
sal-kite-beach.waves_note: Kite Beach — chop and waves with shorebreak; Ponta Preta — a powerful world-class wave (GKA stop), pros only; Ponta Leme — a left-hander with the right swell
sal-kite-beach.hazards: Shorebreak, currents, rocks at Ponta Preta; strong sun
sal-kite-beach.gustiness_note: Steady, strong trade wind from November to May; noticeably weaker in summer
sal-kite-beach.crowd_note: Kite Beach gets crowded in high season — schools teach right there; better to ride at lunchtime or towards evening
pros: Steady, strong trade wind November–May
Warm in winter (around 25 °C)
World-class waves for advanced riders
Resort infrastructure in Santa Maria
cons: Long flight (~6 h from Europe, connecting flights from Russia)
Shorebreak and waves — harder for beginners than lagoons
Crowded at Kite Beach in season
Expensive car hire
sal-kite-beach.wind_dir: NE, cross-onshore from the left (Kite Beach); offshore at Ponta Preta

cyprus-larnaca-kiti-softades.description: The shallow coast southwest of Larnaca — from Kiti lighthouse (Faros) to Softades and Mazotos — is Cyprus's main kite area. In summer a steady daytime wind of 12–20 kn blows, and the shallow warm water suits learning and freeriding. The Softades → Faros downwinder is popular. Larnaca airport is 15–20 minutes away.
cyprus-larnaca-kiti-softades.rating_basis: Kitejungle: steady 12–20 kn wind, season April–October, best months May–September, shallow water; the big international top lists barely mention Cyprus
cyprus-larnaca-kiti-softades.waves_note: A long (10+ km) shallow bay southwest of Larnaca: mostly flat water and chop, hardly any waves
cyprus-larnaca-kiti-softades.hazards: Sources name no particular hazards; downwinders need organised backup
cyprus-larnaca-kiti-softades.gustiness_note: Steady daytime wind that holds until sunset; moderate strength — you need medium and large kites
cyprus-larnaca-kiti-softades.crowd_note: The bay is long, plenty of room; there's a Softades → Faros downwind safari (~5 km) “away from the crowds”
pros: Very close to Larnaca airport
Shallow warm water, long bay
Season from April to October
Large Russian-speaking community on Cyprus
cons: Moderate wind, rarely strong
Irregular wind outside summer

fehmarn.description: Fehmarn is a Baltic island between Kiel and Denmark, linked to the mainland by a bridge over the Fehmarnsund. With more than ten spots on different shores, you can ride here in almost any wind direction: Orth in a westerly, Grüner Brink in a northeasterly, Wulfener Hals and Gold on the south coast. Shallow water in many places makes it easy to learn; the season for travellers is May–October.
fehmarn.rating_basis: Germany's main kite island: more than ten surf spots for different winds; it hosts the German kite championship (Kitesurf-Masters) and used to host the Surf-Festival (de/en.wikipedia)
fehmarn.waves_note: Baltic: from flat water in the shallows (Orth in W, inner bays) to chop and small wind waves on the open beaches (Grüner Brink in NE)
fehmarn.hazards: Cold water; rocks off some shores; bird protection and swimming zones — kiting only in permitted areas; shipping traffic near the Fehmarnsund
fehmarn.gustiness_note: Frontal Baltic wind, steady over the water; gustier near shores with buildings and hills
fehmarn.crowd_note: In summer (July–September) and on windy weekends, lots of kiters from all over Germany
pros: A spot for every wind direction
Shallows for learning, many schools
Easy to reach by car (Hamburg ~1 h 45 min)
Well-developed kite infrastructure and campsites
cons: Cold water (up to ~19 °C in summer), almost always a wetsuit
Changeable weather and wind, lighter wind in summer
Crowded in summer
fehmarn.wind_dir: Almost any: W — Orth, NE — Grüner Brink, S–SW — Wulfen/Gold; pick the spot to suit the direction
fehmarn.airport: HAM — Hamburg, ~1 h 45 min (~150 km); LBC — Lübeck, ~1 h 15 min

sankt-peter-ording.description: Sankt Peter-Ording is a resort on the Eiderstedt peninsula with one of Europe's largest beaches: 12 km long and up to 2 km wide at low tide. Kiters ride in a designated water-sports zone on Ording beach; at low tide shallow tidal lagoons with flat water form. Wind off the North Sea blows often, but the water is cold and conditions depend heavily on the tides (up to 3 m).
sankt-peter-ording.rating_basis: A legendary German spot: from 2006 to 2015 it hosted the annual Kitesurf World Cup, the world's biggest kite event (>130,000 spectators, de.wikipedia); a huge beach 12 km long and up to 2 km wide at low tide
sankt-peter-ording.waves_note: At low tide flat water on the sandbars and in tidal pools; at high tide and in westerly winds, chop and small North Sea waves
sankt-peter-ording.hazards: Tidal currents in the channels (Priele) and fast-rising water; cold water; kiting only in the designated zone — swimming and land-yachting zones nearby; the Wadden Sea is a national park
sankt-peter-ording.gustiness_note: Open sea and a flat shore — the wind is steady; squalls when fronts pass through
sankt-peter-ording.crowd_note: The beach is huge, with the kite zone on Ording beach; lots of kiters on windy summer weekends, but there's enough room
sankt-peter-ording.region: Schleswig-Holstein, Eiderstedt peninsula — North Sea (Wadden Sea)
pros: Huge beach, plenty of room to launch
Shallows and flat water at low tide — easy to learn
Frequent, steady sea wind
You can drive right onto the beach (paid)
cons: Very tide-dependent (range up to 3 m)
Cold water and a cool climate
Long walk to the water at low tide

hvide-sande-ringkobing-fjord.description: Hvide Sande is a fishing town on a narrow sand spit between the North Sea and Ringkøbing Fjord, a shallow brackish lagoon of almost 300 km². In westerly winds the fjord offers shallow flat water for learning, freestyle and foiling, while the sea side of the spit has waves. It's windy almost all year, but the water is cold; the travel season is May–October.
hvide-sande-ringkobing-fjord.rating_basis: One of Northern Europe's main kite regions: a huge shallow lagoon (~300 km², 2–3 m deep) for flat water right next to North Sea waves; popular with German, Danish and Dutch kiters
hvide-sande-ringkobing-fjord.waves_note: In the fjord (a lagoon 2–3 m deep, shallower near the shore) — flat water and chop; on the North Sea beaches on the other side of the spit — waves
hvide-sande-ringkobing-fjord.hazards: Cold water; on the fjord in a westerly the wind pushes you towards the middle of the lagoon; currents by the Hvide Sande lock and channel; at sea — rip currents and groynes; bird reserves in the south of the fjord
hvide-sande-ringkobing-fjord.gustiness_note: Westerlies off the North Sea are steady; on the fjord the wind comes over the dunes of the spit, so it's a little gusty right by the shore
hvide-sande-ringkobing-fjord.crowd_note: The fjord is huge; it only gets crowded at the main launches at weekends
hvide-sande-ringkobing-fjord.region: West Jutland, Holmsland Klit spit between the North Sea and Ringkøbing Fjord
pros: Huge shallow flat-water lagoon
North Sea waves close by — two spots 5 minutes apart
Frequent strong wind
Few people on the water
cons: Cold water (up to ~18 °C in summer), always a wetsuit
Changeable weather, rain
Far from major airports
hvide-sande-ringkobing-fjord.wind_dir: W–SW–NW: side-offshore/side-shore on the fjord (flat water), side-onshore at sea
hvide-sande-ringkobing-fjord.airport: BLL — Billund, ~1 h 15 min (~100 km); EBJ — Esbjerg, ~1 h

cabarete-kite-beach.description: A cosmopolitan town on the north coast of the Dominican Republic and one of the Caribbean's kite capitals. Kite Beach is protected by a reef: inside there's chop for learning and freestyle, outside there are waves, especially powerful in winter. Nearby are the flat-water La Boca lagoon, the Encuentro wave spot and Cabarete Bay; all around are dozens of schools, kite camps (including Kevin Langeree's) and lively nightlife.
cabarete-kite-beach.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG — 4.5/5: wind all year, “well over 250 rideable days” in a good season; a classic Caribbean kite resort with flat water and waves for all levels
cabarete-kite-beach.waves_note: Inside the reef — wind chop and small rolling waves; on the reef — waves, with powerful swells in winter (Dec–Mar); flat water in the La Boca lagoon (river mouth), reef rights at Encuentro
cabarete-kite-beach.hazards: Reef and rock shelves at the entry in places, powerful winter swell, a rock shelf near the shore at Encuentro; hurricane season June–November; chaotic road traffic
cabarete-kite-beach.gustiness_note: Trade wind boosted by the daytime thermal; often light in the morning, the best hours are after midday
cabarete-kite-beach.crowd_note: Kite Beach is the most popular spot: from 15 kn it gets very crowded (up to 50 kites in a small patch); quieter at lunchtime and in the evening, or in Cabarete Bay
cabarete-kite-beach.vibe_note: Bars, restaurants and clubs sit right on Cabarete beach, busy in the evenings.
pros: Wind almost all year, best June–August
Everything in one place: chop, reef waves, flat lagoon
Huge infrastructure: schools, shops, repairs
Puerto Plata airport nearby
cons: Very crowded at Kite Beach
Often no wind in the morning
September–November is lighter and rainier, hurricane season
cabarete-kite-beach.airport: POP — Puerto Plata, ~45 min; STI — Santiago, ~1.5 h

dahab-lagoon.description: A former Bedouin village with a laid-back vibe, diving and a large Russian-speaking community. The kite lagoon by the centres is shallow and waist-deep, with flat water and side-offshore wind; advanced riders go further downwind and to Assala. The Gulf of Aqaba funnels the wind, so Dahab is windier than Hurghada.
dahab-lagoon.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: Egypt's windiest spot thanks to the Gulf of Aqaba effect, a shallow kite lagoon for beginners and a variety of spots for advanced riders; tourist reviews on tonkosti.ru give 10/10 for shallow water and safe learning; IKSURFMAG rating — 4.0
dahab-lagoon.waves_note: The kite lagoon is flat, no shorebreak; further downwind — chop, and at the reefs (Assala, Napoleon Reef) waves for advanced riders
dahab-lagoon.hazards: Offshore wind, coral and rocks at Assala (wear shoes), gusts off the mountains
dahab-lagoon.gustiness_note: The Gulf of Aqaba works like a wind tunnel — the wind is stronger than at other Egyptian spots; it comes off the mountains in gusts and is patchy near shore in places
dahab-lagoon.crowd_note: The kite lagoon is right next to the centres — busy near shore in season; kiting in the windsurf zone (Area 4) is banned from 9:00 to 15:00
pros: Strong, frequent wind (Gulf of Aqaba effect)
Shallow flat lagoon for learning
Cheap accommodation and food, a “hippie” vibe
World-class diving and freediving
cons: In winter the wind is “3 days on / 3 days off” and it's chilly on the water
Restricted kiting zones
Offshore wind — you need a rescue service
Little alcohol in restaurants
dahab-lagoon.wind_dir: N–NNE, side-offshore from the left / side-shore

el-gouna.description: A resort town near Hurghada with several kite beaches; the main one is Mangroovy / Buzzha Beach in the north, with a shallow lagoon of several km² and waist-deep water. The northerly wind blows side-on from the left and picks up by midday; beyond the reef there's room for freestyle and wing foiling. Good infrastructure: hotels, bars, parties.
el-gouna.rating_basis: One of Egypt's best-known kite destinations: big shallow “waist-deep” lagoons, wind almost all year, many centres with hotels; guides (Sportif, surf-magazin, KBC) note the steady side-shore wind; IKSURFMAG rating — 3.5
el-gouna.waves_note: Flat or light chop in the lagoon; beyond the reef (≈200 m) — chop and sometimes small waves
el-gouna.hazards: Coral, sharp shells and dead coral blocks — wear shoes; reef along the edges of the lagoon; kiting banned after 17:00 (coast guard)
el-gouna.gustiness_note: Steady northerly wind, boosted by the mountains; less stable in winter — both strong and light days
el-gouna.crowd_note: Mangroovy gets busy in season, but the centres split the water into zones (lessons / free riding / beyond the reef)
el-gouna.region: Red Sea, 25 km north of Hurghada
el-gouna.vibe_note: El Gouna's marina and centre: bars, restaurants and clubs 10–15 minutes from the spot.
pros: Huge shallow lagoon — ideal for learning
Wind almost all year
Well-developed infrastructure and many centres
30 min from Hurghada airport
cons: Tides: in summer at full moon the lagoon can dry out for a few hours
Access to kite beaches is paid / through the centres
Crowded in season
Very hot in summer
el-gouna.wind_dir: N–NNW, side-shore / side-onshore from the left

hamata.description: A wide sandy beach with a kite centre on the southern Egyptian Red Sea coast, about 2.5 h from Marsa Alam. A waist-deep shallow zone and side-onshore northerly wind suit learning, and further out towards the islands there's room for freestyle. Nearby are the Kite Village camp and hotels with transfers.
hamata.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: a very spacious sandy beach, a large waist-deep zone for beginners, wind all year; the spot is described as popular with kiters
hamata.waves_note: Flat or light chop, even flatter at low tide; no waves or shorebreak
hamata.hazards: Reefs around three islands further offshore; sun and heat in summer
hamata.gustiness_note: The wind is usually a bit stronger in the morning and drops by a few knots after lunch
hamata.crowd_note: A popular spot, but the beach is very wide — enough room for everyone
pros: Wind almost all year
Large shallow zone for beginners
No waves or shorebreak, no sea urchins
Crystal-clear water
cons: Remote: ~2.5 h from the airport
Very hot in summer
Little infrastructure outside the camp/hotels

hurghada-el-ahyaa.description: The northern outskirts of Hurghada (El Ahyaa area), with several shallow lagoons where Russian-speaking kite schools are based. Depth 0.5–1 m, a sandy bottom with no coral or urchins, almost flat water. Handy if you're staying in a Hurghada hotel: schools pick you up from the hotel, and El Gouna is 10–15 min away.
hurghada-el-ahyaa.rating_basis: As a spot in its own right, Hurghada falls short of El Gouna and Soma Bay (according to international guides), but the El Ahyaa area is the main base of Russian-speaking schools: shallow enclosed lagoons with a sandy bottom, convenient for learning
hurghada-el-ahyaa.waves_note: Sheltered shallow lagoons: almost no waves, light chop in strong wind
hurghada-el-ahyaa.hazards: Shallow water (falls onto the bottom), coral outside the lagoons, strong sun; kiting banned after 17:00
hurghada-el-ahyaa.gustiness_note: The same steady northerly wind as in El Gouna; lighter and less stable in winter
hurghada-el-ahyaa.crowd_note: The lagoons are divided between schools; some spots are for their own students only
hurghada-el-ahyaa.region: Red Sea, northern Hurghada (between Hurghada and El Gouna)
pros: Many Russian-speaking instructors
Shallow sandy-bottom lagoon — get up on the board fast
Close to Hurghada hotels and the airport
Wind almost all year
cons: Small lagoons — cramped for advanced riders
Simpler infrastructure than El Gouna
Hot in summer, a 3–5 mm wetsuit needed in winter

ras-sudr.description: The Gulf of Suez coast in western Sinai, 2–2.5 h from Cairo: several kite camps and centres along 40 km of beaches. The wind accelerates down the gulf and blows almost every day; at low tide flat lagoons and waist-deep shallows open up. A relaxed atmosphere, but little infrastructure outside the centres.
ras-sudr.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: 16–25 knots almost daily from March to November, huge shallows at low tide, suits all levels and isn't overcrowded; foreign kite guides see the spot mainly as a “weekend” place for Cairo residents; IKSURFMAG rating — 4.0
ras-sudr.waves_note: At low tide — flat lagoons and waist-deep shallows stretching out ~2 km; at high tide chop and kickers, with waves in places by the reef
ras-sudr.hazards: Reefs and chop beyond the shallows at high tide, strong gusts in late summer; sun
ras-sudr.gustiness_note: The Gulf of Suez wind blows as if through a tunnel, usually steady; in late August–September gusts over 30 knots
ras-sudr.crowd_note: The centres are spread along 40 km of coast — plenty of room, busy only at Kite Beach on peak days
pros: Very windy from March to November
Huge shallows at low tide — easy to learn
Few people on the water
Dolphins on windless days
cons: Far from airports (Cairo ~2.5 h, Sharm ~3 h)
You need a car — centres are far apart
Many centres close in winter
Weak internet
ras-sudr.wind_dir: N–NNW, side-shore / side-onshore (depends on the centre)
ras-sudr.airport: CAI — Cairo, ~2.5 h; SSH — Sharm El Sheikh, ~3 h

safaga-shams.description: A quiet town south of Soma Bay with a kite and windsurf centre at the Shams hotels. In the morning the wind is slightly offshore, swinging along the shore after lunch; there's a flat teaching zone and shallows for launching. A budget alternative to neighbouring Soma Bay.
safaga-shams.rating_basis: Sportif and surf-magazin: suits all levels, flat water and a shallow launch zone, one of the cheapest kite/windsurf spots on the Red Sea; the wind is a bit lighter than in Soma Bay, and Safaga has historically been more of a windsurf destination
safaga-shams.waves_note: Flat water with wind chop, plus a flat teaching zone; no or weak shorebreak
safaga-shams.hazards: Isolated coral heads in the launch zone, offshore wind in the morning; kiting banned after 17:00
safaga-shams.gustiness_note: The thermal wind is strongest in summer; usually 0.5–1 Beaufort force lighter than in neighbouring Soma Bay
safaga-shams.crowd_note: Quieter than El Gouna and Soma Bay; lots of regular guests
safaga-shams.region: Red Sea, 55 km south of Hurghada
pros: Inexpensive by Red Sea standards
Flat water and a shallow launch zone
Fewer people than in El Gouna
cons: Lighter wind than in Soma Bay
Offshore wind in the morning
Little infrastructure outside the hotels
safaga-shams.wind_dir: N–NW: side-offshore from the left in the morning, side-shore from the left after ~11:00

sharm-nabq.description: Nabq Bay, 10–15 min from Sharm El Sheikh airport — the Sinai resort most popular with Russians. Kite centres operate on hotel beaches, riding over a shallow reef flat in a northerly wind blowing along the shore. Convenient for trying kiting on a beach holiday; for stronger wind, people head to Dahab (~1 h).
sharm-nabq.rating_basis: Small hotel-based centres in Nabq Bay; reviews on Yandex Maps (EasyKite — 5.0 from 16 ratings) mention good wind in the Nabq area; as a kite destination it falls short of Dahab and El Gouna, but it's convenient for holidaymakers in Sharm
sharm-nabq.waves_note: Flat or light chop over the shallow reef flat by the hotels; no waves
sharm-nabq.hazards: Coral and a shallow reef flat (wear shoes, careful at low tide), sea urchins, strong sun
sharm-nabq.gustiness_note: The same northerly Gulf of Aqaba wind as in Dahab, but a bit lighter and less regular in winter
sharm-nabq.crowd_note: A few schools on hotel beaches, not many people on the water
sharm-nabq.region: Sinai, Red Sea (Gulf of Aqaba, north of Sharm)
pros: 10–15 min from the airport, lots of hotels
Schools with Russian-speaking service
Warm water all year
Shallows for learning
cons: Lighter and less steady wind than in Dahab
Shallow coral flat — riding depends on the tide
Small hotel-based centres, little room for advanced riders

soma-bay.description: A private resort peninsula 45 km south of Hurghada with five hotels, golf and kite centres. The northwesterly wind blows offshore/along the shore over a big flat-water bay; at low tide the shallows dry out, so a lot of teaching is done from boats. Downwinders to Tobia Island are popular.
soma-bay.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG and TheKiteSpot: flat turquoise water for freestyle and learning, one of Egypt's windiest spots (80–90% windy days in season), strong centres (7Bft, KBC); the downside is the offshore wind and mandatory rescue service; IKSURFMAG rating — 3.5
soma-bay.waves_note: Offshore wind — practically no waves or shorebreak, flat water; light chop beyond the reef
soma-bay.hazards: Offshore wind (blows you out to sea), shallow coral, strong sun; kiting banned after 17:00
soma-bay.gustiness_note: The offshore wind comes over the peninsula — a bit gustier near shore; usually 2–4 knots stronger than forecast
soma-bay.crowd_note: A resort peninsula with several hotels; at peak season it's noticeably busy by the centres, but the bay is big
soma-bay.region: Red Sea, between Hurghada and Safaga
pros: Some of the steadiest and strongest wind in Egypt
Flat water with no shorebreak — freestyle and learning
Rescue boats on the water
Good hotels, diving and snorkelling
cons: Offshore wind — mandatory (paid) rescue service
The shallows near shore dry out at low tide
Isolated resort, little going on outside the hotels
soma-bay.wind_dir: N–NW, side-offshore at the main beach, side-shore at the bend of the bay

fuerteventura-flag-beach.description: Flag Beach is a wide sandy beach on the southern edge of Corralejo, at the edge of the dune nature park and opposite Lobos Island. The northerly trade wind blows along the shore here and is steadier than in the south of the island; in summer it's a good place for learning and freeriding, and in winter a northwest swell brings waves for stronger riders.
fuerteventura-flag-beach.rating_basis: The main kite beach in northern Fuerteventura: easy entry, sand, views of Lobos Island; the wind is steadier than at Sotavento but lighter. Guides (Hello Canary Islands, Fuerteventura Playas) rate it a good spot for all levels in summer
fuerteventura-flag-beach.waves_note: In summer chop and small waves near shore — suits beginners; in winter a northwest swell brings shorebreak and waves along the shore
fuerteventura-flag-beach.hazards: Volcanic rocks and reef exposed at low tide; winter shorebreak; protected nature area — follow the park rules
fuerteventura-flag-beach.gustiness_note: The trade wind in the north of the island is steadier and lighter than in the south; it can drop sharply when it shifts to NE
fuerteventura-flag-beach.crowd_note: Busy around the schools in summer, but the beach is long — you can move further south along the dunes
fuerteventura-flag-beach.region: Canary Islands, northern Fuerteventura (Corralejo, Dunas Nature Park)
pros: Easy entry, sandy bottom, side-shore
Steadier wind than in the south of the island
Corralejo nearby — accommodation, cafés, schools
Close to the airport
cons: Lighter wind than at Sotavento; drops in NE
Volcanic rocks exposed at low tide
Winter shorebreak makes entering the water harder
fuerteventura-flag-beach.wind_dir: N–NE (trade wind) and NW, side-shore / side-onshore
fuerteventura-flag-beach.airport: FUE — Puerto del Rosario, ~30 min (~35 km)

fuerteventura-sotavento.description: Sotavento is a 9-km white beach in southeastern Fuerteventura with a huge shallow tidal lagoon at Risco del Paso. The summer trade wind, accelerated by the terrain of the Jandía isthmus, blows hard and almost every day; windsurf and kite world championship events have been held here for decades. The lagoon has flat water for learning and freestyle, while outside there's open sea with chop.
fuerteventura-sotavento.rating_basis: A long-standing PWA/GKA World Cup stop, Wannakitesurf: “Great”; 75–95% windy days in May–September (TheKiteSpot); Kitejungle — 314 windy days a year, “awesome” in July–August. Downsides — gusty side-offshore wind and a tide-dependent lagoon
fuerteventura-sotavento.waves_note: Flat and shallow in the lagoon (tide-dependent); outside the sand spit — chop and small waves up to ~1 m
fuerteventura-sotavento.hazards: Offshore wind: it will carry you out to open sea — use the rescue service (~€50 per call-out / ~€90 per week); at low tide — shallows and sandbars; tidal currents in the lagoon channels
fuerteventura-sotavento.gustiness_note: The wind comes over the Jandía isthmus, side-offshore and gusty; up to 35–40 kn in July–August
fuerteventura-sotavento.crowd_note: The beach is huge (~9 km), enough room for everyone; the lagoon by the schools can get busy in peak weeks
fuerteventura-sotavento.region: Canary Islands, southern Fuerteventura (Costa Calma / Risco del Paso)
pros: Wind almost every day in summer, often 20–30 kn
Huge shallow flat-water lagoon
Warm climate all year, white sand
Plenty of room on the water
cons: Side-offshore, gusty wind — you need rescue cover
Tide-dependent lagoon: almost dries out at a big low tide
In summer the wind can be too strong and blows sand
Water cool for the latitude (18–23 °C)
fuerteventura-sotavento.airport: FUE — Puerto del Rosario, ~1 h (~75 km)

gran-canaria-vargas.description: Vargas is a rocky-sandy beach on the windy east coast of Gran Canaria near the airport, 10 km north of Pozo Izquierdo, the world capital of windsurfing. The summer trade wind here is one of the strongest and steadiest in Europe, and there are almost always waves. Schools operate mainly in winter, when the wind is lighter.
gran-canaria-vargas.rating_basis: One of Europe's windiest spots: wind almost every day in July–August, averaging 22–24 kn (Kitejungle); next to Pozo Izquierdo, a legendary PWA stop. Downsides — rocks, gusts and waves; more of a spot for experienced riders
gran-canaria-vargas.waves_note: Almost always waves: from chop to 1–3 m, lefts and rights, sometimes barrels; better at low tide — at high tide the waves are stronger and there are more rocks at the entry
gran-canaria-vargas.hazards: Large volcanic rocks on the beach and in the water; strong currents; waves and tide; downwind the beach ends in cliffs — beginners shouldn't drift downwind; protected nature area
gran-canaria-vargas.gustiness_note: In summer the trade wind is very strong and gusty, especially under clouds; acceleration effect between the islands
gran-canaria-vargas.crowd_note: Usually uncrowded; half the bay is reserved for windsurfers
gran-canaria-vargas.region: Canary Islands, east coast of Gran Canaria (Agüimes / Ingenio)
pros: Strong wind practically every day in summer
Wave riding and big air
Warm all year, airport nearby
Few people on the water
cons: Rocks on the beach and at the entry — wear shoes
Gusty, very strong wind in summer
Not for beginners without an instructor
Little infrastructure on the beach itself (a campsite)

lanzarote-famara.description: Famara is a 6-km sandy beach in northwest Lanzarote at the foot of the sheer Risco de Famara cliffs, next to the fishing village of Caleta de Famara (schools, repairs, kite shops). The trade wind blows side-onshore from the NE, and ocean swell creates a beach break almost all year. A kite spot first and foremost for waves and freeriding.
lanzarote-famara.rating_basis: Lanzarote's main wave kite spot: a huge sandy bay beneath the Risco de Famara cliffs, wind steadier from May to September (Hello Canary Islands); Kitejungle — “awesome” in July–August. Best suited to wave riding
lanzarote-famara.waves_note: A long beach break with several peaks; waves from small to big in winter with a northwest swell; the waves break on sandbars
lanzarote-famara.hazards: Fairly strong current and rip; rocks in places; powerful wave peaks in deep water; less beach at high tide
lanzarote-famara.gustiness_note: Wind off the ocean, steady but noticeably lighter than on the islands' east coasts
lanzarote-famara.crowd_note: Plenty of room (the beach is ~6 km), busy only near Caleta de Famara because of surfers
lanzarote-famara.region: Canary Islands, northwest Lanzarote (Caleta de Famara, Teguise)
pros: Waves almost all year
Huge beach, few people
Side-onshore wind — safer than offshore
Stunning scenery
cons: Lighter wind than on the islands' east coasts
Strong current and surf — not for beginners without a school
Cool water (18–22 °C)

tarifa-valdevaqueros.description: Tarifa is the southernmost point of continental Europe and Spain's main kite resort: the Venturi effect in the Strait of Gibraltar accelerates the easterly Levante and the westerly Poniente. The main spots are the 4-km Valdevaqueros beach (with the dune and Punta Paloma) and the long Los Lances by the town. Dozens of schools, rentals and shops, and a lively scene.
tarifa-valdevaqueros.rating_basis: Europe's wind capital: ~180+ windy days a year (Kitejungle), a constant in lists of Europe's best spots; downsides — summer crowds and the fickle, gusty Levante
tarifa-valdevaqueros.waves_note: Mostly chop and small waves up to ~1 m; with Atlantic swell in winter — waves at Los Lances and Dos Mares
tarifa-valdevaqueros.hazards: Offshore Levante at Los Lances and Balneario (carries you into the strait, strong current); rocks at Valdevaqueros at low tide and near Balneario; tides; swimmers in summer. In summer a rescue boat operates during Levante (buying a rescue card in advance is recommended)
tarifa-valdevaqueros.gustiness_note: The Levante is strong (20–50 kn) and gusty, blowing day and night; the Poniente is gentler (10–25 kn), steadier and builds towards lunchtime
tarifa-valdevaqueros.crowd_note: Very crowded in summer: from 15 June to 15 September kiting is allowed only in the Los Lances Norte, Valdevaqueros and Punta Paloma zones, and the beaches are packed with holidaymakers
tarifa-valdevaqueros.region: Andalusia, Costa de la Luz (Strait of Gibraltar)
tarifa-valdevaqueros.vibe_note: The spot is a few kilometres from Tarifa: the town has bars, clubs and restaurants and is very lively in summer. On the beach itself — chiringuitos.
pros: Wind almost all year, two wind regimes (Levante and Poniente)
Huge infrastructure: schools, rentals, shops, cafés
Long sandy beaches, spots for every direction
Easy to reach from Málaga, Seville, Jerez and Gibraltar
cons: Very crowded in summer, with zone restrictions
The Levante is gusty and can be too strong (30–50 kn)
Cool water (16–22 °C), wetsuit needed most of the year
Offshore wind at Los Lances in a Levante
tarifa-valdevaqueros.wind_dir: E (Levante) — side-offshore/offshore at Los Lances, side-shore at Valdevaqueros; W (Poniente) — side-onshore
tarifa-valdevaqueros.airport: XRY — Jerez ~1 h 30 min; AGP — Málaga ~2 h; GIB — Gibraltar ~45 min; SVQ — Seville ~2 h

tenerife-el-medano.description: El Médano is a windy town in southeast Tenerife by the Montaña Roja volcano, the island's best-known kite spot. The northeast trade wind blows almost all year, strongest in July–August; the main beach is a sandy bay with a designated launch zone, with the wave spots El Cabezo and the harbour wall nearby. Warm climate, and TFS airport is 15 minutes away.
tenerife-el-medano.rating_basis: Tenerife's main kite and windsurf spot, hosting national and international competitions; ~300 windy days a year (Web Tenerife). Kitejungle: “great” wind in July–August and in winter, medium crowds
tenerife-el-medano.waves_note: Chop and small waves in the bay; wave spots for advanced riders at the Harbour Wall and El Cabezo
tenerife-el-medano.hazards: Rocks on part of the spot (shoes recommended); Pigs Bay is off-limits/dangerous; the swimming zone is marked with buoys; cliffs and the harbour wall at the wave spots
tenerife-el-medano.gustiness_note: The trade wind is boosted by the headland effect, but buildings near the shore and Montaña Roja cause turbulence closer to town
tenerife-el-medano.crowd_note: Busy by the schools and in the launch zone in summer; the beach has separate zones for different levels and for swimming
tenerife-el-medano.region: Canary Islands, southeast Tenerife (Granadilla de Abona)
pros: Wind almost all year, warm even in winter
Tenerife South airport 10–15 minutes away
Sandy beach with a designated kite zone and lifeguards
Wave spots nearby for advanced riders
cons: The wind is lighter than it used to be because of new buildings; can be patchy near shore
Crowded in summer
Rocks in places; onshore wind and cliffs at El Cabezo

col-du-lautaret.description: The Col du Lautaret (2058 m) on the Grenoble–Briançon road is one of Europe's best-known snowkite spots. Treeless gentle slopes and hummocks around the pass suit both learning and mountain freeriding; schools operate on site. It's the second-highest pass in France that stays open to cars in winter, but it is temporarily closed in blizzards.
col-du-lautaret.rating_basis: A classic snowkite spot in France and the Alps: competitions have been held here (team Semnoz), and there are schools; downsides — regulated riding zones and road closures in bad weather
col-du-lautaret.waves_note: Gentle treeless slopes and hummocks around the pass — suits both smooth riding and “mountain” snowkiting with lift-off over the terrain
col-du-lautaret.hazards: Avalanches on the surrounding slopes, rocks when snow is thin, sudden weather changes; stick to the permitted riding zones
col-du-lautaret.gustiness_note: The wind is channelled and accelerated by the pass; gusty near the slopes and in storms
col-du-lautaret.crowd_note: Lots of kites at the pass on windy weekends; riding zones are limited
col-du-lautaret.region: Hautes-Alpes, between Grenoble and Briançon, 2058 m
pros: 2058 m altitude — reliable snow from December to April
Drive right up to the spot
Terrain for every level
Serre Chevalier resort nearby
cons: Riding is regulated (Écrins National Park, wildlife zones)
Crowded at weekends
The road is closed in blizzards and when avalanche danger is high
Gusty near the slopes
col-du-lautaret.wind_dir: W and E along the pass corridor (Romanche and Guisane valleys), also N
col-du-lautaret.airport: GNB — Grenoble ~2 h; TRN — Turin ~2 h; LYS — Lyon ~3 h

hyeres-almanarre.description: L'Almanarre is a long sandy beach on the western side of the Giens peninsula tombolo near Hyères on the Côte d'Azur. The main wind is the Mistral from the west–northwest, which blows side-shore here and accelerates between the islands; easterly winds bring waves. A classic Mediterranean spot for a spring or autumn trip.
hyeres-almanarre.rating_basis: An iconic southern French spot for windsurfing and kiting in the Mistral and a competition venue; but windy days are few (Kitejungle — ~90 a year, not counting thermals), and there are beach restrictions in summer
hyeres-almanarre.waves_note: In the Mistral (W–NW), chop and small waves near shore; in easterly wind, waves up to 1–1.5 m; on the other side of the tombolo (La Capte) — flat water
hyeres-almanarre.hazards: Mistral gusts; Posidonia seagrass near shore; swimmers and no-kite zones in summer
hyeres-almanarre.gustiness_note: The Mistral is strong and cold and can be gusty; the summer thermal breeze is lighter and steadier
hyeres-almanarre.crowd_note: Lots of kiters and windsurfers on Mistral weekends; in summer the beach fills with holidaymakers
pros: Strong Mistral, side-shore
Sandy beach and shallows near shore
Beautiful setting, Hyères and the Porquerolles islands nearby
Toulon-Hyères airport 5 minutes away
cons: Irregular wind — only with the Mistral or an easterly
Crowded in summer, with kiting restrictions — check the Hyères rules
Cold water in spring (14–15 °C)
hyeres-almanarre.wind_dir: W–NW (Mistral) — side-shore / side-onshore; E (easterly) — side-shore; SW breeze in summer
hyeres-almanarre.airport: TLN — Toulon-Hyères, ~10 min; MRS — Marseille, ~1 h 15 min; NCE — Nice, ~1 h 45 min

leucate-la-franqui.description: La Franqui is a resort village in the commune of Leucate on the Mediterranean coast between Perpignan and Narbonne, one of France's “wind capitals”. The northwesterly Tramontane blows here very often and very hard, especially from autumn to spring; in summer a sea thermal kicks in. The Mondial du Vent festival is held every year; the flat-water Étang de Leucate lagoon is close by.
leucate-la-franqui.rating_basis: One of France's windiest spots — ~250 windy days a year (Kitejungle), the annual Mondial du Vent festival; but the Tramontane is strong, gusty and offshore — a spot for confident riders
leucate-la-franqui.waves_note: In the Tramontane, flat to choppy near the sea shore (wind off the land); in sea wind from the east/southeast — waves; flat water in the Étang de Leucate lagoon
leucate-la-franqui.hazards: The offshore Tramontane carries you out to open sea — ride only with rescue cover or in the lagoon; strong gusts near shore; swimmers and no-kite zones in summer
leucate-la-franqui.gustiness_note: The Tramontane blows off the mountains, strong (often 25–40 kn) and gusty, especially near shore; the summer sea thermal is lighter but steadier
leucate-la-franqui.crowd_note: Busy during the Mondial du Vent (spring) and in summer; in summer there are beach zones and launch corridors
leucate-la-franqui.region: Occitanie, Aude — Gulf of Lion (Étang de Leucate lagoon)
pros: A great many windy days a year
Choice: sea (waves/chop) or lagoon (flat water)
Strong kite scene and the Mondial du Vent festival
Easy to reach by car from Spain and France
cons: The Tramontane is offshore and gusty — dangerous without experience
Cold water in winter and spring (12–14 °C)
Lighter wind and beach restrictions in summer
leucate-la-franqui.wind_dir: NW (Tramontane) — side-offshore at sea; E–SE (Marin, summer thermal) — onshore
leucate-la-franqui.airport: PGF — Perpignan, ~30 min (~35 km); BZR — Béziers, ~1 h

gudauri-jvari-pass.description: Gudauri is Georgia's biggest ski resort, on the Georgian Military Road 2 hours from Tbilisi. Above the resort, by the Jvari (Cross) Pass (2379 m), lie wide treeless slopes and plateaus where snowkiters ride; snow cover reaches 1.5 m in winter. The season runs from December to April, and many instructors speak Russian.
gudauri-jvari-pass.rating_basis: The Caucasus's main snowkite spot next to a popular ski resort: a long high-altitude snow season from December to April, big open slopes; downsides — avalanche risk and gusty mountain wind
gudauri-jvari-pass.waves_note: Wide treeless slopes and plateaus above Gudauri by the Jvari Pass — from gentle fields to freeriding over the terrain
gudauri-jvari-pass.hazards: Avalanches, whiteout, strong gusts on the pass; keep well away from lift lines and pistes
gudauri-jvari-pass.gustiness_note: Mountain wind, stronger on the pass; gusty near the ridges and in foehn conditions
gudauri-jvari-pass.crowd_note: Few kiters compared with skiers; on windy days anywhere from a handful to a few dozen on the plateau
gudauri-jvari-pass.region: Mtskheta-Mtianeti, Kazbegi municipality, Georgian Military Road, 2200–2400 m
pros: Reliable snow from December to April
Combines with skiing and freeriding
Russian-speaking environment, inexpensive Georgia
2 h from Tbilisi
cons: Avalanche-prone slopes
Gusty mountain wind
The Georgian Military Road closes in heavy snowfall
Few dedicated snowkite schools
gudauri-jvari-pass.wind_dir: N–NE from the Kazbegi side and S (foehn) over the pass

karpathos-agrilaopotamos.description: The windward beach of Agrilaopotamos on Karpathos's southwestern cape, ~3 km from Afiartis, is the only place in the south of the island where kiting is allowed (on the leeward side, in the famous windsurf bays Devil's/Paradise Bay, Gun Bay and Chicken Bay, kiting is banned). In summer the Meltemi blows round the clock, reaching 18–35 kn at its peak. Flat water inside the reef, swell outside.
karpathos-agrilaopotamos.rating_basis: Karpathos is “one of the windiest places in Europe”, with a ~90% wind probability in July–August (surf-magazin, windsurf.co.uk); only the windward side is open to kiters, and the island is better known among windsurfers
karpathos-agrilaopotamos.waves_note: Mostly flat water or light chop inside the reef; swell beyond the reef, with waves up to ~1.5 m after several days of strong Meltemi
karpathos-agrilaopotamos.hazards: Sharp reef with sea urchins (two safe channels), gusts near shore, very strong Meltemi (40+ kn at times)
karpathos-agrilaopotamos.gustiness_note: Windward side: the wind is 3–8 kn lighter than in the leeward bays (Devil's Bay, Gun Bay), and gusty for the first ~150 m from shore
karpathos-agrilaopotamos.crowd_note: Noticeably fewer kiters than windsurfers in the neighbouring bays
pros: One of Europe's windiest summer spots
Flat water inside the reef and waves outside
Airport 10 minutes away
Uncrowded
cons: Sharp reef with sea urchins — enter only via the channels
Gusty near shore
Kiting banned in the leeward bays
Few schools, courses mostly for intermediates
karpathos-agrilaopotamos.wind_dir: NW (Meltemi) side-shore; WNW thermal side-onshore from the right

kos-marmari.description: A long sandy beach on the north coast of Kos. The summer Meltemi blows from N–NW and accelerates between the islands of Kalymnos and Pserimos. A sandbar near shore is handy for learning, with chop for riding further out. The neighbouring Mastichari bay (~20 min) is KiteWorldWide's main school and a fallback in a westerly thermal.
kos-marmari.rating_basis: A reliable family spot with a sandbar for learning (Sportif, KiteWorldWide); ranks below Rhodes and Naxos in top lists
kos-marmari.waves_note: A ~50 m sandbar near shore with shallow, sheltered water; chop and bump-and-jump further out, small waves in a strong Meltemi
kos-marmari.hazards: Swimmers by the hotels, windsurfers; the water gets deep quickly further from shore
kos-marmari.gustiness_note: 2–4 Bft in the morning, 3–5 Bft by lunchtime; the Meltemi is accelerated by the Venturi effect between Kalymnos and Pserimos, reaching 6–7 Bft in high summer
kos-marmari.crowd_note: Big hotels nearby, the beach is busy in high season; schools recommend booking ahead
pros: Shallow sandy sandbar — good for beginners
Reliable summer Meltemi
Airport close by, lots of hotels
cons: Crowded on the beach in July–August
Lighter wind in the morning, riding mostly in the afternoon
Unsteady wind outside summer
kos-marmari.wind_dir: N–NW (Meltemi), cross-onshore; thermal from W during the day

lefkada-agios-ioannis.description: A long pebble-and-sand beach by the windmills west of Lefkada town, at the northern tip of the island. In summer the Maistro thermal blows from the northwest every afternoon — one of the most reliable thermals in the Mediterranean. The wind is cross-onshore, the water has chop and small waves, and Preveza airport is about 20 minutes away. Not to be confused with Vasiliki in the south of the island — that's windsurf-only.
lefkada-agios-ioannis.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: an “almost 100% reliable” spot, wind from mid-May (~75%) and on ~95% of days from June to mid-September; plenty of room even on peak days
lefkada-agios-ioannis.waves_note: Medium chop and small waves, rarely above 0.5 m; after several days of 20+ kn wind — shorebreak (usually for no more than 2 days)
lefkada-agios-ioannis.hazards: Shorebreak after several days of strong wind; swimmers in summer
lefkada-agios-ioannis.gustiness_note: The thermal is almost 100% reliable from June to mid-September and blows in the afternoon; the wind is steady, and the onshore direction smooths out gusts
lefkada-agios-ioannis.crowd_note: A long beach — enough room even on the busiest days (IKSURFMAG)
pros: Very reliable daily thermal in summer
Safe onshore direction
Plenty of room on the water
Town and Preveza airport nearby
cons: Wind only in the afternoon and rarely above 20 kn
Chop and shorebreak, little flat water
Little wind outside June–September
lefkada-agios-ioannis.wind_dir: NW–W (Maistro thermal), cross-onshore / onshore from the right

limnos-keros.description: A 3–4 km sandy bay in eastern Lemnos, in a nature reserve with dunes and lagoons (flamingos sometimes visit). Waist-deep water for 150 m from shore across the whole bay makes it one of Greece's best spots for learning. The north of the bay is flat, the middle has chop for first jumps, and the south has small waves.
limnos-keros.rating_basis: TheKiteMag: flat water 5/5, beginners 5/5, waves 3/5; IKSURFMAG and windsurf.co.uk praise the shallows and the range of conditions in one bay
limnos-keros.waves_note: “Three spots in one”: flat water in the north of the bay, light chop in the middle, small waves in the south (rarely above 1 m)
limnos-keros.hazards: Offshore wind in the upper part of the bay and in the evening; no rescue boat in the morning before the centres open
limnos-keros.gustiness_note: A morning spot: best wind roughly 9:00–15:00; by evening the wind drops and turns offshore; can be gusty in the upper part of the bay
limnos-keros.crowd_note: Kitejungle — “medium”; the middle of the bay can get busy by the centre, the southern part is quieter
pros: Standing depth far from shore
Flat water, chop and waves in one bay
Wild nature, little development
Airport 15 minutes away
cons: The island is off the main routes, few flights
In the evening the wind drops and turns offshore
Little infrastructure beyond the campsite and centres
limnos-keros.wind_dir: N–NE (Meltemi), side / cross-shore; slightly cross-off in the upper part of the bay

naxos-mikri-vigla.description: A sandy beach (Parthena) by the Mikri Vigla headland in southwest Naxos — the island's main kite spot and one of the best in the Cyclades. The summer northerly Meltemi is boosted by the thermal and the Venturi effect between Naxos and Paros, and usually blows from lunchtime to sunset. Kite centres with rentals and rescue operate at both ends of the bay.
naxos-mikri-vigla.rating_basis: Kitejungle — 325 windy days (≥12 kn) a year; Generationvoyage/Argophilia rank Naxos No. 1 among Greece's kite destinations for 2025; thekitespot — “a steady 20–25 kn”; kite-and-windsurfing-guide warns that the spot is trickier than it looks
naxos-mikri-vigla.waves_note: From flat water to light chop near shore, small waves up to ~1 m further out; in the rare southerly wind people ride beyond the headland
naxos-mikri-vigla.hazards: Rocky headland at the end of the bay, rocks on the bottom in places (wear water shoes), swimmers, strong Meltemi gusts
naxos-mikri-vigla.gustiness_note: The Meltemi is thermally “pumped up” and accelerates between Naxos and Paros: often 5–10 kn stronger than forecast, gusts by the headland
naxos-mikri-vigla.crowd_note: Generally less crowded than the top spots, but the narrow beach is packed with gear; busy in August
pros: Very steady, strong summer Meltemi
Suits all levels, centres with rescue boats
Beautiful sandy beach, crystal-clear water
Airport nearby and ferries from Piraeus
cons: Wind often stronger than forecast — you need small kites (7–9 m)
Narrow beach, crowded with gear
Swimmers and rocks by the headland
naxos-mikri-vigla.airport: JNX — Naxos, ~20 min; or a ferry from Piraeus/Rafina

paros-pounda.description: Pounda is a sandy beach in southwest Paros, opposite Antiparos. The northerly Meltemi accelerates through the strait and blows along the shore — flat water and steady wind make it one of Greece's best spots for freestyle and learning. A large kite centre with rentals, rescue and a bar operates on the beach.
paros-pounda.rating_basis: Kitejungle — “one of the most popular kite beaches in Greece”, 242 windy days a year; a classic freestyle spot that has hosted world tour events
paros-pounda.waves_note: The strait between Paros and Antiparos: flat water near shore, chop further out; no waves
paros-pounda.hazards: Lots of kiters on the water; the Paros–Antiparos ferry route is close by; follow the beach rules
paros-pounda.gustiness_note: Very steady side-shore wind, accelerated by the Venturi effect in the strait; 25–30+ kn at the height of the Meltemi
paros-pounda.crowd_note: According to kitejungle, medium to busy; crowded on the water in July–August
pros: Steady side-shore wind, flat water
Suits both beginners and freestylers
Full infrastructure on the beach
cons: Crowded at peak season
Over 30 kn in a strong Meltemi
Cool water and air outside summer
paros-pounda.airport: PAS — Paros, ~15 min; or a ferry from Piraeus/Rafina to Parikia (~20 min by car)

rhodes-kremasti.description: A kite beach by the village of Kremasti on the northwest coast of Rhodes, 10 minutes from the airport. The summer Meltemi accelerates in the strait between Rhodes and Turkey and blows along the shore, boosted by thermals during the day — windless days in July–August are rare. The water gets deep quickly, but it suits freestyle and wakestyle well; the station has jet-ski rescue.
rhodes-kremasti.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG (Anja Fuchs): “the perfect summer destination”, windless days in July–August are “very rare”; harder to learn than in Egypt because of the depth
rhodes-kremasti.waves_note: Flat water when the Meltemi starts, chop as it builds, wind swell further out; on onshore days and in the spring/autumn Tramontane — big waves and shorebreak
rhodes-kremasti.hazards: Deep water right off the beach, shorebreak in the northerly Tramontane, big waves on onshore days
rhodes-kremasti.gustiness_note: The Meltemi is accelerated by the nozzle effect between Rhodes and Turkey, with thermals adding to it in the afternoon: 5–7 Bft during the day, 3–5 Bft in the morning
rhodes-kremasti.crowd_note: Busy in front of the station at peak hours, but plenty of room upwind and further out; far less crowded than Prasonisi
pros: Airport 10 minutes away, Rhodes town nearby
Very reliable wind June–September
Warm water (up to 28 °C in summer)
Jet-ski rescue
cons: Narrow strip of standing-depth water — harder for beginners
Shorebreak in the Tramontane in spring and autumn
Crowded by the station at peak times
rhodes-kremasti.wind_dir: W–NW (Meltemi, bending in the strait), side-shore slightly from the left, sometimes side-onshore

rhodes-prasonisi.description: A sandy isthmus at the very southern tip of Rhodes linking the island to the islet of Prasonisi: the Aegean on one side, the Mediterranean on the other.
