cerro-catedral.season: late June – late September / early October (best in August – early September)
cerro-catedral.transfer: Bariloche airport (BRC) ~40 min (~30 km); 19 km from central Bariloche, ~25–40 min by bus or taxi
pros: Skiing in July–September with views of Patagonian lakes
Big vertical and good freeride
Bariloche nearby: restaurants, chocolate, nightlife
Lots of ski schools and easy runs
cons: Low base (~1030 m): wet snow and bare patches lower down
Crowds in July
Fickle Patagonian weather and wind
Unstable prices due to the peso exchange rate
cerro-catedral.airport: BRC — San Carlos de Bariloche, ~40 min
cerro-catedral.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, 2026 season — 160,000 ARS (~$115), one price for high and low season per PowderQuest; the peso exchange rate fluctuates wildly

hintertux-mayrhofen.description: The Zillertal 3000 lift pass combines the year-round Hintertux Glacier (up to 3250 m, 64 km) and the Mayrhofen area — Penken, Ahorn, Rastkogel, Eggalm (142 km). Mayrhofen is famous for Penken Park and Harakiri, Austria's steepest groomed run (78%); Hintertux for skiing in any month and its autumn Betterpark. A popular destination with Russian-speaking travellers.
hintertux-mayrhofen.rating_basis: skiresort.com: Mayrhofen 4.7/5 (“world class”), Hintertux Glacier 4.0/5; Penken Park is one of Europe's best snowparks; Austria's only year-round ski area
hintertux-mayrhofen.hazards: Altitude up to 3250 m — frost and wind on the glacier; crevasses off-piste; in summer the snow turns slushy in the afternoon, and during unusually hot weeks the glacier may close temporarily; avalanche danger on ski routes
hintertux-mayrhofen.crowd_note: Morning queues at the Penkenbahn and Ahornbahn in Mayrhofen; the glacier gets crowded in October–November (national team training camps) and at weekends
hintertux-mayrhofen.season: Hintertux Glacier — year-round (short breaks possible during hot summer weeks); Mayrhofen (Penken, Ahorn, Rastkogel, Eggalm) — early December – mid-April
hintertux-mayrhofen.transfer: Innsbruck ~1 h to Mayrhofen (65 km) plus ~30 min more to Hintertux; Munich ~2.5 h, Salzburg ~2.5 h; Zillertalbahn train from Jenbach to Mayrhofen, then bus to Hintertux
pros: Year-round skiing on the Hintertux Glacier
Pro-level snowparks (Penken Park, Betterpark)
The Harakiri run — a 78% gradient
Lively après-ski in Mayrhofen
Russian-speaking instructors available
cons: The Mayrhofen and Hintertux areas aren't linked — 30 min by bus
Mayrhofen sits low (630 m) — in spring no snow down to the valley, you ride the gondola down
Morning queues in Mayrhofen
hintertux-mayrhofen.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, high season at the ticket office: both the Hintertux Glacier and the Mayrhofen area cost €79 each (separate passes; the combined Zillertal 3000 is multi-day only). skiresort.com gives €82 for 2026/27

ischgl-samnaun.description: Ischgl is one of Austria's best-known resorts: 239 km of pistes in the Silvretta Arena at 2000–2872 m, linked to duty-free Samnaun in Switzerland. Modern lifts, near-total snowmaking and reliable snow from November to May. Famous for its parties, Top of the Mountain concerts and buzzing nightlife.
ischgl-samnaun.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.9/5 — one of the highest scores in the world, “top” in 18 categories; famous for the Top of the Mountain concerts and après-ski
ischgl-samnaun.hazards: Avalanche danger on off-piste slopes and ski routes; wind and frost on the passes towards Samnaun; late returns from après-ski on dark pistes
ischgl-samnaun.crowd_note: Morning queues at the Silvrettabahn and Pardatschgratbahn in the village; plenty of space on the upper slopes; very busy at the season opening and closing (concerts)
ischgl-samnaun.region: Tyrol, Paznaun valley (the area extends into Samnaun, Switzerland)
ischgl-samnaun.season: late November – early May (2026/27: 26 Nov – 2 May; main season until late March, then spring season)
ischgl-samnaun.transfer: Innsbruck ~1.25 h (100 km), Zurich ~2.5–3 h, Munich ~3 h; train to Landeck-Zams, then bus ~45 min
pros: Reliable snow — skiing above 2000 m, season until May
Very modern lifts
Legendary après-ski and concerts
Duty-free shopping in Samnaun
Russian-speaking instructors available
cons: Expensive accommodation in high season
Beginner slopes are up top (Idalp), not by the village
Noisy — not for a quiet family holiday
ischgl-samnaun.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, Silvretta Arena (Ischgl + Samnaun), high season at the ticket office; skiresort.com gives €83 for 2026/27

kaprun-kitzsteinhorn.description: The Kitzsteinhorn above Kaprun is a glacier area in Salzburg province with a season from October to May: skiing up to 3029 m, several snowparks with a superpipe, marked freeride routes and the Top of Salzburg viewing platform. Below is the family-friendly Maiskogel, and next door Schmittenhöhe in Zell am See is on a shared lift pass.
kaprun-kitzsteinhorn.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.4/5 (“outstanding”), “top” in 17 categories including snowpark and freeride; a glacier with one of the longest seasons in Austria
kaprun-kitzsteinhorn.hazards: Altitude above 3000 m — frost, wind, whiteouts; glacier crevasses and avalanches off-piste (freeride routes are not controlled); hard ice in autumn
kaprun-kitzsteinhorn.crowd_note: Busy on the glacier in autumn — national teams train there; morning queues at the Gletscherjet in high season; bearable on winter weekdays
kaprun-kitzsteinhorn.season: Kitzsteinhorn glacier — mid-October to mid-May (2026/27: 10 Oct – 17 May); Maiskogel and the run down to Kaprun — December to March/April
kaprun-kitzsteinhorn.transfer: Salzburg ~1–1.25 h (100 km), Munich ~2.5 h, Innsbruck ~2 h; train to Zell am See, then bus ~15 min
pros: Glacier — skiing from October to May
Strong snowparks and a superpipe
Marked freeride routes
Zell am See with its lake and Schmittenhöhe nearby
Russian-speaking instructors available
cons: Small area of its own (about 60 km)
Wind and closures on the glacier
Skiing down to the valley only in midwinter
kaprun-kitzsteinhorn.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, Kitzsteinhorn (incl. Maiskogel), high season at the ticket office; skiresort.com gives €82 for 2026/27. Nearby Schmittenhöhe (Zell am See) is on the shared Ski ALPIN CARD

kitzbuehel.description: Kitzbühel is a glamorous medieval Tyrolean town and home to the famous Streif downhill on the Hahnenkamm. The KitzSki area (188 km, 800–2000 m) links Kitzbühel, Kirchberg and Jochberg, with lots of gentle blue and red runs, near-total snowmaking, cosy mountain huts and lively nightlife in town.
kitzbuehel.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.9/5 (“world class”), “top” in 18 categories; the legendary Streif on the Hahnenkamm, a historic medieval town
kitzbuehel.hazards: Low altitude — thaws and rain, icy pistes in the morning; the Streif and black runs are very demanding; avalanche danger on ski routes
kitzbuehel.crowd_note: Busy at weekends (close to Munich) and during Hahnenkamm race week in January; morning queues at the Hahnenkammbahn
kitzbuehel.season: from early/mid-November (the Resterhöhe area first) to early/mid-April; the whole area from mid-December (2026/27: 6 Nov – 4 Apr)
kitzbuehel.transfer: Salzburg ~1.25 h (80 km), Innsbruck ~1.25 h (95 km), Munich ~2 h; railway station in town
pros: Atmospheric historic town
188 km of varied pistes, lots for intermediates
Near-total artificial snowmaking
Close to Munich, Salzburg and Innsbruck
Lively après-ski and restaurants
cons: Low-lying (800–2000 m) — snow is unreliable in warm winters, spring comes early
Busy at weekends
Expensive accommodation in Kitzbühel itself
kitzbuehel.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, high season (skiresort.com; Austrian price overview 2025/26 — €83); in 2026/27 the premium period is 20 Dec – 13 Mar, cheaper outside it

soelden.description: Sölden is a glacier resort in the Ötztal with one of the longest seasons in Austria: the Rettenbach and Tiefenbach glaciers open in October and the whole area runs until May. 144 km of pistes up to 3340 m, three panoramic peaks above 3000 m (Big 3), the Bond film “Spectre” shot on the Gaislachkogel, and lively après-ski. Popular with Russian-speaking travellers.
soelden.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.7/5 (“world class”), “top” in 17 categories; three peaks above 3000 m (Big 3), the FIS World Cup opener on the Rettenbach Glacier
soelden.hazards: Altitude up to 3340 m — frost and wind on the glaciers; glacier crevasses off-piste; avalanche danger on ski routes; the Ötztal road can close when avalanche risk is high
soelden.crowd_note: Morning queues at the Giggijoch and Gaislachkogl gondolas in high season; the glaciers get crowded in October–November (team training camps)
soelden.season: Rettenbach and Tiefenbach glaciers — from early/mid-October; the whole area down to the valley — mid-November to early May (2026/27: 9 Oct – 2 May)
soelden.transfer: Innsbruck ~1.25 h (85 km), Munich ~3 h, Zurich ~3.5 h; train to Ötztal station, then bus ~1 h
pros: Glaciers — skiing from October to May
Three peaks above 3000 m
Good snowpark
Lively après-ski
Russian-speaking instructors available
cons: The village stretches along a noisy road
Queues at the lower gondolas
The run from the glacier to the valley can be hard-packed and crowded in the evening
soelden.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, high season per skiresort.com; dynamic pricing — from €68 in 2025/26

st-anton-ski-arlberg.description: St. Anton is the capital of the Ski Arlberg area: 300 km of pistes linked with Lech, Zürs, Stuben and Warth, plus around 200 km of off-piste routes. A legend for freeride and steep slopes, the birthplace of Hannes Schneider's ski school, and home to Austria's rowdiest après-ski (Mooserwirt, Krazy Kanguruh).
st-anton-ski-arlberg.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.8/5 (“world class”), “top” in 18 categories; Austria's largest linked area, the cradle of modern ski technique (Hannes Schneider)
st-anton-ski-arlberg.hazards: High avalanche danger on popular off-piste routes (Valluga, Schindler Kar); steep mogul runs; after après-ski — skiing down to the village at dusk
st-anton-ski-arlberg.crowd_note: Queues at the Galzig and Gampen lifts during holidays and in February; Lech caps the number of lift passes sold per day — it's quieter there
st-anton-ski-arlberg.season: early December – mid/late April (2026/27: 2 Dec – 18 Apr)
st-anton-ski-arlberg.transfer: Innsbruck ~1–1.25 h (100 km), Zurich ~2.5 h, Friedrichshafen ~1.75 h; St. Anton station on the Arlberg railway — direct trains from Zurich, Innsbruck and Vienna
pros: World-class freeride and heliskiing from Lech/Zürs
300 km of pistes on one lift pass
Legendary après-ski
Railway station right in the village
Russian-speaking instructors available
cons: Challenging terrain — not the best choice for complete beginners
Expensive accommodation
Many of the main runs are mogulled by lunchtime
st-anton-ski-arlberg.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, all of Ski Arlberg (St. Anton, St. Christoph, Stuben, Lech, Zürs, Warth, Schröcken), high season (skiresort.com, schneehoehen.de); €81.50 in 2025/26

thredbo.description: Australia's leading ski village, in Kosciuszko National Park: the country's biggest vertical (~670 m), highest lift (2037 m) and longest runs — up to 5.9 km from the summit to Friday Flat. Powerful snowmaking safeguards the season, with good parks and a cosy village with slopeside bars. Neighbouring Perisher is the largest resort in the Southern Hemisphere (about 1200 ha, ~47 lifts, Epic Pass), but without that vertical.
thredbo.rating_basis: skiresort.com — 3.8/5 (“Very good”); the biggest vertical and longest runs in Australia, a genuine mountain village at the lifts
thredbo.hazards: Ice and hard snow in the mornings, strong wind and fog at the summit, black ice on the Alpine Way mountain road (chains mandatory in season)
thredbo.crowd_note: Very crowded during the July school holidays and at weekends (visitors from Sydney and Canberra); quieter on August weekdays
thredbo.region: New South Wales, Snowy Mountains, Kosciuszko National Park
thredbo.season: early/mid-June – late September (reliable snow usually July – August)
thredbo.transfer: Canberra (CBR) ~2.5–3 h (~200 km); Sydney ~6 h (~500 km); Snowy Mountains airport in Cooma ~1 h 15 min
pros: Skiing in July–August
Australia's biggest vertical and longest runs
Lively village with après-ski by the lifts
Powerful snowmaking
cons: Low mountains: snow varies a lot by season, often icy
Expensive lift pass and accommodation
Crowds during school holidays
Far from international airports
thredbo.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, 2026 season — A$239 on weekdays and A$259 at weekends (online, standard days); more expensive on peak days

shahdag.description: A modern resort in Shahdag National Park in northeastern Azerbaijan: gondolas and high-speed chairlifts, about 45 km of pistes with more than 1100 m of vertical, and five hotels at the lifts. Snowmaking covers every run, and the atmosphere is calm and family-oriented. Russian, English and Turkish are widely spoken at the resort.
shahdag.rating_basis: skiresort.com test — 3.4/5 (“Good”): a new resort (opened in 2012) with modern lifts and snowmaking on 100% of runs
shahdag.hazards: Strong wind up top, fog, ice after thaws, avalanche danger off-piste on steep treeless slopes; the mountain road from Qusar during snowfall.
shahdag.crowd_note: Busy at New Year, during Novruz (March) and at weekends when people come from Baku; quiet on weekdays
shahdag.region: Qusar District, Shahdag National Park, Greater Caucasus
shahdag.season: second half of December – late March / early April
shahdag.transfer: Baku ~3–3.5 h (≈200 km: 170 km to Qusar + 30 km into the mountains)
pros: New lifts, snowmaking on 100% of runs
4–5* hotels right by the slopes
Inexpensive lift pass, Russian understood everywhere
Visa-free entry for Russians
cons: Far from Baku (~3.5 h)
Almost no après-ski or village atmosphere
Short season, snow depends on the winter
Few difficult runs and little freeride
shahdag.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, main season — 42 AZN (≈€22) per skiresort.com; in 2024/25 from 30 AZN on weekdays and from 35 AZN at weekends

jahorina.description: A 1984 Olympic resort 30 km from Sarajevo: about 50 km of mostly blue and red runs through pine forest, a new gondola and night skiing. An inexpensive, no-frills resort for beginners and intermediates, easy to combine with a trip to Sarajevo.
jahorina.rating_basis: skiresort.com test — 3.7/5 (“Very good”): lifts, pistes, families, beginners; a 1984 Olympic resort (women's alpine skiing)
jahorina.hazards: Fog and wind on the Ogorjelica summit, ice during thaws. Minefields from the 1990s war still remain in Bosnia and Herzegovina: take a local guide for freeriding and hiking off marked trails.
jahorina.crowd_note: At weekends and on holidays lots of Sarajevo locals and visitors from Serbia and Croatia; quiet on weekdays
jahorina.season: early December – late March / early April
jahorina.transfer: Sarajevo ~45–60 min (≈30 km; taxi ≈50 KM, buses)
pros: Close to Sarajevo airport
Inexpensive lift pass and accommodation
Modern lifts, night skiing
Russian-speaking instructors, visa-free entry for Russians
cons: Low mountains (up to ~1900 m), snow depends on the winter
Almost no difficult runs or freeride
Small area, enough for 2–3 days of active skiing
Modest après-ski
jahorina.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, peak period — 86 KM (≈€44); mid-season 79 KM, early/late season 73 KM; night skiing 58–69 KM (official OC Jahorina price list)

bansko.description: Bulgaria's main ski resort at the foot of the Pirin: an old town with a gondola leaving right from its edge and skiing up to 2500 m. North-facing slopes hold snow until mid-April, and there's a long run down to town. Inexpensive accommodation and food, lively nightlife, World Cup races.
bansko.rating_basis: skiresort.com test — 4.2/5 (“Outstanding”), World Ski Awards — Bulgaria's best resort 2025, FIS World Cup races (January 2026), Lonely Planet Best in Travel 2025
bansko.hazards: Avalanche danger off-piste in the Pirin, wind up top (Todorka), the icy lower run down to town, heavy traffic on blue runs at peak season.
bansko.crowd_note: Notorious morning queues for the gondola from town at weekends and holidays (Christmas, New Year, February); an early start or driving up to Chalin Valog helps
bansko.transfer: Sofia ~2–2.5 h (160 km), Plovdiv ~2.5–3 h (185 km)
pros: Some of Europe's best prices for lift passes, accommodation and food
1500 m vertical, long run down to town
Reliable snowmaking and north-facing slopes
Atmospheric old town and wild après-ski
cons: Morning gondola queues at peak season
Few difficult runs
75 km area — can get repetitive over a week
The lower run to town thaws by spring
bansko.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, high season; prices in euros since 1 Jan 2026 (before that, 110 leva in 2024/25). In the first days of the season, with partial operation, it sold for less (65 leva ≈ €33)

banff-sunshine.description: A high-alpine resort in Banff National Park, 15 km from the town of Banff: three mountains (Goat's Eye, Lookout, Standish) above the treeline, ~1360 ha of terrain and dry Rocky Mountain snow from November to late May. For freeriders there's the legendary Delirium Dive (entry only with an avalanche transceiver). Base yourself in Banff with its restaurants and bars; the shared SkiBig3 lift pass adds Lake Louise, one of Canada's largest resorts (~1700 ha), 60 km away.
banff-sunshine.rating_basis: skiresort.com — 4.0/5 (“Very good”); the longest non-glacier season in Canada, dry Rocky Mountain snow, Delirium Dive
banff-sunshine.hazards: Avalanche danger in Delirium Dive and beyond the ski area boundary (transceiver, shovel and probe mandatory), frostbite at −20…−30 °C, wind and whiteouts above the treeline
banff-sunshine.crowd_note: Morning gondola queues at weekends (visitors from Calgary) and on holidays; quiet on weekdays
banff-sunshine.region: Alberta, Rocky Mountains, Banff National Park
banff-sunshine.season: early November – late May (until Victoria Day weekend); in 2026 there was also a short summer season, 20 June – 5 July
banff-sunshine.transfer: Calgary (YYC) ~1.5–2 h to Banff (~145 km) + ~20 min to the gondola base; shuttles from Banff hotels
pros: Long season: from November to late May
Dry snow and alpine views of the Rockies
Freeride in Delirium Dive and Wild West
The town of Banff with excellent facilities
cons: Severe cold in December–January (down to −25 °C)
Wind and poor visibility up top
Only one slopeside hotel, everything else is in Banff
National park: strict limits on development and backcountry access
banff-sunshine.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult — ~C$184 (November 2025 price, dynamic, higher on peak dates; skiresort.com gives C$189). There's a shared SkiBig3 pass for Sunshine, Lake Louise and Norquay

whistler-blackcomb.description: North America's largest ski resort: two mountains linked by the Peak 2 Peak gondola, ~3300 ha of terrain, more than 200 runs and over 1500 m of vertical. Huge bowls, glaciers and tree skiing for every level, pro-level parks and heliskiing straight from the village; the pedestrian village at the base has the best après-ski in Canada. Lots of snow (~11–12 m a season), but it's maritime and heavier than in the Rockies.
whistler-blackcomb.rating_basis: skiresort.com — 4.6/5; North America's largest resort, consistently near the top of SKI Magazine reader rankings and the World Ski Awards
whistler-blackcomb.hazards: Avalanche danger in the bowls and backcountry, fog and whiteouts in the alpine, cliffs and couloirs, tree wells; rain and ice on the lower slopes
whistler-blackcomb.crowd_note: Morning queues for the village gondolas at weekends (visitors from Vancouver) and at Christmas/New Year; quieter on weekdays in March–April
whistler-blackcomb.season: late November – mid/late May (Whistler closes in April, Blackcomb runs until May)
whistler-blackcomb.transfer: Vancouver (YVR) ~2–2.5 h via the Sea-to-Sky Highway (~137 km), regular airport shuttles
pros: Huge area and vertical, runs up to 11 km
World-class freeride: bowls, couloirs, glaciers, heliskiing
Pro-level snowparks
The best après-ski and a pedestrian village
cons: Very expensive lift pass and accommodation
Frequent rain lower down and fog due to the maritime climate
Crowds at weekends and holidays
Far from Europe
whistler-blackcomb.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult — price depends on the date (Vail Resorts dynamic pricing): a sample online weekday price for 2025/26 is C$305; more at the ticket office on peak days (skiresort.com gives C$351). Cheaper online in advance or with an Epic Pass

laax-flims-falera.description: Laax is Europe's freestyle capital: several snowparks including pro level, a superpipe on Crap Sogn Gion, the indoor Freestyle Academy and the LAAX Open contest. 176 km of pistes between Laax, Flims and Falera up to the Vorab Glacier (3018 m), plus about 40 km of ski routes for freeride.
laax-flims-falera.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.5/5 (“outstanding”), “top” in 17 categories; the LAAX Open and one of the world's largest halfpipes — Europe's leading freestyle resort
laax-flims-falera.hazards: Avalanche danger off-piste and on ski routes; wind and poor visibility on the Vorab Glacier; injury risk in the pro zones of the snowpark
laax-flims-falera.crowd_note: Lots of visitors from Zurich at weekends — queues at the gondolas in Murschetg; quiet on weekdays
laax-flims-falera.season: late November – mid-April (2026/27: 28 Nov – 11 Apr); the Vorab Glacier sometimes opens earlier
laax-flims-falera.transfer: Zurich ~1.5–2 h (150 km); train to Chur, then bus ~30–40 min
pros: Europe's best snowparks and halfpipe
Vorab Glacier — reliable snow up top
Good freeride and 40 km of ski routes
Close to Zurich
cons: Few black runs
Dynamic pricing — expensive on peak days
No confirmed Russian-speaking instructors
laax-flims-falera.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, dynamic price: usually around CHF 72, up to CHF 89 on peak days (2025/26 season)

st-moritz.description: St. Moritz is the Engadine's legendary society resort and the birthplace of winter tourism. The main Corviglia area (155 km, up to 3057 m on Piz Nair) is complemented on a shared lift pass by Corvatsch (3303 m, snowpark and night skiing) and Diavolezza with glacier freeride. Sunny, dry weather, wide immaculate pistes, luxury hotels and few queues.
st-moritz.rating_basis: skiresort.com: Corviglia 4.7/5 (“world class”), “top” in 17 categories; twice host of the Winter Olympics and the Alpine World Ski Championships
st-moritz.hazards: Severe frost in January (the Engadine is one of Switzerland's coldest valleys); avalanche danger off-piste; the Morteratsch Glacier (the run down from Diavolezza) has crevasses — best with a guide
st-moritz.crowd_note: Slopes are usually uncrowded even in high season; queues possible at the Chantarella funicular and the Piz Nair cable car during holidays
st-moritz.season: Corviglia: late November – early April; Corvatsch and Diavolezza (same Engadin lift pass) run until late April – May
st-moritz.transfer: Zurich ~3–3.5 h by train (Rhaetian Railway, via Chur), Milan ~3 h; Engadin-Samedan airport (private aviation) — 10 min
pros: Few people on the slopes
Sunny climate and altitude — reliable snow
Corvatsch's pro snowpark and Friday night skiing
Luxury, gastronomy, society life
Russian-speaking instructors available
cons: Very expensive
The Engadine areas aren't linked — you need a bus/train
Corviglia already closes in early April
Far from airports
st-moritz.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, Engadin St. Moritz (all areas), high season — ≈€104 per a comparative price review; sold in CHF at dynamic prices (CHF 81.5 to 118.5 in the 2023/24 season)

verbier-4-vallees.description: Verbier is the heart of the 4 Vallées (412 km of pistes together with Nendaz, Veysonnaz, Thyon and La Tzoumaz) and one of the world's freeride capitals: the slopes of Mont Fort (3330 m), Tortin and the legendary Bec des Rosses, where the Freeride World Tour final is held. The resort is known for raucous après-ski and pricey chalets.
verbier-4-vallees.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.3/5 (“outstanding”), “top” in 14 categories; Verbier hosts the Freeride World Tour final (Xtreme Verbier) and is one of the benchmark freeride resorts
verbier-4-vallees.hazards: High avalanche danger on popular off-piste routes (Vallon d'Arbi, Tortin); steep ski routes aren't groomed; Mont Fort glacier — crevasses off-piste
verbier-4-vallees.crowd_note: Queues at the Médran gondola and up to Mont Fort at weekends (visitors from Geneva) and in February; especially on powder-day mornings
verbier-4-vallees.season: early December – late April; the upper sectors (Mont Fort, Tortin) sometimes open from November (2026/27: 7 Nov – 25 Apr)
verbier-4-vallees.transfer: Geneva ~2 h (160 km), Sion ~45 min; train to Le Châble, then gondola up to Verbier
pros: World-class freeride and mogul couloirs
Heliskiing on site
412 km of pistes on one lift pass
Buzzing nightlife
Close to Geneva, Russian-speaking instructors available
cons: Expensive
Few easy runs in Verbier itself — beginners are better off in Nendaz/Thyon
Weekend queues
Many of the Mont Fort and Tortin runs are ungroomed “ski routes”
verbier-4-vallees.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, 4 Vallées, high season per skiresort.com (≈€102); the official site's online “best price” starts from CHF 87, −10% when bought 10+ days ahead

zermatt-cervinia.description: Zermatt at the foot of the Matterhorn, together with Italy's Cervinia and Valtournenche, forms the Matterhorn Ski Paradise: 322 km of pistes up to 3899 m and the longest run in the Alps — about 25 km from the Klein Matterhorn down to Valtournenche. The Theodul Glacier is open in summer too. A car-free village, fine dining and strong freeride with heliskiing.
zermatt-cervinia.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.5/5 (“outstanding”), “top” in 16 categories; the highest ski area in the Alps (3899 m) and views of the Matterhorn
zermatt-cervinia.hazards: Altitude up to 3899 m — altitude sickness, frost and wind; glacier crevasses off-piste (only with a guide); avalanche danger; in bad weather the Theodul Pass closes and you can get stuck on the Italian side
zermatt-cervinia.crowd_note: Queues at the Matterhorn Express and up to the Klein Matterhorn at Christmas, in February and at Easter; moderate in January and March
zermatt-cervinia.region: Valais, Pennine Alps (the area continues into Italy — Cervinia, Valtournenche)
zermatt-cervinia.season: winter season from early November (glacier) / late November (whole area) to early May; in summer, skiing on the Theodul Glacier (Matterhorn Glacier Paradise) from May to October
zermatt-cervinia.transfer: Geneva ~3.5–4 h by train, Zurich ~3.5 h, Milan Malpensa ~3 h; car-free village — drive to Täsch and take the 12-min shuttle train. From the Cervinia side: Turin ~2 h, Milan ~2.5 h
pros: The highest area in the Alps — snow almost year-round
Summer glacier skiing
A ~25 km run from Switzerland into Italy
Heliskiing, strong freeride
Russian-speaking instructors available
cons: Very expensive (lift pass, accommodation, food)
Long journey from the airports
Wind and upper-lift closures; crossing to Italy depends on the weather
zermatt-cervinia.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, high season per skiresort.com (≈€126); dynamic pricing: in 2026/27 from CHF 89 (Zermatt only) and from CHF 104 (with Cervinia) on low-season dates

portillo.description: South America's oldest and most legendary resort, at ~2900 m by Laguna del Inca lake, right on the Argentine border; the 1966 World Championships were held here. A small ski area (~500 ha), but steep terrain, couloirs (Super C, Roca Jack) and unusual “va-et-vient” slingshot lifts for slopes where towers can't be built. A private-club atmosphere: nearly all the skiing is for guests of the single hotel and hostels.
portillo.rating_basis: skiresort.com — 2.8/5 (few lifts and services), but a cult spot: the 1966 World Championships, the legendary yellow hotel by Laguna del Inca, the Super C couloir; one of the best-known resorts in the Andes
portillo.hazards: High avalanche danger (in a snowstorm Route 60 and the lifts close), altitude ~3000 m, strong wind and UV, steep couloirs and rocks
portillo.crowd_note: Almost no queues: mostly hotel guests ski here, and day visitors are capped (about 450 a day)
portillo.region: Andes, Valparaíso Region, Los Libertadores pass on the Argentine border
portillo.season: late June – late September / early October (extended to 11 October in snowy 2026)
portillo.transfer: Santiago (SCL) ~2–2.5 h (~160 km via Los Andes on Route 60 to the Cristo Redentor pass); Mendoza (Argentina) ~3–4 h across the border
pros: Empty slopes thanks to the visitor cap
Steep couloirs and world-class off-piste
Dry snow and a high base
Unique atmosphere of an old hotel by a mountain lake
cons: Few runs and lifts, limited infrastructure
Expensive hotel stays (usually week-long packages)
The pass road closes in heavy snowfall
Snow varies a lot from year to year
portillo.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, 2026 season: high season (weekends, holidays and 18 Jul – 2 Aug) — $71, low season — $53; in pesos 67,000 / 48,000 CLP per PowderQuest. Day ticket with lunch — $87

valle-nevado.description: South America's largest resort, 60 km from Santiago: open high-alpine Andean slopes at 2860–3670 m, hotels right on the pistes and views of the Sierra Bella. It links with neighbouring La Parva and El Colorado to form Tres Valles, the largest linked ski area in South America. Lots of off-piste and heliskiing on slopes up to 5000 m; the June–September season makes it the top choice for the Northern Hemisphere's summer months.
valle-nevado.rating_basis: skiresort.com — 3.1/5; South America's largest and most visited resort, linked with La Parva and El Colorado (Tres Valles); part of the Ikon Pass and Mountain Collective
valle-nevado.hazards: Altitude up to 3670 m (altitude sickness, strong UV), the storm-force “viento blanco” wind, avalanche danger off-piste, rocks when snow is thin; chains mandatory on the road in snowfall
valle-nevado.crowd_note: At weekends and during the July winter holidays lots of skiers from Santiago and Brazil, traffic jams on the mountain road; quiet on weekdays in August–September
valle-nevado.season: mid-June – late September/early October (extended to 1 December in snowy 2026)
valle-nevado.transfer: Santiago airport (SCL) ~1.5–2 h (~80 km, the last stretch a 40-hairpin road via Farellones); in snowfall — chains and traffic restrictions
pros: Skiing in June–September, when it's summer in Europe
Altitude: dry snow and lots of sun
The Tres Valles link and heliskiing
Close to Santiago and its international airport
cons: Snowfall varies a lot by year (there are dry seasons)
Traffic jams and restrictions on the mountain road
Expensive slopeside accommodation, little nightlife
No trees — poor visibility in bad weather
valle-nevado.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, ticket office, 2026 season — 93,000 CLP (~$105), one price all season; bought online for a specific date — from 41,500 to 75,500 CLP (+6,000 CLP for the card). There's an “Interconnection” ticket covering linked La Parva and El Colorado

thaiwoo-chongli.description: A modern “ski town” opened in 2015 by the Great Wall of China in the Chongli district, which hosted the skiing events of the 2022 Olympics. About 30 runs with up to 510 m of vertical, almost all on artificial snow; a good base for beginners and intermediates, with a park. The alternative next door is Wanlong: ~22 km of pistes, 560 m vertical, night skiing and a season until mid-April.
thaiwoo-chongli.rating_basis: skiresort.com — 3.2/5; one of the largest modern resorts in Chongli, the district that hosted the snow events of the 2022 Olympics
thaiwoo-chongli.hazards: Severe frost with wind (frostbite), hard artificial snow and ice, altitude ~2000 m
thaiwoo-chongli.crowd_note: At weekends and over Chinese New Year lots of skiers from Beijing, queues for the gondola; quiet on weekdays
thaiwoo-chongli.transfer: High-speed train Beijing (Beijing North/Qinghe) – Taizicheng ~1 h + free shuttle ~15–20 min; by car from Beijing ~3 h (~240 km)
pros: Quick from Beijing by high-speed train
Modern lifts (gondola, high-speed chairlifts)
Reliable snowmaking and well-groomed pistes
Good for beginners and families
cons: Little natural snow, no freeride
Very cold and windy (down to −20 °C)
Weekend crowds
Small vertical
thaiwoo-chongli.airport: PEK/PKX — Beijing, ~3 h by car or ~1.5–2 h by train; ZQZ Zhangjiakou ~1 h

baqueira-beret.description: Spain's largest resort, in the Atlantic-facing Val d'Aran — there's noticeably more snow here, and it's more reliable than in the rest of Catalonia. Three sectors (Baqueira, Beret, Bonaigua) with long blue and red runs, good freeride and heliskiing. An upmarket yet relaxed resort, a favourite of the royal family.
baqueira-beret.rating_basis: skiresort.com test — 4.2/5 (“Outstanding”): size, snow, grooming, freeride; Spain's largest resort
baqueira-beret.hazards: Avalanche danger off-piste (especially Bonaigua and Baciver), strong wind on the Bonaigua pass and the Tuc de la Llança summit, fog, winter closures of the road over the Bonaigua pass.
baqueira-beret.crowd_note: Lots of Spaniards during holidays (the December “puente”, Christmas, Easter) and at weekends; quiet on weekdays from January to March
baqueira-beret.season: late November / early December – early April
baqueira-beret.transfer: Toulouse ~2.5 h (170 km), Barcelona ~4 h (ALSA buses to Vielha), Lleida ~2.5–3 h
pros: The snowiest resort in the Spanish Pyrenees
Large area with varied terrain
Good freeride in Bonaigua and Baciver, heliskiing
Excellent Val d'Aran gastronomy
cons: Expensive accommodation in Baqueira 1500
Crowds during Spanish holidays and weekends
Not close to a major airport
Modest nightlife
baqueira-beret.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, ticket office — €71.50; €67.50 with the BaqueiraPASS card; skiresort.com gives €75 (probably 2026/27)

sierra-nevada.description: Europe's southernmost major ski resort, 30 km from Granada: the slopes of Veleta peak rise to 3300 m, with views of the Mediterranean on clear days. Sunny, with lots of wide blue and red runs, a strong snowpark and noisy Spanish nightlife in Pradollano. You can combine skiing with the Alhambra and the sea.
sierra-nevada.rating_basis: skiresort.com test — 4.1/5 (“Outstanding”): pistes, beginners, snowpark, après-ski; Europe's southernmost major resort, host of the 2017 FIS Freestyle and Snowboard World Championships
sierra-nevada.hazards: Strong wind and upper-lift closures, ice in the mornings after thaws, intense sun (goggles and sunscreen needed), altitude up to 3300 m, fog; traffic jams on the A-395 at weekends.
sierra-nevada.crowd_note: At weekends and holidays lots of day-trippers from Granada, Málaga and Madrid, queues for the gondolas from Pradollano; quiet on weekdays
sierra-nevada.season: late November – late April (sometimes until early May)
sierra-nevada.transfer: Granada ~1 h (bus from the city ~45–60 min), Málaga ~2 h
pros: Lots of sun and altitude up to 3300 m
Powerful snowmaking, season until late April
World Championship-level snowpark, night skiing
Granada and the Costa Tropical beaches nearby
cons: Few difficult runs and little freeride
Strong wind often closes the top (Veleta)
Dry climate — in snowless winters skiing is on artificial snow only
Weekend crowds
sierra-nevada.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult: €55–69 depending on the date (more during holidays and high season, more at the ticket office than online in advance); skiresort.com — €62 in the main season

levi.description: Finland's most popular ski resort, above the Arctic Circle: a low fell with floodlit runs on every side, a compact village at the lifts and an airport 15 minutes away. Ideal for families and beginners, and for combining skiing with the northern lights, huskies and reindeer; the season runs from October to May. The Finnish alternative is Ruka (Kuusamo), with a similar range of runs and a very long season.
levi.rating_basis: skiresort.com test — 4.3/5 (“Outstanding”): snow, families, beginners, snowpark, accommodation; Finland's largest resort, a World Cup slalom stop in November
levi.hazards: Severe frost (down to −30 °C) and wind at the summit — frostbite, polar night in December–January (skiing only under floodlights), poor visibility in blizzards, hard snow.
levi.crowd_note: Peak times are Christmas and New Year, the Finnish winter holidays (February – early March) and Easter; quiet on weekdays in January and April
levi.season: early October (1–2 runs on stored snow) – early May; fully open from late November, best in February – April
levi.transfer: Kittilä ~15–20 min (15 km); from Helsinki a ~1.5 h flight, or the night train to Kolari + bus ~1 h
pros: Airport 15 minutes away, compact village
Reliable snow from October to May
Floodlit runs, great for kids and beginners
Lapland exotica: northern lights, huskies, reindeer
cons: Only ~335 m vertical, few difficult runs
Severe frost and polar night in December–January
Expensive accommodation and flights during holidays
Almost no freeride
levi.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult (12–64), main season — €60 per skiresort.com; the official price in the 2023/24 season was €51.50

alpe-dhuez.description: The “island in the sun” of the Alps: 250 km of pistes from 1125 to 3330 m (Pic Blanc), south-facing slopes and lots of sunny days. It's the start of the Sarenne, one of the world's longest black runs (16 km). Good for families and intermediates, with snowparks and decent off-piste terrain off Pic Blanc.
alpe-dhuez.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.2/5 (“outstanding”), “top” in 11 categories: size, pistes, snow reliability, families, beginners, freeride, snowpark
alpe-dhuez.hazards: Avalanche danger off-piste around Pic Blanc and Grandes Rousses; Sarenne Glacier — crevasses off-piste; a 21-hairpin mountain road up to the resort — chains/winter tyres needed
alpe-dhuez.crowd_note: During the French February holidays queues at the gondolas from the village (DMC, Pic Blanc); moderate the rest of the time
alpe-dhuez.region: Isère, Grandes Rousses massif, French Alps
alpe-dhuez.season: early December – mid/late April (2026/27: 5 Dec – 18 Apr, lift pass valid until 25 Apr)
alpe-dhuez.transfer: Grenoble (GNB) ~1.5 h, Lyon ~2 h, Geneva ~2.5–3 h; bus from Grenoble station ~1.5 h
pros: Lots of sun and wide pistes
The Sarenne run — 16 km from Pic Blanc (3330 m)
Good artificial snowmaking
Close to Grenoble and Lyon
cons: South-facing slopes — the snow turns slushy quickly in spring
1960s–70s resort architecture
No confirmed Russian-speaking instructors
alpe-dhuez.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, Grand Domaine, main period 19 Dec 2026 – 9 Apr 2027; cheaper at the start and end of the season. skiresort.com gives €66 (probably 2025/26)

chamonix.description: Chamonix is the world capital of mountaineering and freeride at the foot of Mont Blanc. The unlinked Grands Montets, Brévent-Flégère and Balme areas add up to ~120 km of pistes, but the real draw is off-piste: the glacier descents of the Grands Montets and the legendary 20 km Vallée Blanche from the Aiguille du Midi (3842 m). A lively town with bars and restaurants, though beginners have better-suited resorts.
chamonix.rating_basis: A world-class freeride icon (Vallée Blanche, Grands Montets); the individual areas score 3.5–3.7/5 on skiresort.com because they're scattered and have few easy runs
chamonix.hazards: Serious avalanche danger and glacier crevasses off-piste — on the Vallée Blanche and glaciers only with a mountain guide and avalanche gear; altitude up to 3842 m; fast-changing weather
chamonix.crowd_note: Morning queues at the Grands Montets after snowfall and at the Aiguille du Midi cable car; the areas aren't linked — transfers by bus
chamonix.season: Grands Montets: late November – early May; Brévent-Flégère and Balme: mid-December – April; Vallée Blanche (from the Aiguille du Midi) — usually January to April
chamonix.transfer: Geneva ~1–1.5 h (88 km), Lyon ~3 h, Turin ~2 h via the Mont Blanc Tunnel
pros: World-class freeride and glacier descents
Vallée Blanche — 20 km off-piste from 3842 m
A real mountain town with life beyond the slopes
Close to Geneva; Mont-Blanc Unlimited opens up Courmayeur and Verbier
cons: The areas aren't linked, you need buses
Few easy runs, the lower slopes are low (~1000 m)
The top Grands Montets cable car (3275 m) is closed until December 2027
Queues on powder days
chamonix.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, Chamonix Le Pass (Brévent-Flégère, Grands Montets, Balme and the small areas) at the ticket office; online in advance — from €47. Mont-Blanc Unlimited (incl. the Aiguille du Midi, Les Houches, Courmayeur) — €100

les-arcs-paradiski.description: Les Arcs is four ski-in/ski-out villages (1600, 1800, 1950, 2000), linked by the Vanoise Express cable car with La Plagne to form Paradiski (425 km). The Aiguille Rouge (3226 m) offers a 7 km run with ~2000 m of vertical down to Villaroger. Good for families and intermediates, with strong freeride and a park; easy access by train.
les-arcs-paradiski.rating_basis: skiresort.com: Les Arcs 4.1/5, La Plagne 4.4/5 (“outstanding”); “top” for size, snow reliability, beginners and freeride
les-arcs-paradiski.hazards: Avalanche danger on the off-piste slopes of the Aiguille Rouge and Villaroger; wind up top, Vanoise Express closures in strong wind
les-arcs-paradiski.crowd_note: French February holidays — queues in Arc 1800 and Arc 2000; quiet in January and March
les-arcs-paradiski.season: mid-December – late April (2025/26 season: 13 Dec – 25 Apr; 2026/27: 12 Dec – 25 Apr)
les-arcs-paradiski.transfer: Chambéry ~2 h, Geneva ~2.5–3 h, Lyon ~2.5 h; train to Bourg-Saint-Maurice, then the funicular to Arc 1600 (7 min)
pros: 425 km of Paradiski pistes on one lift pass
The run from the Aiguille Rouge — ~2000 m vertical
Funicular from Bourg-Saint-Maurice station
Lots of easy runs, good for families
Russian-speaking instructors available
cons: 1960s–70s villages, the architecture is an acquired taste
Shorter season than Val Thorens/Tignes (until late April)
Après-ski is more modest than in Val d'Isère
les-arcs-paradiski.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, Paradiski (Les Arcs + La Plagne via the Vanoise Express), high season (schneehoehen.de); Les Arcs/Peisey-Vallandry only — €70 (skiresort.com)

tignes-val-disere.description: Formerly the Espace Killy, one of the highest and snowiest areas in the Alps: 300 km of pistes between Tignes (2100 m) and Val d'Isère (1850 m), topping out on the Grande Motte Glacier (3456 m). A freeride legend and the birthplace of La Folie Douce; a strong snowpark in Tignes and summer glacier skiing.
tignes-val-disere.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.7/5 (“world class”), “top” in 17 categories, including snow reliability, freeride and snowpark
tignes-val-disere.hazards: High avalanche danger off-piste (frequent avalanches in Val d'Isère); above the treeline — whiteouts and wind; on the glacier — crevasses beyond the markers; altitude up to 3456 m
tignes-val-disere.crowd_note: During the February holidays and at weekends queues at the main lifts out of Val d'Isère and Tignes-le-Lac; quieter in January and March
tignes-val-disere.season: late November – early May; summer skiing on the Grande Motte Glacier (roughly mid-June – July/early August, a few runs)
tignes-val-disere.transfer: Chambéry ~2.5 h, Geneva ~3 h, Lyon ~3 h; train to Bourg-Saint-Maurice, then bus ~45–60 min
pros: Altitude and reliable snow from November to May
World-class freeride
Summer skiing on the Grande Motte Glacier
Excellent snowpark in Tignes
Russian-speaking instructors available (SnoCool, Evolution 2)
cons: Expensive, especially Val d'Isère
Tignes — 1970s architecture and lots of concrete
Few easy runs for complete beginners, poor visibility above the treeline in bad weather
tignes-val-disere.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, the whole Tignes – Val d'Isère area, high season (schneehoehen.de); skiresort.com gives €75 (probably the 2025/26 season)

val-thorens.description: Les 3 Vallées is the world's largest linked ski area: Courchevel, Méribel, Les Menuires, Saint-Martin-de-Belleville, Orelle and Val Thorens on one lift pass. Val Thorens (2300 m) is Europe's highest resort, with reliable snow from late November to May. It suits every level: miles of blue and red runs, strong freeride and famous après-ski.
val-thorens.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.7/5 (“world class”), “top” in 18 categories; the world's largest linked area, Val Thorens repeatedly voted best resort at the World Ski Awards
val-thorens.hazards: Avalanche danger off-piste; there are no trees above 2300 m — visibility is lost in snowfall and fog; strong wind and frost on the summits; altitude above 3000 m
val-thorens.crowd_note: The huge area spreads people out, but during the French and British February holidays there are queues at key lifts in Val Thorens and Courchevel; blue runs get crowded towards evening
val-thorens.season: Val Thorens: late November – early May; the whole 3 Vallées area is linked roughly from early December to mid-April
val-thorens.transfer: Chambéry ~2 h, Lyon ~2.5–3 h, Geneva ~3 h; train to Moûtiers, then bus ~50 min
pros: 600 km of pistes on one lift pass
Val Thorens's altitude — snow from November to May
Ski-in/ski-out almost everywhere
Strong ski schools, Russian-speaking instructors available
Lively après-ski (La Folie Douce, Courchevel 1850)
cons: Expensive accommodation, especially in Courchevel
Val Thorens is above the treeline — poor visibility and wind in bad weather
Queues during the February holidays
val-thorens.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, 3 Vallées, high season (20 Dec – 10 Apr); Val Thorens–Orelle only — €71. skiresort.com gives €84.20 (probably already the 2026/27 season)

bakuriani.description: Georgia's oldest ski resort, in pine forest above Borjomi: a cosy village, kids' areas with magic carpets and a calm atmosphere — the best choice in Georgia for families. Several areas (Kokhta, Mitarbi, Didveli, Tatra); in 2023 the resort hosted the Freestyle and Snowboard World Championships. Cheap, and almost everyone speaks Russian.
bakuriani.rating_basis: skiresort.com test — 3.2/5 (“Good”); host of the 2023 FIS Freestyle and Snowboard World Championships; Georgia's best family resort according to reviews
bakuriani.hazards: Avalanche danger off-piste in Didveli and on Kokhta after snowfall, wind up top, icy slopes after thaws, black ice on the mountain road from Borjomi.
bakuriani.crowd_note: Busy over the New Year and Christmas holidays (until mid-January) and at weekends when people come from Tbilisi; calm on weekdays in February–March
bakuriani.season: mid/late December – late March (in snowy years until mid-April)
bakuriani.transfer: Tbilisi ~3 h (≈180 km), Kutaisi ~3–3.5 h; from Borjomi the narrow-gauge “Kukushka” train (~2.5 h) or a minibus ~40 min
pros: Family atmosphere, kids' areas and nursery slopes
Very cheap: lift pass ~€19, instructors, accommodation
Pine forest, slopes sheltered from the wind
Russian understood almost everywhere, visa-free for Russians
cons: The areas aren't fully linked yet, you have to drive between them
Short season, dependent on snowfall
Grooming and service lag behind Europe
Almost no après-ski
bakuriani.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult — 55 lari (≈€18–19) per skiresort.com and a 2026 season review; instructor ~100–120 lari/hour

gudauri.description: Georgia's highest and largest ski resort, on the Jvari (Cross) Pass: treeless slopes up to 3276 m, about 1300 m of vertical and some of Europe's best freeride at a low price, plus heliskiing and a cable car to the Kobi valley. The resort is fully geared to Russian-speaking guests: almost all locals speak Russian. The resort claims over 50 km of pistes; skiresort.com counts about 35 km of marked runs.
gudauri.rating_basis: skiresort.com test — 3.3/5 (“Good”): praised for huge open freeride terrain and heliskiing, marked down for grooming, queues and lift breakdowns; Georgia's main resort and one of the most popular with Russian-speaking skiers
gudauri.hazards: High avalanche danger off-piste (unguided freeriders have died), the Kobi – Gudauri run is often closed due to avalanches, strong wind and whiteouts on treeless slopes, altitude above 3000 m and strong sun, closures of the Georgian Military Road, lift breakdowns.
gudauri.crowd_note: Morning lift queues and crowded blue runs over the New Year holidays and at weekends (many tourists from Russia and Tbilisi); quieter in the afternoon and on weekdays in March
gudauri.season: mid/late December – mid-April (best in February – March)
gudauri.transfer: Tbilisi ~2–3 h (≈120 km; taxi from the airport 170–200 lari, minibus from Didube ~15 lari), Vladikavkaz ~2–3 h via the Upper Lars checkpoint (≈110 km, border queues), Kutaisi ~4–5 h
pros: Huge open freeride fields, heliskiing
Very cheap lift pass and instructors
Almost everyone speaks Russian, visa-free for Russians
Altitude up to 3276 m and plenty of natural snow
cons: Grooming and service are worse than in Europe
Queues and crowded blue runs during holidays
Wind and power cuts stop the lifts
The road over the Jvari Pass and the border closes in snowfall
gudauri.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, unlimited — 70 lari (≈€23); 4 days — 260 lari, a week — 370 lari; single ride 20 lari. The day-pass price hasn't changed for several seasons

gulmarg.description: A Himalayan freeride resort in Kashmir: a two-stage gondola climbs from 2650 m almost to the summit of Apharwat (~3980 m), opening up huge untracked bowls, couloirs and forest with over 1300 m of vertical. There are few groomed runs — this is a place for experienced riders with a guide and avalanche gear; in some seasons heliskiing operates. In recent years the resort has become a favourite of Russian freeriders: very cheap and lots of snow.
gulmarg.rating_basis: skiresort.com — 3.2/5 for infrastructure; a cult spot for freeriders: one of the world's highest gondolas (up to ~3980 m), huge untracked slopes and forest, low prices
gulmarg.hazards: Very high avalanche danger — foreign skiers, including Russians, have died in Gulmarg; a guide, transceiver, probe and shovel are essential. Altitude ~4000 m (altitude sickness), strong wind, an unstable situation in Kashmir — check foreign ministry travel advice
gulmarg.crowd_note: The slopes are uncrowded, but tickets for gondola phase 2 are limited — at peak season they sell out 2–3 days ahead; gondola queues at weekends due to Indian tourists
gulmarg.region: Kashmir (Jammu and Kashmir), Himalayas — Pir Panjal Range
gulmarg.season: second half of December – late March (best powder mid-January – February)
gulmarg.transfer: Srinagar airport (SXR) ~1.5–2 h by taxi (~50 km via Tangmarg); fly to Srinagar via Delhi
pros: World-class freeride and big vertical
Abundant snow and few people on the slopes
Very low prices for accommodation and guides
Himalayan and Kashmiri exotica
cons: Few lifts and groomed runs, limited infrastructure
Gondola phase 2 is often closed due to wind and avalanche danger
Political instability in the region, complicated logistics
Almost no après-ski (alcohol is hard to come by)

dizin.description: Iran's main ski resort, in the Alborz range north of Tehran: base at 2650 m, lifts up to 3600 m, 4 gondolas and dry snow. The slopes are mostly for intermediate and advanced skiers; off-piste there's freeride with a guide, but lots of rocks. Exotic and cheap, but with strict rules: a mandatory dress code for women (headscarf) and no alcohol.
dizin.rating_basis: skiresort.com — 3.0/5; Iran's largest and best-known resort, the first in the country recognised by FIS; high base and dry snow
dizin.hazards: Avalanche danger (the road via Shemshak is often closed), rocks off-piste, altitude up to 3600 m and strong UV; an unstable situation in the country — check foreign ministry travel advice before you go
dizin.crowd_note: At weekends (Thursday–Friday) and holidays — crowds from Tehran and gondola queues; quiet on weekdays
dizin.season: December – April (until May in snowy years)
dizin.transfer: From Tehran ~2.5 h via Karaj (~120 km) or ~70 km on the short road via Shemshak (often closed due to avalanches); Imam Khomeini airport (IKA) ~3–3.5 h
pros: High base and dry snow
Very inexpensive for foreigners
Big vertical for its size
Iran's exotica and culture
cons: Outdated lifts and limited infrastructure
Weekend crowds
No après-ski or alcohol, strict dress code
Difficult political situation and sanctions (foreign bank cards don't work)

cortina-dampezzo.description: Cortina d'Ampezzo is the “Queen of the Dolomites”, a society resort with the pedestrian Corso Italia and the host town of the 2026 Winter Olympics. 120 km of pistes across several areas (Tofana, Cristallo, Faloria, Lagazuoi – Cinque Torri) with dramatic views of the Dolomite rock faces; the Dolomiti Superski pass covers 1200 km in 12 valleys. Great for leisurely skiing, gastronomy and shopping.
cortina-dampezzo.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.1/5 (“outstanding”), “top” in 13 categories; host of the 2026 Winter Olympics (women's alpine skiing on the Tofana), the Olympia delle Tofane World Cup run
cortina-dampezzo.hazards: Steep couloirs and cliffs off-piste (Tofana, Cristallo) — rockfall and avalanches; hard ice on the Olympic runs; winding mountain roads to the resort
cortina-dampezzo.crowd_note: Slopes are usually uncrowded — many guests come for the social life; busy at Christmas and on Italian weekends
cortina-dampezzo.season: late November – early April; some sectors (Tofana) may run until late April (2026/27: 21 Nov – 2 May)
cortina-dampezzo.transfer: Venice ~2 h, Treviso ~2 h, Innsbruck ~2.5 h, Bolzano ~2 h
pros: Dolomite scenery (a UNESCO site)
2026 Olympic infrastructure
Uncrowded slopes
Gastronomy, shopping, society life
Russian-speaking instructors available
cons: Scattered areas, buses needed
Expensive
Little serious freeride and a modest snowpark
cortina-dampezzo.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, Dolomiti Superski, high season; €89 for 2026/27. Cortina's local lift pass is about €80 (skiresort.com)

livigno.description: Livigno is a high-altitude (1816 m) duty-free resort on the Swiss border: two sides of the valley (Mottolino and Carosello) with 115 km of pistes, reliable snow from late November to May and one of Europe's best snowparks. Inexpensive by Alpine standards and popular with young people and snowboarders; in 2026 it hosted the Olympic snowboard and freestyle events.
livigno.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.4/5 (“outstanding”), “top” in 17 categories; the Mottolino snowpark was the venue for snowboard and freestyle at the 2026 Olympics
livigno.hazards: Severe frost and wind on open slopes; the Foscagno and Forcola passes in winter — chains, possible closures; avalanche danger off-piste
livigno.crowd_note: Busy at Christmas, in February and at Easter (many guests from Eastern Europe); Saturday is changeover day, so the slopes are quieter
livigno.season: late November – early May (2026/27: 28 Nov – 2 May)
livigno.transfer: Milan Bergamo ~3.5–4 h, Milan Malpensa ~4 h, Innsbruck ~3 h, Zurich ~3.5 h (via the Munt la Schera tunnel)
pros: Altitude — season until early May
Pro-level Mottolino snowpark
Duty-free zone — cheaper shopping and fuel
Lots of easy and intermediate runs
Lively après-ski
cons: Far from airports, the road goes over passes
Little challenging terrain and modest vertical (~1000 m)
Very cold in January
livigno.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, high season (26 Dec – 8 Jan and 31 Jan – 29 Mar); €61 on Saturdays in high season. skiresort.com gives €72 (probably 2025/26)

madonna-di-campiglio.description: Madonna di Campiglio is an elegant Trentino resort at the foot of the Brenta Dolomites. The linked Skiarea Campiglio (155 km) joins Madonna, Pinzolo, Folgarida and Marilleva; near-total snowmaking, immaculate pistes, the Ursus snowpark and the legendary Canalone Miramonti slalom slope, home of the 3Tre World Cup race.
madonna-di-campiglio.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.7/5 (“world class”), “top” in 17 categories; the 3Tre World Cup slalom on the Canalone Miramonti
madonna-di-campiglio.hazards: Avalanche danger and cliffs off-piste; hard ice on the pistes in the morning; mountain roads — winter tyres and chains
madonna-di-campiglio.crowd_note: Busy during Italian holidays (Christmas, New Year) and in February; quiet on weekdays in January and March
madonna-di-campiglio.transfer: Verona ~2.5 h, Milan Bergamo ~3 h, Innsbruck ~3 h; train to Trento, then bus ~1.5 h
pros: 155 km of linked pistes and excellent grooming
Near-total artificial snowmaking
The beautiful Brenta Dolomites
A good choice for families and intermediates
Russian-speaking instructors available
cons: Not very high (up to 2504 m), season until mid-April
Expensive accommodation in Madonna itself
Little genuine freeride
madonna-di-campiglio.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, Skiarea Campiglio (Madonna, Pinzolo, Folgarida, Marilleva), high season; €89 on peak dates. skiresort.com gives €85 (probably 2025/26)

val-gardena.description: Val Gardena (Ortisei, Santa Cristina, Selva) is one of the main valleys of Dolomiti Superski: 181 km of its own pistes and direct access to the 40 km Sella Ronda circuit around the Sella massif, with 1200 km in 12 valleys on the shared pass. Breathtaking Dolomite scenery, South Tyrolean food in the mountain huts, the Saslong World Cup run and the 10.5 km La Longia run from Seceda.
val-gardena.rating_basis: skiresort.com: 4.7/5 (“world class”), “top” in 17 categories; World Cup on the Saslong, the Sella Ronda circuit, the Dolomites a UNESCO site
val-gardena.hazards: Steep rocky slopes off-piste — rockfall couloirs and avalanches (Val Mezdì only with a guide); hard ice on groomed pistes in the morning; on the Sella Ronda make sure you catch the last lifts
val-gardena.crowd_note: During Italian holidays, in February and on the Sella Ronda — queues at the Dantercepies and Ciampinoi lifts, busy on the main runs
val-gardena.season: early December – early April (2026/27: 4 Dec – 4 Apr)
val-gardena.transfer: Bolzano ~1 h, Innsbruck ~1.5–2 h, Verona ~2.5 h, Venice/Treviso ~3 h, Munich ~3.5 h
pros: The Dolomites — some of the most beautiful scenery in the Alps
The Sella Ronda circuit and 1200 km on one lift pass
Excellent mountain huts and food
Near-total artificial snowmaking
Russian-speaking instructors available
cons: Not very high (up to 2518 m) — in snowless winters you ski on artificial snow
Crowded on the Sella Ronda in February
Little genuine freeride, the season ends in early April
val-gardena.airport: BZO — Bolzano, ~1 h (major airports: VRN — Verona ~2.5 h, INN — Innsbruck ~1.5–2 h)
val-gardena.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, Dolomiti Superski (1200 km in 12 valleys), high season; €89 for 2026/27. A Val Gardena/Alpe di Siusi-only pass is about €83 (skiresort.com)

hakuba-valley.description: The Hakuba Valley is ten resorts in the Japanese Northern Alps with a shared Hakuba Valley lift pass and buses between them; the main one is Olympic Happo-One, with more than 1000 m of vertical. It has Japan's most “alpine” terrain: open slopes above the treeline, tree-skiing freeride at Cortina and Tsugaike, and backcountry. Also good for beginners (Iwatake, Tsugaike) and families; the Happo and Echoland villages have restaurants and bars.
hakuba-valley.rating_basis: Nagano 1998 Olympic runs, a Freeride World Tour stop; skiresort.com gives Happo-One itself 3.3/5 for infrastructure; one of Japan's two leading resorts
hakuba-valley.hazards: High avalanche danger in the Northern Alps backcountry, registration and gear required; whiteouts, strong wind and icing on the Happo ridge, tree wells in the forest
hakuba-valley.crowd_note: Queues for the Happo gondola at weekends and over New Year, lots of Australians in January; the valley's other resorts are quieter
hakuba-valley.season: early December – early May (reliable snow from late December to March)
hakuba-valley.transfer: From Tokyo: shinkansen to Nagano ~1.5 h + bus ~1 h 10 min; direct bus/transfer from Haneda or Narita ~4–5 h
pros: Japan's biggest and steepest terrain, genuine alpine freeride
One lift pass for the valley's 10 resorts
Lots of snow and onsen in the village
Easy to reach from Tokyo by rail
cons: The resorts aren't linked by lifts — you need a bus
The lower slopes depend on snow at the start and end of the season
Poor visibility and wind up top close the upper lifts
Pricier than local Nagano resorts
hakuba-valley.airport: HND — Tokyo Haneda, ~4 h (NRT Narita ~4.5–5 h)
hakuba-valley.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, Happo-One only (ticket office, weekends) — ¥8,700; the shared Hakuba Valley Ticket for the valley's 10 resorts — ¥10,400 (¥11,100 announced for 2026/27)

niseko-united.description: Hokkaido's largest resort: four linked areas on a single mountain, Niseko Annupuri, with a shared lift pass and views of Mount Yotei. Famous for dry “Japow” — about 15 m of snow a season, tree skiing and official gates into the backcountry. Hirafu is an international village with loads of restaurants, bars and English-speaking ski schools; it also has the biggest night-skiing operation in Japan.
niseko-united.rating_basis: skiresort.com — 4.4/5 (“Outstanding”); one of the world's best-known powder resorts, top of Japan in reviews
niseko-united.hazards: Avalanche danger beyond the ski area — exit only through open gates and with avalanche gear; tree wells, whiteouts and strong wind at the summit, frostbite in January–February
niseko-united.crowd_note: Queues at the lower Hirafu lifts and crowds in the village at New Year, Chinese New Year and during the Australian holidays (January); quieter on weekdays in March
niseko-united.season: late November – early May (main season mid-December – March)
niseko-united.transfer: New Chitose airport (Sapporo) ~2–2.5 h by bus or transfer (~117 km); from Sapporo ~2 h
pros: Tons of light, dry snow, consistent snowfall in December–February
Legal backcountry access through gates (Niseko Rules)
Night skiing until 20:30
Well-developed infrastructure, lots of restaurants and English-speaking staff
cons: Modest vertical (~900 m) and moderately steep runs
Frequent fog, wind and upper-lift closures
Expensive accommodation and crowds in peak weeks
Very cold in January–February
niseko-united.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, shared All Mountain pass for the 4 areas, main season (13 Dec – 22 Mar) — ¥12,000; cheaper in early spring and late season. ¥12,600 (regular season) and ¥13,500 (peak, 24 Dec – 28 Feb) announced for 2026/27

rusutsu.description: A resort-hotel spread over three mountains (East, West and Isola), an hour's drive from Niseko: lots of “Japow” in the trees, wide runs with views of Lake Toya and Mount Yotei, and few people. Good for families and tree-skiing fans, but nightlife is limited to the hotel. The Hokkaido alternative is Furano in the centre of the island: colder, drier snow, open until early May, 2025/26 lift pass ¥8,000.
rusutsu.rating_basis: skiresort.com — 4.1/5 (“Outstanding”); renowned for tree powder and well-groomed runs, the first Japanese resort to win “Best Small Resort” from the British Good Skiing & Snowboarding Guide
rusutsu.hazards: Avalanche danger and tree wells off-piste, severe frost and wind in January–February, whiteouts
rusutsu.crowd_note: Noticeably quieter than Niseko; queues only at the gondolas by the hotel during holidays
rusutsu.season: late November / early December – late March (sometimes until the first days of April)
rusutsu.transfer: New Chitose ~1.5 h by bus/transfer; Sapporo ~1.5–2 h; Niseko ~40 min
pros: Excellent tree freeride and powder without the crowds
Close to Chitose airport
Night skiing and family facilities
cons: Expensive lift pass at the ticket office (cheaper online)
Small vertical (~600 m)
Almost no après-ski outside the hotel
Closes in late March
rusutsu.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, ticket office, main season (20 Dec – 15 Mar) — ¥16,200; online in advance — ¥12,000 (~€68)

karakol.description: Kyrgyzstan's main ski base, in a spruce-forested gorge above the town of Karakol near the eastern shore of Issyk-Kul: four or five chairlifts up to 3040 m, about 20 km of pistes, steep slopes and lots of powder. Higher up by snowmobile you reach 3450 m and the Tian Shan backcountry; cat-skiing in Jyrgalan and hot springs are nearby.
karakol.rating_basis: Kyrgyzstan's best ski base: ~20 km of pistes, lots of steep terrain and powder (2.5–4 m of snow a season), but slow old chairs; skiresort.info test — 2.9 out of 5; Powderhounds recommends it as a warm-up before cat-skiing in Jyrgalan
karakol.hazards: Avalanche danger off-piste (the boundary between pistes and untracked terrain is barely marked), altitude up to 3000–3450 m, frost and wind up top; the mountain road to the base can be icy
karakol.crowd_note: Almost no queues except over the New Year holidays; most guests stick to the nursery slopes, leaving the powder untouched
karakol.region: Issyk-Kul Region, Terskey Ala-Too range, Tian Shan (11 km from Karakol)
karakol.season: mid-December – late March (in snowy years from late November to early April)
karakol.transfer: 11 km from Karakol (~25–30 min by taxi, no shuttles); Issyk-Kul airport (Tamchy) ~200 km, ~3 h; Bishkek ~400 km, 6–7 h; Almaty ~6–7 h via the Kegen – Karkyra border crossing
pros: Good powder and steep tree slopes, few people
Very low prices for lift passes and accommodation
Snowmobile rides up to 3450 m, backcountry and cat-skiing nearby
No visa needed, Russian spoken everywhere
cons: Old, slow chairlifts
A long trip from Bishkek and Almaty
Modest service and rental
Snow varies from season to season
karakol.airport: IKU — Issyk-Kul (Tamchy), ~3 h; FRU — Bishkek, ~6–7 h
karakol.lift_pass_note: 1 day (09:00–16:00), adult: 2000 som in high season 31 Dec – 10 Jan; in regular season — 1400 som (Tue–Thu) and 1700 som (Fri–Mon); night skiing 18:30–22:00 — 1000/1200 som; card — 300 som

yongpyong.description: South Korea's oldest and largest resort, venue for the technical events of the 2018 Olympics (Pyeongchang). The runs are almost entirely on artificial snow, a long gondola goes up to the Balwangsan summit, and there's night skiing until midnight. Popular with people from the Russian Far East as a nearby destination; in 2015 the resort advertised lessons in English, Spanish, Italian and Russian.
yongpyong.rating_basis: skiresort.com — 3.1/5; Korea's largest and best-known resort, technical events of the 2018 Olympics
yongpyong.hazards: Hard artificial snow and ice on steep runs, severe frost with wind in January, collisions on crowded slopes at weekends
yongpyong.crowd_note: Very busy at weekends and on Korean holidays (Lunar New Year) — people come from Seoul; noticeably quieter on weekdays
yongpyong.season: mid/late November – late March, sometimes until early April
yongpyong.transfer: From Seoul ~2.5–3 h by shuttle/bus (~200 km) or KTX to Jinbu (Odaesan) station ~1.5 h + 15 min by taxi/shuttle; from Incheon ~3 h
pros: Close to Vladivostok and Seoul, easy logistics
Reliable snowmaking and well-groomed runs
Night skiing until midnight
The Olympic Rainbow run for experienced skiers
cons: Small amount of terrain (~24 km)
Little natural snow, no freeride (off-piste skiing is banned)
Weekend crowds
Cold wind in January

shymbulak.description: The main ski resort of Kazakhstan and all of Central Asia, in the Trans-Ili Alatau above Almaty: a gondola from the Medeu ice rink, skiing from 2260 to 3180 m (Talgar Pass), about 20 km of pistes and huge freeride potential. Popular with Russians — no visa, Russian spoken everywhere, and a city full of restaurants half an hour away.
shymbulak.rating_basis: Central Asia's largest and most developed resort, 30 minutes from Almaty: a gondola from Medeu, skiing up to 3180 m, lots of off-piste terrain (Powderhounds); skiresort.info test — 3.1 out of 5
shymbulak.hazards: High avalanche danger off-piste in the Trans-Ili Alatau, strong wind and cold on the Talgar Pass (3180 m), altitude — altitude sickness possible; mudflows in the off-season
shymbulak.crowd_note: At weekends and holidays (New Year, Nauryz) queues for the Medeu – Shymbulak gondola and the lower chairs; noticeably quieter on weekdays
shymbulak.region: Trans-Ili Alatau, Tian Shan, above the Medeu valley, Almaty
shymbulak.season: mid/late November – mid-April (until May in snowy years)
shymbulak.transfer: Almaty airport ~35 km: 40–60 min by taxi to Medeu, then the gondola to Shymbulak; you can also drive to the base
pros: Altitude up to 3180 m — reliable snow and a long season
Lots of off-piste terrain below the Talgar Pass
30–40 minutes from a big city and airport
Visa-free for Russians, Russian spoken everywhere
cons: Small ski area (~20 km of pistes)
A noticeable lift pass price hike in 2025/26
Queues at weekends and holidays
Wind and cold above 3000 m
shymbulak.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult — 26,000 ₸ (up from 17,500 ₸, per Ranking.kz, December 2025); tiered pricing introduced: about 30% cheaper on average in low season (other sources say 12,000–13,400 ₸); the Medeu – Shymbulak gondola in high season (25 Dec – 11 Jan) — 5000 ₸ one way

kolasin.description: A fast-growing resort on Mount Bjelasica, 10 km from the town of Kolašin: two areas (1450 and 1600) linked by a chairlift, about 45 km of pistes up to 2070 m. Plenty of snow thanks to moist winds off the Adriatic, a very cheap lift pass, a quiet atmosphere and wide slopes. Under the Kolasin Valleys master plan the area is set to grow to 150 km by 2030.
kolasin.rating_basis: skiresort.com test — 3.6/5 (“Very good”): pistes, lifts, snow, families, freeride; one of Europe's cheapest resorts for lift passes
kolasin.hazards: Avalanche danger off-piste after heavy snowfall, wind and fog on the Bjelasica ridge, snowdrifts and black ice on mountain roads, warm Adriatic thaws.
kolasin.crowd_note: Queues only over the New Year holidays and at weekends; the resort is growing fast but still uncrowded
kolasin.season: mid-December – early April (in snowy years from late November)
kolasin.transfer: Podgorica ~1–1.5 h (~45–60 min on the new motorway to Kolašin + the drive up to the resort), Tivat ~2.5–3 h; the Belgrade – Bar train stops in Kolašin
pros: One of the cheapest lift passes in Europe
Snowy climate, good freeride terrain
Few people, new chairlifts
An hour from Podgorica airport, the sea nearby
cons: Still a small area with little slopeside infrastructure
Almost no après-ski
Only partial snowmaking
Little information about ski schools and instructors
kolasin.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, main season — €25 per skiresort.com and a SportsCover Direct (Time Out) review; the season the price refers to isn't stated, check locally

mavrovo.description: North Macedonia's main ski resort, on the shore of Lake Mavrovo in a national park: about 15 km of pistes (other sources say up to 27 km), ~620 m vertical, with ski tours to Mount Korab (2764 m) nearby. Very cheap and quiet, but the lifts are mostly old T-bars. The resort is run by Jahorina's operator (OC Jahorina). A higher alternative is Popova Šapka near Tetovo (1672–2380 m, ~18 km of pistes, 1,300 MKD).
mavrovo.rating_basis: skiresort.com test — 2.8/5; North Macedonia's largest resort, but with old lifts and low mountains
mavrovo.hazards: Unreliable snow and ice during thaws, fog, avalanche danger on tours to Korab, snowdrifts on the Gostivar – Mavrovo road.
mavrovo.crowd_note: Busy only over the New Year holidays and at weekends (visitors from Skopje); almost empty on weekdays
mavrovo.region: Mavrovo National Park, western North Macedonia
pros: Very cheap lift pass and accommodation
Beautiful national park and lake
Ski touring and freeride around Korab
Visa-free for Russians
cons: Small area, old T-bar lifts
Low mountains — unreliable snow
Modest infrastructure and après-ski
2 hours from Skopje
mavrovo.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult (24+) — 1,500 MKD (≈€24); youth 14–23 — 1,250 MKD, children — 1,050 MKD. Season pass holders get 2 free days at Jahorina (shared operator OC Jahorina)

trysil.description: Norway's largest ski resort: about 80 km of pistes on four sides of Trysilfjellet (Turistsenteret, Høgegga, Fageråsen, Skihytta) with ski-in/ski-out accommodation. One of Europe's best for families with children and beginners, with excellent snowparks and night skiing. If you want bigger mountains and freeride, look at Hemsedal.
trysil.rating_basis: skiresort.com test — 4.4/5 (“Outstanding”): snow, families, beginners, snowpark, accommodation; Norway's largest resort. The alternative with more mountainous terrain is Hemsedal (44 km, 830 m vertical, 4.3/5)
trysil.hazards: Severe frost (down to −20…−30 °C) and wind on the treeless summit, frostbite, short daylight in December–January, whiteouts up top, ice on steep slopes.
trysil.crowd_note: Peak times are the Norwegian winter holidays (February), Easter and New Year; queues at the gondola in Turistsenteret, quiet on weekdays in January and March
trysil.region: Innlandet, eastern Norway (near the Swedish border)
trysil.transfer: Scandinavian Mountains Airport in Sälen (SCR, Sweden) ~45 min, Oslo Gardermoen ~2.5 h (≈190 km, buses)
pros: Norway's largest area, lots of slopeside accommodation
Great for families and beginners, kids' areas
Reliable snow and powerful snowmaking
Night skiing, good snowparks
cons: Low mountain (up to 1100 m) — little freeride
Expensive: lift pass, food, alcohol
Severe frost and short days in December–January
Far from Oslo
trysil.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, main season — 808 NOK (≈€76) per skiresort.com; SkiStar uses dynamic pricing, cheaper when bought online in advance

queenstown-coronet-peak.description: The closest ski field to Queenstown: 280 ha of open, treeless slopes, ~460 m vertical, a powerful snowmaking system and night skiing on Wednesdays and Fridays. Neighbouring The Remarkables (1610–1943 m, ~20 km of pistes) is the best choice for beginners and snowparks, on the same NZSki pass. The big plus is Queenstown with its restaurants, bars and adventures (bungy, jet boats, heliskiing in the Southern Alps).
queenstown-coronet-peak.rating_basis: skiresort.com — 3.7/5 (The Remarkables — 3.6/5); New Zealand's first ski field (1947), the best snowmaking in the Southern Hemisphere, Queenstown the “adventure capital”
queenstown-coronet-peak.hazards: Strong wind and whiteouts on open slopes, ice in the mornings on man-made-snow runs, black ice on the mountain road (chains needed); avalanche danger off-piste
queenstown-coronet-peak.crowd_note: Busy during the July school holidays in New Zealand and Australia and at weekends; quiet on weekdays in August–September
queenstown-coronet-peak.season: mid-June – late September (The Remarkables — until early October)
queenstown-coronet-peak.transfer: Queenstown airport (ZQN) ~25 min; 16 km from central Queenstown, ~20 min, ski buses available
pros: Skiing in July–September 20 minutes from town
Night skiing and powerful snowmaking
Great après-ski and Queenstown's entertainment
One lift pass for Coronet Peak, The Remarkables and Mt Hutt
cons: Low altitude and vertical, little natural snow
No slopeside accommodation — you drive up every day
Wind and changeable weather
Expensive flights from Europe
queenstown-coronet-peak.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, 2026 season — NZ$180 (one price for weekdays and weekends); NZSki passes (Superpass, Saver Pass) are also valid at The Remarkables and Mt Hutt

poiana-brasov.description: Romania's main ski resort, 12 km from medieval Brașov: a small area on Mount Postăvarul with about 840 m of vertical, a gondola and night skiing. Good for a short trip combined with sightseeing in Transylvania (Bran, Brașov), but a bit small for a week of skiing.
poiana-brasov.rating_basis: skiresort.com test — 2.9/5: a small area (~14 km) with a large share of difficult runs; Romania's most popular resort
poiana-brasov.hazards: Icy slopes after thaws, fog, heavy traffic on the pistes at weekends; off-piste — dense forest and bears in the surroundings (in the warmer months).
poiana-brasov.crowd_note: At weekends and holidays lots of visitors from Bucharest, queues for the gondola and cable car; calm on weekdays
poiana-brasov.transfer: Brașov-Ghimbav ~30 min, Bucharest (Otopeni) ~3 h (≈170 km), Sibiu ~2.5 h
pros: Brașov and the castles of Transylvania nearby
~840 m vertical, some steep runs
Night skiing, snowmaking on the main runs
New Brașov airport 30 minutes away
cons: Only ~14 km of pistes
Low mountains — unreliable snow
Weekend queues
Russians need a Schengen visa
poiana-brasov.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult, main season — 240 RON (≈€48) per skiresort.com

kopaonik.description: Serbia's main ski resort, on a plateau inside a national park: a compact hotel centre at 1700 m and about 55 km of pistes up to the Pančićev vrh summit (2017 m). Good for beginners and families, with night skiing and lively nightlife. Visa-free for Russians, with Russian-speaking instructors.
kopaonik.rating_basis: skiresort.com test — 4.2/5: families, beginners, restaurants, accommodation; Serbia's largest resort
kopaonik.hazards: Strong wind and fog on the open plateau, ice during thaws, black ice on the mountain road; avalanche risk off-piste is low but possible in steep couloirs.
kopaonik.crowd_note: Peak times are New Year, Orthodox Christmas and the Serbian school holidays (late January – February), plus weekends; quiet on weekdays in March
kopaonik.transfer: Niš ~2–2.5 h (≈110 km), Belgrade ~4 h (≈280 km; ~5 h by bus)
pros: Visa-free entry for Russian citizens, Russian-speaking instructors available
Ski-in/ski-out hotels in a compact centre
Inexpensive by European standards
Night skiing, lively après-ski
cons: Low mountains (up to 2017 m) — snow depends on the winter and snowmaking
Few difficult runs
Far from Belgrade, poor public transport
Busy during holidays and school breaks
kopaonik.lift_pass_note: 1 day, adult: 5,600–6,500 RSD depending on the period (high season at the top end); skiresort.com — 5,900 RSD ≈ €50

abzakovo.description: A popular Urals resort in Bashkortostan near Novoabzakovo: 13 runs totalling about 15 km on the slopes of Mount Shaitan, with artificial snowmaking and floodlights. Good for family skiing and weekends from Magnitogorsk, Chelyabinsk and Ufa; 25 km away is the Bannoe resort (Metallurg-Magnitogorsk) on Lake Bannoe, with a gondola and 450 m of vertical.
abzakovo.rating_basis: One of the Urals' main resorts: 13 runs (15 km), snowmaking, night skiing; skiresort.info test — 2.8 out of 5. Neighbouring Bannoe (Metallurg-Magnitogorsk, 25 km) — 450 m vertical, a Doppelmayr gondola, but only a few runs
abzakovo.hazards: Severe frost (−20…−30 °C) and wind in December – February, icy pistes during thaws; practically no avalanche danger
abzakovo.crowd_note: Queues for the Kometa chairlift at weekends and over the New Year holidays, quiet on weekdays
abzakovo.region: Beloretsky District, Bashkortostan, Southern Urals (near Magnitogorsk)
abzakovo.season: late November – mid-April; in good years from early November to early May
abzakovo.transfer: Magnitogorsk ~60 km, ~1 h (bus/suburban train to Novoabzakovo, then 3 km); Magnitogorsk airport ~1 h; Ufa ~5 h, Chelyabinsk ~4.5–5 h
pros: Snowmaking — a reliable season from November
Night skiing on floodlit runs
Suits beginners and families
A second resort, Bannoe, nearby
cons: Small vertical (~300–370 m) and few difficult runs
Severe frost and wind in January
Mostly T-bar lifts
Far from major airports
abzakovo.lift_pass_note: 1 day, weekdays — 3400 ₽ (more at weekends); in 2024/25 from 3000 ₽ on weekdays and from 3400 ₽ at weekends, shared with Metallurg; 2 hours — from 1600 ₽

arkhyz.description: A new year-round resort in the North Caucasus with the Romantik village at the lower stations: about 27 km of pistes on the southern and northern slopes, modern gondolas and bubble chairlifts, and the Orbita viewing platform at 3030 m.
