costa-blanca-sella.airport: ALC — Alicante, ~1 h; VLC — Valencia, ~1.5–2 h
school_notes: Week-long trips and sport and multi-pitch courses
Guides for the Alicante areas
Beginner and intermediate courses

el-chorro.description: The limestone Los Gaitanes gorge by the famous Caminito del Rey walkway is one of Europe's top winter areas. Hundreds of routes for beginners and intermediates, classic multi-pitches of up to 12 pitches on the Frontales, and hard overhangs at Desplomilandia and Makinódromo. Warm Andalusian winters and direct flights to Málaga.
el-chorro.rating_basis: One of Europe's most popular winter areas: >1,500 routes from grade 4 to the eighth grade, classic multi-pitch on the Frontales, the Caminito del Rey gorge; high ratings on UKC/theCrag/27crags
el-chorro.hazards: Rockfall on multi-pitches (including from mountain goats) — wear a helmet; heat; scrambling on the approaches
el-chorro.crowd_note: Busy from November to April, especially at Christmas and Easter; there can be queues on Amptrax and in Escalera Árabe, and the classics are polished
el-chorro.region: Andalusia, Málaga province, Álora — Los Gaitanes gorge (Caminito del Rey)
el-chorro.season: mid-October to early May; best November–April; up to 40 °C in summer — off-season
el-chorro.transfer: ~1 h by car from Málaga (A-357); the village has an El Chorro train station; you need a car to get between sectors
el-chorro.rock_note: grey and orange limestone: slabs and vertical walls on the Frontales (walls up to 200 m), overhangs and tufas at Desplomilandia and Makinódromo, steep caves at Poema de Roca
el-chorro.approach: from 5 min to 1–2 h; the Frontales are reached on foot from the parking by the reservoir, in places scrambling along rock ledges; Desplomilandia, Makinódromo and Abdalajís are easier to reach by car
el-chorro.restrictions: Natural park: climbing in the Gaitanes gorge itself along the Caminito del Rey is no longer possible (access to the walkway only with a booking and from the northern entrance); the old routes of the Los Albercones sector by the railway shelter are banned; roadside parking in the park is prohibited where signposted; sectors may be temporarily closed during bird nesting — follow announcements from local clubs
el-chorro.guidebook: El Chorro (2024, >1,500 routes, >80 sectors: El Chorro, Desplomilandia, Valle de Abdalajís), Rockfax El Chorro
el-chorro.stay: Climbers' lodges Climbing Lodge, The Olive Branch (rooms, van parking) and Finca La Campana, Parque Ardales campground by the lake; also Álora, Ardales and the Abdalajís valley
pros: Warm, dry winter
Routes for all levels, good for beginners
Classic multi-pitch on the Frontales
Close to Málaga airport, climbers' lodges
cons: Summer heat up to 40 °C
Polished classics
Approaches to some sectors are long and involve scrambling
Crowded during holidays
famous_lines: Amptrax 6a+, ~200 m (Frontales) — the ultimate multi-pitch classic
Vía de las Cabras 5 (Suizo) — the area's first route, 1972
school_notes: Beginner courses, multi-pitch with a private guide, combos with the Caminito del Rey; gear and shoes included
Climbing camp-course
Certified guides
Climbing courses in Andalusia

mallorca.description: The island where modern deep-water soloing was born: overhanging limestone cliffs, caves and arches above the turquoise water of the east coast, including Sharma's Es Pontàs 9a+. In winter and spring climbers head for the sport routes in the Tramuntana mountains — Sa Gubia, Fraguel, Gorg Blau.
mallorca.rating_basis: The best place for DWS in Europe (Rockfax), Sharma's Es Pontàs, plus hundreds of sport routes in the Tramuntana for winter; 27crags, UKC, Climb Europe
mallorca.hazards: Falls into the water from height — entering the water badly causes injuries; swell and rocks at the base, sea urchins; heat; old bolts on some routes
mallorca.crowd_note: In summer the coves are full of swimmers and Cala Barques can get busy; in winter the mountain crags are quiet
mallorca.region: Balearic Islands; DWS on the east coast (Porto Cristo, Cala Barques, Cala Serena), sport in the Tramuntana mountains (Sa Gubia, Fraguel, Gorg Blau)
mallorca.season: DWS: June–October (warm water), best September–October; sport climbing: late September–May
mallorca.transfer: Palma airport (car hire on site), ~1 h to Porto Cristo, ~20 min to Sa Gubia; ferries also run from Barcelona and Valencia
mallorca.rock_note: limestone: on the coast, overhanging sea cliffs, caves and arches 5–20 m above the water for DWS; in the Tramuntana mountains, grey walls and the multi-pitch routes of Sa Gubia
mallorca.approach: DWS cliffs: 5–20 min from parking at the coves, then a down-climb or traverse to the start above the water; mountain crags: 5–30 min; a car is needed
mallorca.restrictions: Before your trip check current access to Cala Magraner and Port de Sóller (there have been construction works and barriers); the older routes at Cala Magraner have old bolts. DWS only when the sea is calm and the rock is dry
mallorca.guidebook: Rockfax Mallorca Deep Water Soloing (490 routes, 16 crags), Mallorca Sport Climbing; DWS topo on 27crags (≈780 routes, 20 crags)
mallorca.stay: For DWS — Cala d'Or and Porto Cristo in the south-east; for sport — Palma, Sóller, Valldemossa, Port de Pollença
pros: Europe's best deep-water soloing
Two seasons: DWS in summer and autumn, sport in winter and spring
Lots of flights and infrastructure
Warm sea
cons: DWS depends on the swell and how damp the rock is
Hot and touristy in summer
Crags are spread across the island — car needed
In winter the mountains can get prolonged rain and seepage
mallorca.airport: PMI — Palma de Mallorca, ~1 h to the east coast
famous_lines: Es Pontàs 9a+ (DWS, arch near Santanyí) — Chris Sharma, 2007
Cova del Diablo (Porto Cristo) — DWS test pieces up to 18 m
school_notes: Guided climbing and deep-water soloing
Group and private sessions, family climbing

margalef.description: A valley of conglomerate walls and caves in the Montsant Natural Park — the mecca of pocket climbing. It has whole sectors of grade 4–6 routes for beginners alongside some of the hardest routes in the world (First Round First Minute 9b, Perfecto Mundo 9b+). Because of its huge popularity, access to the main zones has required a booking since 2025.
margalef.rating_basis: One of the world's best conglomerate areas: ~1,870 routes, 9b and 9b+, lots of quality 6a–7b; popular with all levels (27crags, UKC, PlanetMountain)
margalef.hazards: Finger injuries on one- and two-finger pockets, summer heat, pebbles popping out of the conglomerate
margalef.crowd_note: ~89,000 visits a year; at Easter and over the 1 November holiday the main zones are overflowing — which is why barriers and booking were introduced
margalef.region: Catalonia, Priorat (Tarragona), Serra del Montsant Natural Park
margalef.season: October–April; in winter the south-facing walls of Espadelles, in spring and autumn everything, in summer shady sectors early in the morning and in the evening
margalef.transfer: A car is needed: there's almost no public transport; Reus ~1.5 h, Barcelona ~2–2.5 h
margalef.rock_note: conglomerate with pockets from single-finger to palm-sized holes: overhangs, caves, powerful routes up to 50 m
margalef.approach: short approaches of 5–20 min from the El Pont and La Presa car parks; comfortable, safe ground at the base of the walls — suitable for families
margalef.restrictions: Since 14 October 2025 access to the two main zones (Sant Salvador and Embassament / Espadelles) is through barriers with online booking, €5 per car per day, capped at ~210 and ~190 cars; overnight stays outside designated areas are not allowed. The area lies within the Montsant Natural Park
margalef.stay: El Racó de la Finestra and Can Severet refugios, houses and apartments in the village, campervan and tent areas by the El Pont and La Presa car parks (as of 2026 some services had closed — check in advance)
pros: Unique pocketed conglomerate
Routes for all levels — from 4 to 9b+
Short approaches and safe ground at the base of the walls
Siurana and Montsant nearby
cons: Overflowing on holidays and at Easter
Paid access and booking since 2025
Pockets are hard on the fingers
Hot in summer
margalef.airport: REU — Reus, ~1.5 h; BCN — Barcelona, ~2–2.5 h
famous_lines: First Round First Minute 9b — Chris Sharma, 2011
school_notes: Russian-speaking guides and coaches, based in a mountain house between Siurana and Margalef
Guides from the Explore-Share network
Guided group trips

rodellar.description: The Mascún canyon in the Sierra de Guara, with huge limestone arches and caves, is Spain's main summer sport climbing area. Shade in the deep canyon and a river for swimming offer relief from the heat, while tufa-covered overhangs provide powerful 7a–8c routes. There are few easy routes — beginners are usually taken to nearby Alquézar.
rodellar.rating_basis: One of Spain's best summer sport areas: 800+ routes in a scenic canyon with arches, strong overhanging 7a–8c lines; high ratings on PlanetMountain/Mountain Project
rodellar.hazards: Seasonal seepage on the tufas, loose rock in the canyon, river crossings, heat in July–August
rodellar.crowd_note: In July–August and over the May holidays the canyon is full of climbers and canyoneers, with queues on the Las Ventanas and El Camino classics
rodellar.region: Aragon, Huesca, Sierra y Cañones de Guara Natural Park, Mascún canyon
rodellar.season: late April to November; best May–June and September–October; in July–August people climb in the shade of the canyon, but it's hot and crowded; cold and wet in winter
rodellar.transfer: A car is needed: Zaragoza ~1–1.5 h, Barcelona ~2.5–3 h (≈270 km via Lleida, Monzón, Barbastro); the village is at the end of the road
rodellar.rock_note: orange-grey canyon limestone: steep overhangs, huge arches and caves, tufas, powerful endurance routes
rodellar.approach: ~10–30 min down into the canyon from the village; between sectors along the riverside path, fording the river in places
rodellar.restrictions: Climbing is regulated by a Guara Natural Park order (2015) because of nesting bearded vultures, Bonelli's eagles and Egyptian vultures: in the Mascún canyon and on most Alcanadre sport sectors climbing is allowed year-round, but the classic Peña Grau only from 1 August to 30 November; “quiet zones” are closed completely, and new sectors need the park's permission. Don't toprope directly through the anchors, and don't park where you block tractors
rodellar.guidebook: Rodellar Rock Climbing and Bouldering Guidebook; topo at Camping Mascún
rodellar.stay: Camping Mascún (at the trailhead, with a shop and restaurant) and El Puente with bungalows, Refugio Kalandraka, Albergue Las Almunias, Valle de Rodellar apartments; stock up on groceries in Huesca
pros: Shade in the canyon — climbable in summer
World-class overhanging endurance routes
Campgrounds right by the trail
A stunning canyon with a river
cons: Few easy routes
Tufas seep after a rainy winter and spring
Crowded and hot in summer
Car needed
rodellar.airport: ZAZ — Zaragoza, ~1–1.5 h; BCN — Barcelona, ~2.5–3 h; REU — Reus, ~1 h 45 min
school_notes: Local guiding office: climbing, via ferrata, canyoning
Guides and courses, including women's courses
Beginner courses

siurana.description: A village on the edge of a limestone plateau above a reservoir and one of the icons of Spanish sport climbing. Technical vertical walls with small holds, a huge choice of 6b–8b and the ultra-hard La Rambla 9a+ and La Capella 9b. Sunny in winter, hot in summer.
siurana.rating_basis: One of Spain's main sport areas: >1,700 routes, the legendary La Rambla 9a+ and Ondra's 9b, a convenient campground next to the crags; high ratings on UKC/theCrag
siurana.hazards: Drop-offs at the edge of the plateau along the paths, heat and sun, sharp rock; some routes have chipped holds
siurana.crowd_note: Busy at the peak of the season (October–November, Easter), but the sectors are spread out — it's easy to move to a neighbouring one
siurana.season: October–April; sunny south-facing walls in winter, shady sectors in May–June and September (El Pati, Can Codolar, Reserva India)
siurana.transfer: From Reus a taxi costs €40–50, or take the bus to Cornudella (a few times a day), then 10–15 min uphill; ~2 h by car from Barcelona
siurana.rock_note: compact orange-grey limestone: vertical to slightly overhanging, small edges and pockets, technical climbing with crux moves; walls up to 35–40 m
siurana.approach: all sectors are on foot from the village or campground, 5–30 min; 10–15 min by car from Cornudella
siurana.restrictions: Overnighting in campervans in the car parks and on the roadside is tolerated for now, but this may change — the official campground by the village is a better bet
siurana.guidebook: Siurana Climbing (more than 2,000 routes), local topos at the campground and in Cornudella's shops
siurana.stay: Camping Siurana by the village (tents, campervans, cabins for 4–6 people) — all sectors within walking distance; apartments and refugios in Cornudella de Montsant
pros: Huge volume of quality 6a–8c routes
Everything on foot from the campground
Sunny, stable weather in winter
Margalef, Montsant and Arras nearby — easy to combine
cons: Too hot in summer
Stiff technical grades
Hard to get to without a car
Fewer easy routes than 6b+ and up
siurana.airport: REU — Reus, ~45 min (flights mostly April to October); BCN — Barcelona, ~2 h
school_notes: A community of guides and coaches working in Russian, German, French, English and Czech
“Gym to crag” courses and coaching, gear and transfer from Reus/Tarragona
Guides covering the Tarragona areas

ceuse.description: A horseshoe of limestone walls at ~1,800–2,000 m above Gap — the summer mecca of sport climbing. Famous for its perfect pocketed rock, long (30–40 m) routes and spaced bolts, and for the Biographie sector, where the world's first 9a+ and 9b+ were climbed. There's plenty of quality 6a–6c, but its real fame lies at 7a and above.
ceuse.rating_basis: One of the world's best sport crags for rock quality; the legendary 9a+–9b+ lines of Sharma, Ondra and Megos; top ratings on 27crags/theCrag
ceuse.hazards: In early spring after a snowy winter, seepage and the risk of snow cornices falling from the ridge; long runouts between bolts; mountain thunderstorms in summer
ceuse.crowd_note: Busy on Berlin and the Biographie classics in July–August; Face de Rat and the more distant sectors are quieter
ceuse.season: late May to early October; best June–September
ceuse.transfer: A car is needed: ~25 min from Gap on the D19 via Sigoyer to the end of the road at Col des Guérins; train/bus to Gap or Tallard, then a taxi for €40–60
ceuse.rock_note: blue-grey pocketed limestone of the highest quality: pockets, vertical and overhanging, walls up to 130 m in a horseshoe around the summit
ceuse.approach: 45 min to 1 h 15 min uphill (≈500 m of ascent, 3 km) from the upper car park or the Les Guérins campground
ceuse.guidebook: Céüse (Rolland & Girousse, 2023), the 27crags app with Laurent Girousse's topos
ceuse.stay: Les Guérins campground right below the trail (season roughly mid-May to September), van parking at the Maison de Céüse, gîtes in Sigoyer; shops in Gap and Tallard
pros: World-class rock and long routes
Cool in summer thanks to the altitude
Campground right at the trailhead — doable without a car
Huge choice of 7a–8c
cons: Long, steep approach of ~1 h
Spaced bolts and stiff grades
Few easy routes for beginners
Short season, almost nothing to climb in bad weather
ceuse.airport: MRS — Marseille, ~2–2.5 h by car; GNB — Grenoble, ~2 h; also Nice and Turin

fontainebleau.description: A vast sandstone forest near Paris — the birthplace of modern bouldering. Thousands of boulders are grouped into colour-coded “circuits”, from children's yellow to black and white, so the area is equally good for beginners and for climbing 8A+. The main massifs: Bas Cuvier and Apremont, Franchard, Trois Pignons (95.2, Bois Rond, Canche aux Merciers), Éléphant, Buthiers.
fontainebleau.rating_basis: The world's most famous bouldering area: >30,000 problems, 100+ colour-coded circuits, a history going back to the 1940s; tops every ranking on 27crags/UKC
fontainebleau.hazards: Highballs with poor landings, ticks in the forest, damage to the fragile sandstone when climbing on it damp
fontainebleau.crowd_note: At weekends and at Easter the classics of Bas Cuvier, Apremont and Trois Pignons are packed with Parisians and Brits; on weekdays and at the more distant massifs it's quiet
fontainebleau.region: Île-de-France, Fontainebleau forest, ~70 km south of Paris
fontainebleau.season: year-round, except in heat and rain; best March–May and September–October; dry winter days give the best friction
fontainebleau.transfer: From Paris: train from Gare de Lyon to Fontainebleau-Avon or Bourron-Marlotte, ~40–60 min; from CDG about 2 h by RER B + train; for a trip longer than a couple of days you need a car — the massifs are scattered throughout the forest
fontainebleau.rock_note: fine-grained quartz sandstone: rounded “soap-bar” slopers, ledges, cracks and highballs among the sandy clearings of a pine forest
fontainebleau.approach: 2–20 min through the forest from the car parks; at Bas Cuvier the boulders are visible right from the parking; drive between massifs
fontainebleau.restrictions: Never climb on wet or damp sandstone — the rock crumbles, so wait for it to dry after rain; clean your shoes before every attempt, brush off chalk, don't make tick marks; carry crash pads rather than dragging them along the ground. The forest is managed by the ONF: wild camping and fires are prohibited, and some areas close during hunting — check the ONF website
fontainebleau.guidebook: Fontainebleau Climbs, Fontainebleau Fun Bloc, Fontainebleau Off Piste, Essential Fontainebleau (Stone Country); the bleau.info online database, 27crags
fontainebleau.stay: La Musardière campground near Milly-la-Forêt (close to Trois Pignons, open mid-February to November), FontaineblHostel & Camping, gîtes and Airbnbs in Bourron-Marlotte, Milly and Fontainebleau
pros: Endless problems at every grade
Ideal for beginners and families: colour-coded circuits, soft sandy ground
Easy to reach from Paris by train
Forest shade for warm days
cons: Rain stops climbing completely, and the sandstone needs time to dry
Distinctive friction technique and sandbagged grades
Crowds at weekends and at Easter
Car needed to get between massifs
fontainebleau.airport: ORY — Paris Orly, ~50 min by car; CDG — ~1.5 h
famous_lines: La Marie Rose 6A (Bas Cuvier) — the forest's first grade 6, 1946
school_notes: Certified guides, crash pads and transfer from the station; half a day from ~€47
Beginner sessions through the tourist office

gorges-du-tarn-jonte.description: Two neighbouring limestone canyons in the Causse du Larzac near Millau. The Tarn is famous for overhanging yellow-orange walls with long endurance routes — paradise for 7a and up, with few easy routes. The Jonte gorge near Le Rozier has vertical walls up to 150 m with multi-pitch routes and vultures circling close by.
gorges-du-tarn-jonte.rating_basis: The Tarn is a cult crag of the 1990s (Güllich, the Gymnaze and Baumes sectors) with long overhanging 7a–8c routes; the Jonte offers classic multi-pitch with vultures; high ratings on theCrag/PlanetMountain
gorges-du-tarn-jonte.hazards: Summer heat on south-facing walls, spaced bolts on some routes, loose rock, steep approaches; in the Jonte some routes require your own gear
gorges-du-tarn-jonte.crowd_note: In summer and over the May holidays the gorge is full of tourists and canoes, and the popular Tarn sectors can get busy; the Jonte is quieter
gorges-du-tarn-jonte.region: Occitanie, Lozère / Aveyron, Le Rozier — Les Vignes, ~20 km from Millau
gorges-du-tarn-jonte.season: April–October; best in spring and September–October; in summer, shady Tarn sectors in the morning/evening and swimming in the river
gorges-du-tarn-jonte.transfer: A car is essential: Montpellier — Millau ~1.5 h on the A75, then 20 min to Le Rozier; Toulouse ~3 h
gorges-du-tarn-jonte.rock_note: Tarn: yellow-orange dolomitic limestone with black and blue streaks — overhangs, bulges, endurance routes up to 70–80 m; Jonte: vertical walls up to 150 m with multi-pitch lines
gorges-du-tarn-jonte.approach: 5–15 min from the riverside road (the Tarn near Les Vignes, the Jonte from Le Rozier and Peyreleau), with steep paths in places
gorges-du-tarn-jonte.restrictions: The south side of the Jonte gorge is closed to climbing (vulture colonies); park only in designated places — sleeping in cars in the car parks is prohibited and the police patrol
gorges-du-tarn-jonte.guidebook: Gorges du Tarn et de la Jonte (local topo), Adrian Berry's “Gorges du Tarn” (2011), FFME Languedoc-Roussillon (2021)
gorges-du-tarn-jonte.stay: Campgrounds along the Tarn near Les Vignes and Le Rozier, gîtes in Le Rozier and Peyreleau; shops and rental in Millau
pros: World-class long overhanging 7a–8c routes
Short approaches from the road
Multi-pitches in the Jonte
A river for swimming on rest days
cons: Few routes below 6a
No sun at the bottom of the gorge in winter — cold
Stiff grades on the older routes
Car needed
gorges-du-tarn-jonte.airport: RDZ — Rodez, ~1.5 h; MPL — Montpellier, ~2 h
famous_lines: Les Femmes et les Grimpeurs d'Abord 5c (Les Vases, Jonte)
L'Air du Temps 6b, 6 pitches (Air du Temps, Jonte)
school_notes: Climbing and multi-pitch routes with an instructor
School at the entrance to the gorges
Climbing instructors
Climbing course (stage)

gorges-du-verdon.description: Europe's deepest canyon, with limestone walls up to 350 m — a legend of multi-pitch climbing. Most routes start with a rappel from the rim of the gorge, so the only way out is up. There are also short crags for learning near La Palud (Col d'Ayen, Félines, Petit Eycharme).
gorges-du-verdon.rating_basis: A European multi-pitch classic: walls up to 350 m above a turquoise river, hundreds of lines, historically the birthplace of French sport climbing; high ratings on theCrag/UKC
gorges-du-verdon.hazards: Rappelling in to the start of the route with no way down, thunderstorms and heat, stones knocked off the rim by tourists, old protection on some classic routes
gorges-du-verdon.crowd_note: In spring and September there can be parties queuing for the rappel on the Escalès classics; the learning crags are quiet
gorges-du-verdon.season: April–May and September–October; in summer climbers stick to walls in the shade in the afternoon
gorges-du-verdon.transfer: By car only: ~2.5 h from Nice or Marseille; the nearest towns are Castellane and Moustiers-Sainte-Marie
gorges-du-verdon.rock_note: compact grey canyon limestone: vertical walls of 100–350 m, “gouttes d'eau” pockets, slabs and cracks; you rappel in to the start of the routes from the rim of the gorge
gorges-du-verdon.approach: 5–15 min from the parking spots on the Route des Crêtes, then a rappel (often 2×45–50 m) to the start of the route — the only way back is up the route; you need double ropes and solid rappelling skills
gorges-du-verdon.restrictions: Griffon vulture colony and peregrine falcons: the Verdon Regional Nature Park publishes an annual list of “sensitive routes” (voies sensibles) that climbers are asked to avoid from January to the end of August (some from June to August): the Chasteuil, Encastel, Naziaque, Fenrir, Mayreste, Courchons sectors and others. This is a recommendation rather than law, but climbers respect it
gorges-du-verdon.guidebook: “Verdon” topos sold at the La Palud and Castellane tourist offices; theCrag database
gorges-du-verdon.stay: Municipal campground and guesthouses in La Palud-sur-Verdon (the village has a gear shop, a climbers' bar and a bakery), also Rougon and Moustiers-Sainte-Marie; book accommodation ahead in summer
pros: World-class multi-pitches with incredible exposure
Short approaches from the road along the canyon rim
La Palud, a climbers' village with a shop and campground
Wide choice from 5c to 8c
cons: Committing: you rappel in and the only retreat is up
Hot and full of tourists in summer, cold in winter
Some routes are sparsely bolted or need your own gear
Car needed
gorges-du-verdon.airport: NCE — Nice, ~2.5 h; MRS — Marseille, ~2.5 h
famous_lines: La Demande ~6a, 350 m, semi-trad (Escalès) — the first line on the Escalès
Ula ~300 m, trad, double rack of cams
school_notes: DEJEPS instructor, 5-day courses for groups of 3–5, March–October, gear included
Climbing courses and adventure programmes
Climbing with an instructor

chiatura-katskhi.description: The area around the mining town of Chiatura in Imereti is Georgia's main sport climbing area: the Katskhi crags (96 routes in 9 sectors, including a cave and a canyon), Sveri (63 routes) and a solid crag above the town itself (30 routes). Around 190 routes 5a–8b, more than half of them 6a+…7a. The famous Katskhi Pillar with a monastery on its summit is nearby.
chiatura-katskhi.rating_basis: Georgia's main sport area by number of routes and ascents on theCrag (~190 routes 5a–8b); theCrag calls Katskhi one of the best places in the country; minimal infrastructure
chiatura-katskhi.hazards: Summer heat, rockfall on new routes
chiatura-katskhi.crowd_note: Mostly local clubs from Tbilisi and Kutaisi climb here — usually empty
chiatura-katskhi.season: April–June and September–October; summers in Imereti are hot and humid, winters damp and cool
chiatura-katskhi.transfer: ~1.5 h by car from Kutaisi airport; ~180 km (~3.5 h) from Tbilisi
chiatura-katskhi.rock_note: solid limestone in the canyons around Chiatura: vertical, overhanging and a cave, routes of 12–23 m
chiatura-katskhi.approach: Short approaches from the road; the crag above Chiatura is reached by a steep road that a normal car can manage, with a small parking area
chiatura-katskhi.guidebook: No printed guidebook; topos on theCrag: Katskhi (96 routes, 9 sectors), Sveri (63), the crag above Chiatura (30)
chiatura-katskhi.stay: Guesthouses and apartments in Chiatura; pitching a tent by the crags is awkward, but you can sleep in your car
pros: Lots of grade 6 routes on good limestone
Empty and inexpensive
Close to Kutaisi airport, delicious food
cons: No printed guidebook or infrastructure
Few hard routes
Hot, humid summers
chiatura-katskhi.airport: KUT — Kutaisi, ~1.5 h; TBS — Tbilisi, ~3.5 h

kalymnos.description: Kalymnos is an island in the Dodecanese and probably the world's most popular place to combine sport climbing with a seaside holiday. Some 4,000+ routes on 99 crags, from slabs to grottos with stalactites and tufas, almost all within a 20–35-minute walk of Masouri. There are also multi-pitches of up to 11 pitches on Telendos, and DWS.
kalymnos.rating_basis: One of the world's most popular sport climbing areas: 4,000+ routes on 99 crags, an international climbing festival, and five-star reviews across the board
kalymnos.hazards: Heat and sun, sharp tufas and stalactites, rockfall below the grottos, goats above the crags knocking down stones, scooter riding
kalymnos.crowd_note: In October (festival) and May there are queues on the classics at the Grande Grotta and the sectors around Masouri; the more distant sectors and Telendos are quieter
kalymnos.season: Year-round except the hot summer; best September–November and March to early June
kalymnos.transfer: Fly to Kos, take a 10-min taxi to Mastichari port and a 25–30-min ferry to Pothia; there are also Athens — Kalymnos flights and ferries from Piraeus (9–14 h) and Rhodes
kalymnos.rock_note: grey and orange limestone: tufas, stalactites, huge grottos and overhangs, as well as slabs and pocketed walls
kalymnos.approach: 20–35 min on foot from Masouri to most sectors; the north (Arginonta, Skalia, Emporios) by scooter; Telendos is a 10-min boat ride from Myrties
kalymnos.restrictions: No paid permits; proceeds from the local guidebook go to the rebolting fund. Wild camping on the island is prohibited
kalymnos.guidebook: Kalymnos Rock Climbing (Aris Theodoropoulos, Katie Roussou), 2023–2025 editions, with an app; also the Rockfax guide (~2,300 routes) and topos on 27crags
kalymnos.stay: Studios and apartments in Masouri, Armeos and Myrties right below the crags; book ahead for May and October; you'll need a scooter for the more distant sectors
pros: Huge choice of routes at every grade, excellent bolting
Crags close to your accommodation and the sea
The grottos are an option on rainy days
Warm winter, climbable almost year-round
cons: Hot summers
Queues on the classics in high season
Scooter needed for the more distant sectors
Sharp limestone
kalymnos.airport: KGS — Kos, ~1–1.5 h including the ferry; JKL — Kalymnos (flights from Athens)
school_notes: Platform for certified guides: lead climbing courses and multi-pitches
Multi-pitch courses with local instructors
Private guides, coaching, DWS

leonidio.description: Leonidio is a small town in the eastern Peloponnese surrounded by red limestone cliffs; in 10 years it has become one of Europe's best winter sport climbing areas. About 2,700 routes in 111 sectors, from slabs to tufa-covered overhangs, plus multi-pitches in the canyon; the sea is close by, as is another area, Kyparissi (~1 h).
leonidio.rating_basis: One of Europe's main winter sport areas (8a.nu: “the winter capital of the future”), 2,700+ routes, an annual festival, glowing reviews from the BMC and UKC
leonidio.hazards: Sharp limestone, stones dislodged by goats above the crags, heat on south-facing walls in spring, winding mountain roads
leonidio.crowd_note: Busy at popular sectors near town at Christmas, in November and at Easter, but with so many sectors there are few queues
leonidio.season: October–April; peak from mid-October to early January, and spring is good too; hot from mid-May to September
leonidio.transfer: ~3.5 h by car from Athens airport (toll motorway, then a winding mountain road along the coast); bus from Athens ~4 h; Kalamata airport is closer but has fewer flights
leonidio.rock_note: red and grey limestone: tufas and overhangs, technical walls on small holds, multi-pitch walls in the canyon
leonidio.approach: A couple of minutes to the roadside sectors (Sabaton, Montanejos); 10–30 min uphill to most others; some sectors require a car
leonidio.restrictions: No permits or fees; climbing is supported by the Pánjika cooperative (guidebook proceeds go to route maintenance). Please use the free municipal toilets
leonidio.guidebook: Leonidio & Kyparissi (Pánjika cooperative), 5th edition 2026: 2,673 single-pitch and 49 multi-pitch routes in 111 sectors; topos also on 27crags and theCrag
leonidio.stay: Apartments and guesthouses in Leonidio and Plaka; a large beach campground ~5 km away (Camping Semeli)
pros: Sunny south-facing sectors — excellent in winter
Wide choice of grade 6–7 routes, good bolting
Lively town, sea, campground
Kyparissi nearby
cons: Too hot in summer
Car needed for some sectors
Long drive from Athens
leonidio.airport: ATH — Athens, ~3.5 h by car; KLX — Kalamata

5-day beginner climbing course in Greece

meteora.description: Meteora is a group of conglomerate towers up to 300 m high, crowned with monasteries (UNESCO). About 900 multi-pitch routes put up in the Saxon Switzerland tradition: sparse ring bolts, runouts, and slings threaded around “pebbles” for protection. Nearby are the sport areas of Theopetra, Pyli and Mouzaki and the Rizoma bouldering.
meteora.rating_basis: Unique conglomerate towers with monasteries (UNESCO), ~900 multi-pitch routes up to 285 m; but the sparse ring bolts and runouts on pebbles put off sport climbers
meteora.hazards: Long runouts, pebbles popping off, confusion when rappelling from single ring bolts, heat
meteora.crowd_note: Lots of tourists at the monasteries, but the routes are usually free
meteora.season: April to mid-June and mid-September to November; possible on sunny winter days, very hot in summer
meteora.transfer: ~360 km from Athens (train or bus to Kalambaka, ~4–5 h), ~230 km from Thessaloniki; the nearest city is Larissa; Kastraki is 2 km from Kalambaka
meteora.rock_note: conglomerate: towers up to 300 m high with “pebbles” instead of holds; slabs and vertical faces, technical rather than powerful climbing
meteora.approach: 5–30 min from Kastraki and the roads between the towers; descent by rappelling from ring bolts
meteora.restrictions: UNESCO site. Climbing is forbidden on the six towers with active monasteries (an agreement dating from the 1970s); no adding bolts to the classics; overnight stays, fires and camping between the towers are prohibited. No permits or fees; wear modest clothing to visit the monasteries
meteora.guidebook: Meteora – Climbing and Hiking (Hasse, Stutte; ~230 routes) and its 2000 supplement; Meteora Sport Climbing Guide (Vangelis Bastios, 2022) — sport in Meteora, Theopetra, Sarakina; the selections Best of the Classics (206 routes) and Rock Around the World
meteora.stay: Vrachos and Kastraki campgrounds in Kastraki village, guesthouses in Kastraki and Kalambaka
pros: Unique scenery and atmosphere
Long grade 5–6 routes
Campgrounds right below the towers
No fees
cons: Sparse protection — experience and trad gear needed
Hot in summer
Wet conglomerate is slippery; the “monastery” towers are off-limits
meteora.airport: SKG — Thessaloniki, ~3 h; ATH — Athens, ~4 h

paklenica.description: Paklenica is a national park on the slopes of Velebit above the Adriatic and Croatia's main climbing area. About 600 marked routes: short sport routes in the Klanci canyon section and long multi-pitches up to 350 m on Anića kuk, Veliki Čuk and Debeli kuk. A mix of sport, “big wall” and the sea 10 minutes away.
paklenica.rating_basis: Croatia's main climbing area: ~600 equipped routes from 3 to 8b+, multi-pitches up to 350 m on Anića kuk, an international climbers' meeting in early May
paklenica.hazards: Rockfall on the big walls, old pitons, heat and snakes in summer, the strong bora wind
paklenica.crowd_note: Crowded in Klanci over the May holidays (the international climbers' meeting) and in summer; the big walls are quieter
paklenica.season: April to late October; hot in summer, but there's plenty of shade in the canyon; in winter the sunny Crljenica is possible, though the bora can blow
paklenica.transfer: Zadar airport is ~45 km away (taxi, rental car or bus to Starigrad); ~2 h from Split
paklenica.rock_note: karst limestone of the Velika Paklenica canyon: short sport routes in Klanci and walls up to 350 m (Anića kuk), old routes on pitons and new ones on bolts
paklenica.approach: The Klanci sector is 5 min from the parking at the canyon entrance; 30–60 min along the trail to Anića kuk and the other big walls
paklenica.restrictions: National park: paid entry (1-, 3- and 5-day and annual tickets; climbing is included in the ticket). Climbing is allowed only in the Velika Paklenica canyon (forbidden in Mala Paklenica); soloing is forbidden and helmets are mandatory; new routes only with the park's permission; some routes close for nesting; camping in the park is prohibited
paklenica.guidebook: Paklenica Climbing Guide (2026 edition); topos on theCrag and 27crags (~1,200 routes including neighbouring areas)
paklenica.stay: Campgrounds and apartments in Starigrad-Paklenica by the park entrance; three mountain huts in the hills

Shade in the canyon in summer
Lots of routes for beginners
Rescuers on duty in summer

hampi.description: Hampi is the ruins of a medieval capital amid endless granite boulders on the banks of the Tungabhadra. A winter bouldering classic: more than a thousand problems from easy to 8A, cheap living in guesthouses among rice paddies and palm trees, and crash pad rental for next to nothing.
hampi.rating_basis: One of the world's largest boulder fields (UKC): 1,400+ problems in the guidebook, 700+ according to PlanetMountain, a unique landscape with the ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire
hampi.hazards: Heat, sharp granite, stomach bugs (don't drink tap water), stray dogs, monkeys and bats (rabies risk), snakes and scorpions under the boulders
hampi.crowd_note: In season a couple of hundred climbers live on the island, but there are enough boulders for everyone
hampi.season: November–February; best December–January (cool and dry); from March the heat approaches 40°, and June to September is monsoon
hampi.transfer: Fly to Bangalore, take an overnight train or bus to Hospet (~7 h), a 20–30-min rickshaw ride and a boat to the island; ~8–9 h by bus from Goa
hampi.rock_note: orange granite of ancient boulder fields: sharp small holds, friction; by the river, water-polished grey granite
hampi.approach: Most boulders are 5–20 min on foot from the Hampi Island (Virupapur Gaddi) guesthouses; cross the river by boat
hampi.restrictions: Hampi is a UNESCO site: don't climb on temples or monuments; some guesthouses have been demolished under the monument protection plan, and accommodation is shifting to Hospet and the villages; some boulders are on private land; alcohol is officially banned
hampi.stay: Simple guesthouses and huts on Hampi Island (Virupapur Gaddi), hotels in Hampi Bazaar and Hospet; prices shoot up at Christmas and New Year
pros: A huge number of boulders within walking distance
Very cheap
Unique scenery with UNESCO temples
Easy to combine with Goa
cons: Short season: hot even in November and February
Sharp rock — hard on the skin
Accommodation uncertainty due to guesthouse demolitions

hampi.airport: BLR — Bangalore, ~7 h; GOI — Goa, ~8 h

arco.description: A small town at the northern tip of Lake Garda — one of the hubs of European climbing and the birthplace of the Rock Master competition. Thousands of sport routes on well over a hundred crags, from practice slabs to 9b, plus the big multi-pitch walls of the Sarca valley. The mild climate makes climbing possible almost all year round.
arco.rating_basis: The cradle of Italian sport climbing and home of Rock Master: >5,000 routes on 130+ crags and the big walls of the Sarca valley, all close to Lake Garda (PlanetMountain, Climb Europe, theCrag)
arco.hazards: Rockfall on the big walls, polish, summer heat, mountain thunderstorms
arco.crowd_note: Very busy at Easter and on public holidays (Germans, Austrians, Italians), and the Massone classics are polished; the more distant crags are quieter
arco.region: Trentino, northern shore of Lake Garda, Sarca valley
arco.season: March–May and September–November; in winter, south-facing walls on calm days; in summer, shady and higher sectors, plus the Ora wind in the afternoon
arco.transfer: Verona ~1 h 15 min by car (≈80 km), Bergamo ~2 h; buses from Rovereto/Trento; a car is advisable
arco.rock_note: grey and orange limestone of the Sarca valley: slabs, vertical walls and overhangs on 130+ sport crags, and the big walls of Monte Brento and Monte Casale up to 1,000–1,400 m
arco.approach: most sport crags are 2–20 min from the road, or reachable on foot/by bike from Arco; the big walls involve mountain approaches of 1 h or more
arco.restrictions: Many crags are on private land — conflicts with landowners and closures do happen; respect local bans and access restrictions; parking at Massone is limited — better to walk or cycle
arco.guidebook: Arco Rock (6,000 routes, 139 crags), Arco Pareti / sport climbing guide (~4,400 routes, 131 crags)
arco.stay: Hotels, apartments, B&Bs and campgrounds in Arco and Riva del Garda; the town has dozens of gear shops

Sport, multi-pitch and big walls in one place
Mild winters and lots of schools
A town with infrastructure and a lake for rest days

finale-ligure.description: Hills above the Italian Riviera with dozens of limestone crags among woods and olive groves — Italy's classic winter area. Around 4,000 sport routes from 3a to 8c+, mostly 6a–7a, with technical climbing on small pockets. On rest days there's the sea, medieval Finalborgo and mountain biking.
finale-ligure.rating_basis: One of Italy's oldest and largest sport climbing areas: ~4,000 routes, technical pocketed limestone, a winter season by the sea; Climb Europe, Mountain Project, PlanetMountain
finale-ligure.hazards: Polish, northerly wind in winter, sectors closed for nesting — fines apply
finale-ligure.crowd_note: On holidays and weekends Monte Cucco and Rocca di Corno are popular and the classics are polished; there are so many crags that you can always find a quiet spot
finale-ligure.region: Liguria, province of Savona, Italian Riviera (Finalborgo)
finale-ligure.season: October–May; in winter, south-facing sectors by the sea sheltered from the northerly wind; in spring and autumn, everything; hot and crowded in summer
finale-ligure.transfer: Genoa ~45 min–1 h on the A10; Nice ~1.5–2 h; train to Finale Ligure Marina station; you need a car or scooter for the crags
finale-ligure.rock_note: “pietra di Finale” — pale, porous reef limestone: small pockets, edges, technical vertical climbing; routes are usually 20–30 m, the Bric Pianarella wall up to 250 m
finale-ligure.approach: 5–30 min along forest trails from the parking in the Aquila, Ponci and Perti valleys; the crags are spread over ~10 km², so you need a car or scooter
finale-ligure.restrictions: Protection of peregrine falcons and eagle owls: parts of Caprazoppa (from the relay mast down to the sea by Torre Colombara), Pianarella (beyond the “Via Lunga”), Casa delle Vacche, Rocca di Corno (beyond the route “Il Futuro è un'Ipotesi”) and the whole of Capo Noli above the Via Aurelia are closed year-round; Monte Tolla, Bric Reseghe, Rocca degli Uccelli and the right and central sectors of the Bastionata di Boragni are closed from 1 January to 31 July
finale-ligure.guidebook: Finale Climbing (Versante Sud, 2022, in English), about 4,000 routes in 213 sectors
finale-ligure.stay: Campgrounds and apartments in Finalborgo and Finale Marina, agriturismi in the valleys; Finalborgo has gear shops and climbers' bars

Beginner course, May–June

sardinia-cala-gonone.description: The limestone coast of the Gulf of Orosei, with crags right above the beaches — a classic winter destination. Cala Gonone has more than 700 routes, from beginner slabs to the Millennium cave with tufas up to 8c+, while further south in Ogliastra there are the multi-pitches of Punta Giradili and the Goloritzé spire, plus more than 1,200 routes at Ulassai and Jerzu.
sardinia-cala-gonone.rating_basis: One of the best winter areas in the Mediterranean: limestone above a turquoise sea, the Millennium cave, the classic multi-pitches of Goloritzé and Giradili; Climb Europe, UKC, PlanetMountain
sardinia-cala-gonone.hazards: Rusty protection on some of the older routes by the sea (Cala Luna), rappel anchors hard to find on Grotta dei Colombi, cold mistral wind on the multi-pitches
sardinia-cala-gonone.crowd_note: Few people in winter; the Biddiriscottai and Buchi Arta classics are popular over holidays; in summer the beaches are packed with tourists
sardinia-cala-gonone.region: Sardinia, Dorgali (Cala Gonone), Gulf of Orosei; further south — Baunei, Ulassai, Jerzu
sardinia-cala-gonone.season: October–May; 13–20 °C by the sea in winter, best November–April; too hot and touristy in summer
sardinia-cala-gonone.transfer: A car is needed: Olbia ~1.5–2 h via the SS131 DCN and SS125; Cagliari ~3 h; Alghero ~2.5–3 h; ~1 h on a mountain road from Cala Gonone to Baunei
sardinia-cala-gonone.rock_note: white and grey limestone by the sea: caves with tufas (Millennium), slabs and walls above the Cala Fuili and Cala Luna beaches, multi-pitch walls of 200–400 m (Grotta dei Colombi, Punta Giradili, the Goloritzé spire)
sardinia-cala-gonone.approach: from 5 min (Buchi Arta) to 30–60 min along coastal trails to the beach sectors; the Millennium cave has a via ferrata-style approach; some sectors can be reached by boat
sardinia-cala-gonone.guidebook: Rock Climbing in Cala Gonone (Corrado Conca, 2025, >700 routes in 9 areas); online topos at climbingitaly.com
sardinia-cala-gonone.stay: Apartments and hotels in Cala Gonone and Dorgali (much is closed in winter, but accommodation is cheap), a climbers' house in Lotzorai, apartments in Baunei and Arbatax
pros: Climbing above the sea and beaches
Mild winters
World-class seaside multi-pitches
Few people outside summer
cons: Some shops and restaurants close in winter
The scirocco makes the caves damp and slippery
Far from airports, car needed
Too hot in summer
sardinia-cala-gonone.airport: OLB — Olbia, ~1.5–2 h; CAG — Cagliari, ~3 h
famous_lines: Millennium cave 6a–8c+ — tufas on a par with Kalymnos's Grande Grotta
Wolfgang Güllich 7a (6b obl.), 400 m (Punta Giradili, Baunei)
school_notes: Guides for sport and multi-pitch routes

wadi-rum.description: Wadi Rum is a UNESCO-listed desert in southern Jordan with sandstone massifs up to 500 m high. About 350 routes, mostly trad and long 5–6b multi-pitches up cracks, many of them following old Bedouin paths; sport routes can be counted on one hand. This is adventure climbing: long approaches, rappel descents, nights in the desert.
wadi-rum.rating_basis: A legendary adventure climbing area: walls up to 500 m in a UNESCO desert, Tony Howard's 1980s classics; few bolted routes for sport climbers
wadi-rum.hazards: Loose rock and fragile holds, sun-bleached slings at the anchors, sand that wears through ropes, flash floods, heat and dehydration, cold nights in winter
wadi-rum.crowd_note: Lots of jeep tourists, few climbers — the routes are usually deserted
wadi-rum.region: Wadi Rum Protected Area (UNESCO), southern Jordan
wadi-rum.season: October–May; best in November and March–April; too hot in summer (+40 °C)
wadi-rum.transfer: 40–50 min by taxi from Aqaba (20–40 JD); 3–4 h from Amman (80–110 JD); buses run twice a day from Aqaba and Amman to the Rest House
wadi-rum.rock_note: sandstone desert massifs up to 500 m high: long crack systems and chimneys, with fragile and crumbly rock in places
wadi-rum.approach: 15–60 min on foot from Rum village to the Jebel Rum walls; the more distant massifs (Burdah, Barrah, Nassrani) by Bedouin jeep
wadi-rum.restrictions: Entry to the protected area costs 5 JD per person (free with the Jordan Pass). Tourists may not drive around the desert on their own — for the more distant walls you need a local Bedouin guide / driver. Wet sandstone is fragile: once the surface has dried, wait another day. There are almost no bolts; trad ethics
wadi-rum.guidebook: Treks and Climbs in Wadi Rum (Tony Howard, Cicerone, 4th ed. 2007, out of print; ~350 routes); Thierry Souchard's 2017 selected guide (180 multi-pitches) and a digital topo on OmegaRoc
wadi-rum.stay: Camping by the Rest House in Rum village (~2 JD with your own tent), Bedouin homes in the village (15–25 JD with dinner and breakfast) and desert camps (~50 JD with meals and transfer)
pros: Long trad routes in fantastic scenery
Empty walls
Bedouin hospitality, Petra nearby
cons: Almost no bolts — trad experience and gear needed
Fragile sandstone, no climbing after rain
A guide-driver needed for the more distant walls
Hot summers
wadi-rum.airport: AQJ — Aqaba, ~50 min; AMM — Amman, ~4 h

ogawayama.description: Ogawayama is a granite area in a pine forest at around 1,500–1,700 m and the birthplace of Japanese free climbing in the early 1980s. It's known for cracks and friction slabs (trad and multi-pitch) and one of the best boulder fields in Japan. The domes of Mizugaki-yama, with long multi-pitches, are nearby.
ogawayama.rating_basis: Japan's most popular climbing area and the birthplace of Japanese free climbing (Mountain Project): granite cracks, slabs and 21 bouldering sectors, with strong problems up to 5 dan
ogawayama.hazards: Unreliable old pitons on trad routes, falls on slabs, summer thunderstorms, bears and ticks in the forest
ogawayama.crowd_note: Lots of Japanese climbers at weekends and on holidays (Golden Week in early May); quiet on weekdays
ogawayama.season: April–November; best in May and September–October; June is the rainy season (tsuyu), frost and snow from December to March
ogawayama.transfer: ~3–4 h by car from Tokyo on the Chūō Expressway; or train to Shinano-Kawakami station (Koumi Line) and a taxi
ogawayama.rock_note: pale granite in a pine forest: cracks, friction slabs, pocketed boulders; the “Japanese Yosemite”
ogawayama.approach: All 21 bouldering sectors are within walking distance of the Mawarime-daira campground: 5–40 min through the forest
ogawayama.restrictions: Mawarime-daira campground is open from late April to early November (entry ¥700 per day + ¥1,300 per night in a tent); book ryokan in advance; trad routes need your own gear; cash is essential. The neighbouring granite massif is Mizugaki-yama (Yamanashi): multi-pitches on domes, cracks, sport and bouldering
ogawayama.guidebook: Ogawayama Bouldering Area Guide (2020); Ogawayama, Mitake, Mitsumine (Tokio Muroi); Nihon no Iwaba No. 3 (Kitayama Makoto) for routes; the books are in Japanese and sold at the Ogawayama shop
ogawayama.stay: Campground and bungalows in the Mawarime-daira meadow at the foot of the crags (late April to early November), ryokan
pros: Classic granite: cracks, slabs and bouldering in one place
Cool in summer thanks to the altitude
Campground right by the rock
cons: Japanese grades (kyu/dan) and harsh grading
Rainy season in June, snow in winter
Hard to reach without a car
Guidebooks in Japanese
ogawayama.airport: HND / NRT — Tokyo, 3–5 h by car

ak-suu-karavshin.description: The Ak-Suu and Kara-Suu (Karavshin) valleys in the Turkestan Range are a legendary big-wall granite area, the “Patagonia of Asia”. Asan and Usen peaks, the Russian Tower, Peak 4810 and the north face of Ak-Suu (5,217 m) offer routes of 400 to 1,400 m — from free climbing at 6c–8a+ to Russian grade 6B. For experienced climbers only: expedition logistics, a border zone and no infrastructure whatsoever.
ak-suu-karavshin.rating_basis: One of the world's best big-wall granite areas (the “Patagonia of Asia”): routes up to 1,400 m, a classic venue of Russian mountaineering championships and international expeditions
ak-suu-karavshin.hazards: Rockfall and ice in the afternoon, thunderstorms and hail, altitude, remoteness from help, border zone
ak-suu-karavshin.crowd_note: Only a few expeditions come each season — the walls are almost always empty
ak-suu-karavshin.region: Batken Region, Turkestan Range (Pamir-Alay), Ak-Suu and Kara-Suu valleys
ak-suu-karavshin.season: Mid-June to September; best July–August; more precipitation in autumn, and the area is inaccessible in winter
ak-suu-karavshin.transfer: Fly to Bishkek, then on to Osh or Batken; drive to Vorukh (Karavshin) or Uzgurush / Katran (Lyailyak), then a day on foot with horses or donkeys; a helicopter drop-off is possible
ak-suu-karavshin.rock_note: monolithic granite of the “Patagonia of Asia”: walls of 400–1,400 m, cracks and dihedrals, with ice and rockfall up high
ak-suu-karavshin.approach: A day on foot or on horseback to base camp from Vorukh (Karavshin) or Katran / Uzgurush (Lyailyak), or a helicopter from Osh or Batken; 2–3 h from base camp to the walls
ak-suu-karavshin.restrictions: Border zone near the Tajik and Uzbek borders: a border permit is required (~$40 for a month, takes about a month to arrange, insurance required); there's a military checkpoint at the valley entrance. The route to Karavshin passes through the Tajik enclave of Vorukh — a Tajik visa may be needed
ak-suu-karavshin.guidebook: No guidebook: topos in reports in the Alpine Journal, the American Alpine Journal, alpinemag.fr and in descriptions from the Mountaineering Federation of Russia; routes are graded on both the French scale and the Russian one (5A–6B)
ak-suu-karavshin.stay: Tented base camps only (Kara-Suu, Ak-Suu, ~3,000 m); agencies in Osh and Bishkek rent out camp tents, gas, generators and satellite phones
pros: Huge world-class granite walls
Almost nobody around
A summer season, when the Mediterranean is too hot
cons: Expedition logistics and a border permit
No infrastructure or rescue services
Rockfall, ice and thunderstorms at altitude
ak-suu-karavshin.airport: OSS — Osh, or Batken; 1–2 days to base camp
famous_lines: Perestroika Crack 7a+, 800 m (Russian Tower / Peak Slesov, Ak-Su)
North face of Ak-Suu, Shabalin's “Nose” 6B, ~1,400 m
school_notes: Bishkek agency: border permit, transport, camp, guides, gear rental

thakhek.description: Jungle, rice paddies and karst towers 12 km from the town of Thakhek. All the climbing has grown up around the Green Climbers Home camp: 600+ sport routes in 50 sectors, many just minutes from the bungalows. Steep limestone with tufas and pockets, a good choice of 6a–7b and the overhanging cave of The Roof.
thakhek.rating_basis: UKC calls Thakhek the best sport climbing area in Southeast Asia: 600+ routes (camp figures), 51 sectors (Mountain Project), crags minutes from the camp
thakhek.hazards: Snakes, scorpions and insects in the jungle, dogs in town (rabies risk), heat; serious medical care is available only in Thailand
thakhek.crowd_note: December–January are the busiest months and the camp can be full; November and February are quieter
thakhek.season: October–April (the camp is open from October to May); best November–February; monsoon in summer, camp closed
thakhek.transfer: Fly Bangkok — Nakhon Phanom, bus across the Friendship Bridge to Thakhek (~1.5 h), then a taxi ~12 km to the camp; buses also run from Vientiane
thakhek.rock_note: steep karst limestone: pockets, tufas, huecos; the overhanging cave of The Roof
thakhek.approach: Most sectors are 0–10 min from the camp; the distant Phantasia sector is about 30 min
thakhek.restrictions: Climbing is organised around the Green Climbers Home camp: the guidebook is sold at the camp and proceeds go to the bolt fund; respect the local villages and rice paddies
thakhek.guidebook: Green Climbers Home guidebook, sold at the camp (~USD 16–20)
thakhek.stay: Green Climbers Home camp (two camps): bungalows, tents with bedding, kitchen and bar; book ahead for December–January
pros: Crags minutes from the camp
Cheap, everything included at the camp
Courses and rental on site
Varied aspects — you can almost always find shade
cons: Season limited by the camp's opening (October–May)
Heat in March–April
Remote, basic medical care
thakhek.airport: KOP — Nakhon Phanom (Thailand), ~2 h including the border; VTE — Vientiane, ~5–6 h
famous_lines: L4 One of the Best 7a (Open All Hours)
school_notes: Climbers' camp: courses from beginner to lead climbing, rental of ropes, quickdraws and shoes

taghia.description: Taghia is a Berber village deep in the High Atlas, surrounded by limestone walls up to 800–900 m high. One of the world's best areas for long sport multi-pitches: dozens of bolted routes 6b–8a on compact rock, many of them 300–600 m long. There are no roads — just a trail and mules, and life in simple gîtes.
taghia.rating_basis: A cult area for bolted big walls: walls up to 800–900 m, modern bolted routes up to 8a (ClimbingAway); Alex Honnold free soloed Les Rivières Pourpres; the downside is the complicated logistics
taghia.hazards: Flash floods in narrow canyons, rockfall with runoff from the plateau, evening thunderstorms, cold on the walls, stomach bugs; no rescue service
taghia.crowd_note: In spring and autumn a few dozen climbers stay in the gîtes, but there are plenty of routes — no queues
taghia.region: Béni Mellal-Khénifra, Central High Atlas, Zaouiat Ahansal
taghia.season: April–May and September–October; in summer you can climb on shady walls; cold from November to March, with occasional snow
taghia.transfer: From Marrakech to Zaouiat Ahansal 5–6 h by 4×4 taxi (or 9–10 h on two buses via Azilal), then ~2 h on foot with mules
taghia.rock_note: compact grey and orange limestone on big walls of 200–900 m with no ledges or vegetation; long, continuous pitches
taghia.approach: No road to the village: ~2 h on foot from Zaouiat Ahansal (mules carry the gear); from the village to the walls is 15 min to 2.5 h uphill
taghia.restrictions: No permits. A remote area with no road and no mountain rescue — you need to be fully self-sufficient on multi-pitches and descents; respect the ways of the Berber village (clothing, photos); always treat your water
taghia.guidebook: Taghia — Montagnes Berbères (Christian Ravier, in French); handwritten topos of new routes are kept at Said's gîte
taghia.stay: Two gîtes in the village (Said Messaoudi's Gîte Tawjdat and Youssef's Maison de Taghia) — half board, hot water and electricity
pros: Walls up to 800 m with modern bolting
Compact rock without ledges
An authentic Berber village
Few people
cons: Complicated logistics and long approaches
Almost no routes for beginners
No rescue service
Stomach bugs
taghia.airport: RAK — Marrakech, ~8 h including the walk-in
famous_lines: Les Rivières Pourpres 7b+ (600 m, Petit / Piola / Robert)
school_notes: Guided trips to the Taghia multi-pitches (9 days)

todra-gorge.description: Todra is a narrow canyon with sheer walls up to 300 m on the southern slopes of the High Atlas, near the Tinghir oasis. Sport routes from 4b to 8c and endless limestone multi-pitches right from the road, with hotels at the foot of the walls. A good option in spring, autumn and on sunny winter days.
todra-gorge.rating_basis: Morocco's best-known climbing area: ~350 routes 4b–8c (ClimbingAway), multi-pitches up to 350 m in a scenic canyon; downsides are the uneven fixed gear and tourists by the sectors
todra-gorge.hazards: Rockfall from the walls, unreliable anchors on old routes, flash floods and a washed-out road after downpours, no mountain rescue and no phone signal
todra-gorge.crowd_note: Few climbers; by day the gorge entrance is crowded with tourists and souvenir sellers
todra-gorge.region: Drâa-Tafilalet, Tinghir, southern slopes of the High Atlas
todra-gorge.season: March–June and September–November; in winter you can climb on sunny walls (~15° by day, frost at night); July–August is scorching
todra-gorge.transfer: Fly to Ouarzazate, then ~3 h by car; ~7 h from Marrakech across the Atlas (or a bus to Tinghir and a 15 km taxi ride)
todra-gorge.rock_note: grey and orange limestone on the canyon's sheer walls up to 300 m: vertical faces, friction slabs, pockets
todra-gorge.approach: Sectors along the road in the gorge: 1–15 min from the car or hotel; Pieds dans l'Eau requires wading across the river
todra-gorge.restrictions: No permits; the two sectors at the gorge entrance are busy with tourists and vendors during the day — climb in the morning or towards evening. Not all routes have chained anchors; Morocco has no mountain rescue service; floods wash out the road into the gorge
todra-gorge.guidebook: Todra — Rock Climbing in Morocco's Todra Gorge (Oxford Alpine Club / Cordee, 5th ed.); a local printed guide from 2014 (Tizgui); digital topo in the ClimbingAway app
todra-gorge.stay: Hotels and hostels in Tizgui village and right in the gorge (Hotel Yasmina, Mansour, La Vallée), campsites on the road to the gorge; for more comfort, kasbahs in Tinghir
pros: Long bolted multi-pitches
Approach — minutes from your hotel
Cheap, a colourful Berber oasis
Climbable in winter too
cons: Inconsistent fixed gear and anchors
Tourists and vendors by the main sectors
Very hot in summer
No rescue service or phone signal in the gorge
todra-gorge.airport: OZZ — Ouarzazate, ~3 h; ERH — Errachidia, ~2.5 h; RAK — Marrakech, ~7 h
famous_lines: Vol de Défilé 6a (Aiguille du Gué, 4 pitches)
school_notes: Local guides, gear rental and sales, route rebolting in agreement with the authorities

tsaranoro.description: Tsaranoro is a set of granite walls up to 800 m high above a valley by the Andringitra massif in southern Madagascar. Some of the world's hardest multi-pitch routes have been climbed here (Mora Mora 8c), but there are also 6b–7a classics such as Out of Africa. Camp Catta sits right below the walls, surrounded by ring-tailed lemurs and Betsileo villages.
tsaranoro.rating_basis: One of the world's best granite big-wall areas (UKC, PlanetMountain): walls up to 800 m, bolted multi-pitches from 6a to 8c (Mora Mora, Adam Ondra); 50–100 routes (ClimbingAway)
tsaranoro.hazards: Long walls and descents in the dark, heat on sunny slabs, cold on the summits in July, stomach bugs, no rescue service
tsaranoro.crowd_note: Only a handful of climbers even in September — the walls are empty
tsaranoro.region: Haute Matsiatra, Tsaranoro valley by the Andringitra massif, Ambalavao
tsaranoro.season: May–October (dry season); September and early October are the most popular, while July is cold on the summits; November to March brings heat and rain
tsaranoro.transfer: Fly to Antananarivo, then a full day on the road via Fianarantsoa and Ambalavao (the last stretch is a dirt track by 4×4); the camps arrange transfers
tsaranoro.rock_note: compact big-wall granite up to 800 m: slabs and vertical faces on small edges, almost no natural protection — routes are bolted ground-up
tsaranoro.approach: 30 min to 1.5 h uphill on foot from Camp Catta below the walls; the road from Ambalavao is a dirt track, with the last part by 4×4
tsaranoro.restrictions: A remote area with no rescue service — complete self-sufficiency on the big walls, early starts (or you'll be spending the night on the wall); new routes require your own bolts and ground-up bolting skills on lead; respect local customs and taboos (fady); treat your water
tsaranoro.guidebook: Route topos are kept at Camp Catta; there is no separate modern guidebook — topos on theCrag
tsaranoro.stay: Camp Catta right below the walls (tents, bungalows, bar) or Tsaranoro Camp; basic camping in the village
pros: World-class granite big walls
Empty walls, no queues
Camp right below the walls
Lemurs and the exotic feel of Madagascar
cons: Long, arduous journey
Almost no easy routes
No rescue service or medical care nearby
Bolting is sparse in places
famous_lines: Out of Africa 7a (Tsaranoro Kely, 580 m, 14 pitches)

el-potrero-chico.description: A canyon of giant limestone “fins” near Monterrey — one of North America's top winter destinations and the best area in the Americas for long sport multi-pitches. Well-bolted routes of up to 23 pitches (Time Wave Zero), hundreds of single-pitch routes 10 minutes from the campground and a friendly climbing scene in December–January.
el-potrero-chico.rating_basis: One of North America's top winter destinations and the best area in the Americas for long sport multi-pitches: ~680 routes on Mountain Project (~7k views a month), more than 140 multi-pitches of up to 23 pitches
el-potrero-chico.hazards: Rockfall (helmet essential), long rappels off multi-pitch routes in the dark, heat on sunny days, fast-building thunderstorms; dogs and petty theft at the campgrounds
el-potrero-chico.crowd_note: In December–January (especially over the holidays) there are queues on the popular multi-pitches Space Boyz, Estrellita and Time Wave Zero — parties start before dawn
el-potrero-chico.region: Nuevo León, Sierra Madre Oriental, near the town of Hidalgo (40 km from Monterrey)
el-potrero-chico.season: November–February (peak December–January, when climbers from all over North America gather); October and March are warm but climbable; from April to September the heat tops +30 °C, and late summer brings downpours and tropical storms
el-potrero-chico.transfer: Fly to Monterrey, then a taxi or a La Posada transfer to Hidalgo (~45 min, taxi ~$50–60); by car from Laredo (Texas) ~3 h on toll roads
el-potrero-chico.rock_note: grey-orange limestone on vertical slab “fins” up to 600 m high on both sides of the canyon: vertical and slightly overhanging walls with slots, pockets and arêtes; loose rock in places
el-potrero-chico.approach: 5–20 min on foot from the campgrounds and guesthouses at the canyon entrance; up to 30–40 min to the more distant multi-pitches
el-potrero-chico.restrictions: The canyon lies within El Potrero Chico municipal park — driving in requires a parking pass (check with the park administration). If driving from the US: tourist card, Mexican insurance, daytime driving only on toll roads; check the safety advisories for Nuevo León state before your trip. Helmets are a must — rockfall happens in the canyon.
el-potrero-chico.guidebook: Magic Ed's guidebook (The Whole Enchilada) and the Rakkup digital guide; updated topos are sold on site at cafés and campgrounds
el-potrero-chico.stay: Climbers' campgrounds and guesthouses at the canyon entrance: La Posada (pool, restaurant, airport transfers), Homero's (since 1989), Quinta La Pagoda (closest to the walls), Rancho el Sendero, Estancia San José; camping ~$5–8, rooms ~$20–50
pros: Long, fully bolted mid-grade multi-pitches
Warm, dry winter
Cheap living, campgrounds 10 min from the walls
A great place to step up from single-pitch sport to multi-pitch
cons: Few hard top-end single-pitch routes
Queues on popular multi-pitches over the holidays
Loose rock on less-travelled routes
Safety concerns when driving through northern Mexico
famous_lines: El Sendero Luminoso 5.12+ (7b/7b+), 15 pitches, El Toro — free soloed by Alex Honnold in 2014
school_notes: US school: winter climbing programmes and multi-pitch courses in Potrero Chico

castle-hill-kura-tawhiti.description: Kura Tawhiti (Castle Hill) is a field of huge limestone boulders on hills between the Torlesse and Craigieburn ranges and New Zealand's premier bouldering spot. The rounded shapes demand friction and mantel technique, while neighbouring Flock Hill, Spittle Hill and Quantum Field add thousands more problems. The site is sacred to Ngāi Tahu, and the rules of conduct are strict.
castle-hill-kura-tawhiti.rating_basis: New Zealand's premier bouldering spot (Wikipedia, ClimbNZ): thousands of limestone boulders in the Castle Hill Basin, problems up to 8A and beyond, iconic scenery
castle-hill-kura-tawhiti.hazards: Sudden weather changes and westerly winds, hypothermia in winter, strong sun (high UV), falls from tall highballs onto uneven ground
castle-hill-kura-tawhiti.crowd_note: Lots of tourists and climbers at the boulders closest to the car park; Flock Hill and the more distant sectors are quiet
castle-hill-kura-tawhiti.region: Canterbury, Castle Hill Basin, SH73 to Arthur's Pass
castle-hill-kura-tawhiti.season: March–May and October–November (southern hemisphere autumn and spring); cold in winter with occasional snow, but friction is excellent on dry, sunny days; a bit hot in the sun in summer
castle-hill-kura-tawhiti.transfer: ~80 min by car from Christchurch on SH73; the TranzAlpine train passes by but doesn't stop
castle-hill-kura-tawhiti.rock_note: grey limestone “castle” boulders on grassy hills: rounded shapes, slopers, mantels and friction; the rock polishes quickly
castle-hill-kura-tawhiti.approach: 10–20 min on foot from the car park on SH73 along a trail across private pasture
castle-hill-kura-tawhiti.restrictions: A DOC reserve with Tōpuni status (wāhi tapu, sacred sites of Ngāi Tahu): stay on the trail, don't dig or trample rare plants, respect temporary access restrictions; brush off chalk and tick marks; new bolts are prohibited and trad is discouraged; no dogs. Neighbouring Flock Hill is a private station and requires a short online certification
castle-hill-kura-tawhiti.guidebook: The Comprehensive Castle Hill Climbing Guide; online topos on castlehillbasin.co.nz and ClimbNZ
castle-hill-kura-tawhiti.stay: Holiday houses in Castle Hill village, the DOC campsite at Craigieburn, hostels and hotels in Springfield and Christchurch
pros: A huge number of boulders for all levels
Short approach from the highway
Spectacular scenery
Easy to reach from Christchurch
cons: The rock polishes quickly
Changeable mountain weather, snow in winter
Strict cultural rules

paynes-ford.description: Paynes Ford is a set of limestone walls along the Takaka River in subtropical bush near Golden Bay — New Zealand's most “holiday-like” sport climbing area. About 250 routes 5–7b+, mostly 15–25 m long, with the legendary Hangdog climbers' campground right by the crags. The Tarakohe sea cliffs are nearby.
paynes-ford.rating_basis: New Zealand's best sport area for a climbing holiday: ~250 routes (Mountain Project) next to a climbers' campground, limestone in the bush; few hard routes
paynes-ford.hazards: Slippery rock in damp weather, sandflies, wasps in late summer
paynes-ford.crowd_note: At Christmas and New Year Hangdog is full and there are waits on popular routes; almost empty in winter
paynes-ford.season: year-round; best March–May and October–November; humid and crowded in summer (Christmas–New Year), cool in winter but with good friction
paynes-ford.transfer: ~1.5–2 h by car from Nelson over Takaka Hill; ~6 h from Christchurch
paynes-ford.rock_note: grey limestone in subtropical bush by the river: vertical and slightly overhanging, pockets, flowstone, slopers, roofs in places
paynes-ford.approach: 5–15 min along well-kept trails from Hangdog Camp and the reserve car park; the Tarakohe sea cliffs are 15 min away by car
paynes-ford.restrictions: The crags are in the Paines Ford Scenic Reserve (DOC): no fires, stay on the trails; after heavy rain the walls take several days to dry — don't climb on dirty or wet rock
paynes-ford.guidebook: Golden Bay Climbing Guide; online topos on theCrag and thetopo.com
paynes-ford.stay: Hangdog Camp — a private climbers' campground a few metres from the crags (showers, toilets, bunkhouse); accommodation in Takaka, 5 min away
pros: Campground a minute from the crags
Lots of mid-grade routes
Beautiful bush and a river for swimming
Climbable year-round
cons: Few hard routes
Humid in summer — the rock gets greasy
Walls take a long time to dry after rain
Far from major cities

guamka.description: Guamka is a hamlet at the entrance to the Guam Gorge, with 400 m cliffs above the Kurdzhips River, and the main sport climbing area of southern Russia. More than 250 routes from 4 to 9a in 17 shady forest sectors. Other crags lie nearby in Adygea: the historic Khadzhokh sectors (“Korotyshki”, “Rossiya” — about twenty routes), “Obval” above Dakhovskaya, and Doguako (60+ routes, ~1,100 m).
guamka.rating_basis: The main sport area of southern Russia: 250+ routes up to 9a, rated 5 stars by the Russian Climbing Federation (FSR), national climbing festivals; shady crags make summer climbing possible
guamka.hazards: Ticks, rockfall, limestone slippery after rain, snakes
guamka.crowd_note: In summer and at weekends lots of climbers from Krasnodar and training camps; during festivals the popular sectors are busy
guamka.region: Krasnodar Krai, Apsheronsky District, on the border with Adygea (Western Caucasus)
guamka.season: April–October; best July–October (cool by the rock, August is the most stable month); frequent rain in spring and June
guamka.transfer: Fly or take the train to Krasnodar (~156 km, ~3 h by car via Apsheronsk); Apsheronsk — Guamka bus twice a day
guamka.rock_note: limestone in the forest above the Kurdzhips River: vertical and overhanging, routes of 12–35 m, up to 50 m in the “Stalingrad” sector
guamka.approach: Sectors in the forested part of the gorge, 10–40 min on foot from the hamlet
guamka.restrictions: While the tourist train is running on the narrow-gauge railway, walking through the gorge from its start to the station by the “1707” café is not allowed. No climbing fees; the guidebook is sold to support bolting
guamka.guidebook: “Skalolazanie v Guamke” (Climbing in Guamka; AllClimb — the Pologrudovs and ClimbLife — the Shaferovs, with FSR support, 2019 ed.): 250+ routes in 17 sectors, 5b–9a; the FSR database “Skaly Rossii” (Rocks of Russia)
guamka.stay: Gagarin campground, the FSR base camp by the Kurdzhips River, hotels and guesthouses in the hamlet (“Guamka”, “Bolshaya Medveditsa”, “Orekhovaya Roshcha”); thermal pools in Volodeya, 7 km away
pros: Shade and cool air in summer
Big choice of grade 6–7 routes plus hard lines
Campgrounds and accommodation by the rock, a river for swimming
Lots of Russian-speaking training camps
cons: Few sunny sectors in spring and autumn
Rain in spring and early summer
Far from the airport
famous_lines: “Stalingrad” sector — long routes 6b–8b+, up to 50 m
school_notes: Summer camps and coached training, by the guidebook authors
9-day intensive with transfer from Krasnodar and apartments
Trips and training sessions in the Guam Gorge

indyuk.description: Mount Indyuk (859 m) is a rock massif 30 km from Tuapse with views of the Black Sea coast and one of the main sport climbing areas of southern Russia. Around 125–139 routes 4–8a in the “Perya”, “Karaul” and “Korona” sectors and ~20 trad routes up to 150 m on monolithic porphyritic tuff. Life is in tents below the crags, with the sea nearby.
indyuk.rating_basis: One of the main sport areas of southern Russia: 125–139 routes 4–8a and ~20 trad routes up to 150 m on monolithic volcanic rock; rated 5 stars by the FSR; downsides are the long approach and water shortages in summer
indyuk.hazards: Heat and dehydration in summer, ticks, rockfall on long routes
indyuk.crowd_note: Over the May holidays and at weekends lots of climbers come from Krasnodar and the coast; quiet the rest of the time
indyuk.region: Krasnodar Krai, Tuapse District, Western Caucasus (30 km from the Black Sea coast)
indyuk.season: Mid-April to late October; best mid-April to mid-June and the second half of September–October; July–August are hot and the springs dry up; snow from late December to March
indyuk.transfer: ~3–4 h by car from Krasnodar via Dzhubga and Tuapse (or via the Shaumyan Pass); local trains to the “1744 km” or “Indyuk” stations; ~30 km from Tuapse
indyuk.rock_note: monolithic porphyritic tuff (volcanic rock): friction slabs, vertical walls on small holds, overhangs, roofs, “hourglass” threads; buttresses up to 150 m, crags facing every direction
indyuk.approach: 1–1.5 h from Indyuk village or the “1744 km” platform to the campsites below the crags, then 10–20 min to the sectors
indyuk.restrictions: No fees. Camping in tents only at the campsites (“Rodnikovaya Polyana”, “Lokomotivskie Nochevki”); there's little water by the crags — the springs dry up from July, and in August the nearest permanent spring is between Indyushka and Indyushonok
indyuk.guidebook: Guidebook by G. Dultsev (2003) and guidebook by M. Foigel (2008); descriptions on climbinduk.org and in the FSR database; AllClimb online guide (~139 routes)
indyuk.stay: Tents at the equipped campsites below the crags; the nearest accommodation is in Indyuk village and on the Tuapse coast
pros: Unusual monolithic rock, varied features
Sun and shade — crags face every direction
Black Sea coast nearby
Free, tent life
cons: Long approach of 1–1.5 h
Hot with little water in summer
Few hard routes
indyuk.airport: KRR — Krasnodar, ~3.5 h; AER — Sochi, ~3 h
famous_lines: “Korona” (Crown) sector — 41 routes on the summit, up to 50 m
Begunki — the easiest route in the area
Ruslo — the hardest route in the area

krasnoyarsk-stolby.description: The Krasnoyarsk Stolby are syenite rock pillars in the taiga on the outskirts of Krasnoyarsk — the cradle of Russian climbing and the birthplace of “stolbizm”, ropeless climbing on traditional “khody” (passages). Around 500 “khitrushki” boulder problems 5A–8A and 121 sport routes 4–8b on 14 massifs (Kitaiskaya Stenka, Takmak, Pervy Stolb and others).
krasnoyarsk-stolby.rating_basis: The cradle of Russian climbing (first route in 1851, “stolbizm”), ~500 khitrushki and 121 routes; rated 5 stars by the FSR; but a short season and long approaches
krasnoyarsk-stolby.hazards: Tick-borne encephalitis, ropeless climbing on the khody, old bolts, slippery wet rock, no drinking water along the trails
krasnoyarsk-stolby.crowd_note: At weekends the Central Stolby and Takmak are busy with tourists and local stolbisty; the “Khitrushki” festival in September and a winter one in January
krasnoyarsk-stolby.region: Krasnoyarsk Krai, Krasnoyarsk Stolby National Park
krasnoyarsk-stolby.season: May–October, best July–September; lots of ticks in May–June; in winter only locals climb (Christmas festival in January)
krasnoyarsk-stolby.transfer: Krasnoyarsk airport → city ~40 min; to the Laletino ranger post by car on the M54 highway (parking ~70 RUB) or by minibus to the “Turbaza” stop; to Takmak, buses 39, 8a and 30a to “Bazaikha”
krasnoyarsk-stolby.rock_note: syenite (a granite-like rock): rock pillars up to 100 m high in the taiga, rounded shapes, cracks, khitrushki on boulders and the traditional khody of the stolbisty
krasnoyarsk-stolby.approach: Central Stolby: ~5 km on foot from the Laletino ranger post (~7 km from the “Turbaza” stop), or ride up on the Bobrovy Log chairlift; the Takmak area is 1–2 km from Bazaikha
krasnoyarsk-stolby.restrictions: National park: entry is free; visitors may stay only in the tourist and excursion zone, on the trails, during daytime; fires, tents outside the tent camp at the Narym ranger post, damaging the rock, graffiti and stripping moss are prohibited. Climb only in dry weather. Vaccination against tick-borne encephalitis is necessary. On some old routes the bolts haven't been checked for a long time
krasnoyarsk-stolby.guidebook: Guidebook “Krasnoyarskie Stolby” (240 pp., 2016; sport routes, khody and khitrushki of the Central area); the FSR “Skaly Rossii” database (c-f-r.ru); maps on stolby.ru
krasnoyarsk-stolby.stay: The tent camp and huts at the Narym ranger post — the only place you may stay overnight; otherwise accommodation in Krasnoyarsk (20–40 min to the entrance)
pros: Unique history and the culture of stolbizm
Hundreds of khitrushki on rough syenite
Cool in summer, shade in the taiga
Free entry
cons: Short season
Long walk-ins
Ticks in May–June
Few sport routes, some bolts are old
famous_lines: Slonik (Little Elephant) — the most famous boulder of the Stolby
Golubye Katushki — a popular khod (Central Stolby)
school_notes: Commercial tour of the Stolby with climbing instruction
Mountaineering and climbing school on natural rock

treugolnoe-karelian-isthmus.description: Lake Treugolnoe (Triangular Lake) is the main sport climbing area of the Karelian Isthmus and north-west Russia: granite walls above a forest lake with 200+ routes 5a–8c+ (half of them up to 6c) and 200+ boulders. 1.5 km away is Lietlahti park with 500+ boulder problems, and closer to Kuznechnoye lies the legendary Yastrebinoe Lake (Bolshie Skaly), home since 1987 of the “Skalolazanie dlya vsekh” (Climbing for All) festival. The Karelian crags around Lake Ladoga (Impilahti, Hiitola) are little developed.
treugolnoe-karelian-isthmus.rating_basis: The best sport area in north-west Russia: 200+ routes up to 8c+ and 200+ boulders by the lake, plus 500+ boulders in nearby Lietlahti park; rated 5 stars by the FSR
treugolnoe-karelian-isthmus.hazards: Mosquitoes and ticks, slippery wet granite in shady sectors, crossing a stream on a log
treugolnoe-karelian-isthmus.crowd_note: On summer weekends lots of people come from St Petersburg — parking spaces and campsites are scarce; quiet on weekdays
treugolnoe-karelian-isthmus.region: Leningrad Oblast, Vyborgsky District, Karelian Isthmus (including Lietlahti park and Yastrebinoe Lake)
treugolnoe-karelian-isthmus.season: May–September; best June–September; lots of mosquitoes in summer, especially in shady sectors
treugolnoe-karelian-isthmus.transfer: ~3 h by car from St Petersburg on the Scandinavia highway via Lesogorsky and Topolki (the last ~12 km is a dirt road) or via the Priozerskoye highway; without a car — local train to Vyborg, bus to Lesogorsky and a taxi
treugolnoe-karelian-isthmus.rock_note: Karelian granite above a forest lake: big overhangs, roofs, friction, chimneys; mostly south-facing, dries quickly after rain
