treugolnoe-karelian-isthmus.approach: ~20 min from the car to the campsites and the main massif; the “Reka” massif is 20 min away across a stream on a log, “Gornyak” 1.5 km along a trail; the last stretch of dirt road is better done in a 4×4
treugolnoe-karelian-isthmus.restrictions: Border zone: a permit is required (free via Gosuslugi or by e-mail, valid for a month; checked periodically) — for the lake as well as for the Lietlahti farmstead and park. Take all your rubbish with you; the good campsites are usually “claimed” by regulars, and it's bad form to take them
treugolnoe-karelian-isthmus.guidebook: Guidebook by Ovsyannikov and Tselishchev (2008) and the Triangular Lake app; topos on 27crags and theCrag; the FSR “Skaly Rossii” database
treugolnoe-karelian-isthmus.stay: Tents at the campsites by the lake and on Upper Novoselskoye Lake; a guesthouse at the Lietlahti farmstead 1.5 km away (by arrangement, permit required)
pros: World-class granite near St Petersburg
Routes and boulders in one place
Overhangs for rainy days, dries quickly
Tent life by the lake, white nights
cons: Border zone — permit required
Mosquitoes
Short season
Poor road on the last stretch
school_notes: Coached trips and camps on the Karelian Isthmus
Organised trips from St Petersburg
One-day and multi-day climbing trips from St Petersburg

osp-misja-pec.description: Osp is a small village on the edge of the Karst near the Italian border and Slovenia's main sport climbing area. Together with Mišja Peč and Črni Kal there are more than 600–700 routes: the overhanging endurance amphitheatre of Mišja Peč (mostly 7a–8a and up to 9a+), the big wall and cave of Osp up to 140 m, and the easy vertical climbing of Črni Kal.
osp-misja-pec.rating_basis: The centre of Slovenian climbing: ~700 routes on three crags; Mišja Peč is one of Europe's best overhanging sectors with routes up to 9a+, plus the “cave” climbing of Osp
osp-misja-pec.hazards: Polished holds, long runouts near the top of routes, rockfall, summer heat
osp-misja-pec.crowd_note: On autumn and spring weekends Mišja Peč is busy with Italians from Trieste and Slovenians
osp-misja-pec.region: Slovenian Littoral, the Karst near the Italian border (Trieste)
osp-misja-pec.season: Year-round, best October–December and March–April; in summer only early in the morning and in the shade; November–February can be cold and damp, with the bora blowing
osp-misja-pec.transfer: Trieste airport is ~40 min away; Ljubljana is 1–1.5 h by car; ~15 min from Trieste via the Rabuiese border crossing
osp-misja-pec.rock_note: grey karst limestone: the horseshoe-shaped overhanging amphitheatre of Mišja Peč, the big wall and cave of Osp (up to 140 m), the vertical walls of Črni Kal
osp-misja-pec.approach: 5–15 min on foot from the campground in Osp to the Osp wall and Mišja Peč; Črni Kal is 10 min away by car
osp-misja-pec.restrictions: In spring some routes in the central sector of Mišja Peč are closed until June because of nesting owls and peregrine falcons (bans by Projekt OSP and the nature conservation services; the list of routes is posted on signs at the crag). Check at the campground whether the right-hand sector of the big Osp wall is open. Don't park in the village and don't pitch tents below the wall
osp-misja-pec.guidebook: Regional guidebook to the Slovenian Littoral and Trieste (~3,100 routes on 32 crags); topos on theCrag
osp-misja-pec.stay: Vovk climbers' campground in Osp (year-round, within walking distance of the walls), a hostel in Očizla; Trieste is 15 min away
pros: World-class hard routes
Overhangs stay dry in the rain
Campground by the crags, Trieste nearby
Sunny sectors in winter
cons: Few easy routes at Osp itself and Mišja Peč
Polished classics
Hot in summer, the bora can blow in winter
osp-misja-pec.airport: TRS — Trieste, ~40 min; LJU — Ljubljana, ~1.5 h

railay-tonsai.description: The Railay peninsula and neighbouring Tonsai are Southeast Asia's best-known climbing area: karst towers right above the beaches, sport routes, multi-pitches on Thaiwand Wall and deep-water soloing (DWS) from boats. This is where the trend for “beach” climbing in Asia began; there are plenty of schools and rental shops.
railay-tonsai.rating_basis: A classic of world tropical climbing: 700+ routes on 49 walls (UKC), multi-pitches above the sea and DWS; downsides are polish, corroded old bolts and heat
railay-tonsai.hazards: Heat and dehydration, corroded bolts and slings, rotten stalactites, tides on the approaches, aggressive monkeys (rabies risk); inspect any rental gear
railay-tonsai.crowd_note: 1-2-3 Wall and the beginner walls are packed with school groups; the harder Tonsai sectors are quieter
railay-tonsai.season: November–April (dry season); best December–February; June to October is monsoon season — rain and cancelled boats
railay-tonsai.transfer: Fly to Krabi, ~40 min by taxi to the Ao Nang pier, then a 10–15-min longtail boat
railay-tonsai.rock_note: tropical limestone of karst towers above the sea: stalactites, tufas, caves and overhangs; polished on popular routes
railay-tonsai.approach: No roads: 10–15 min by longtail from Ao Nang; 2–20 min on foot from the beaches to the walls, some walls only at low tide or by boat
railay-tonsai.restrictions: According to local sources, the area belongs to Hat Noppharat Thara – Mu Ko Phi Phi National Park; some walls are accessible only at low tide. Old stainless-steel bolts corrode quickly — trust only glued-in titanium ones (the Thaitanium programme) and check against the guidebook
railay-tonsai.guidebook: Rock Climbing in Thailand and Laos (Elke Schmitz); the King Climbers guidebook; Thailand Climbing (Sam Lightner Jr.) — part of the proceeds go to rebolting
railay-tonsai.stay: Bungalows and guesthouses in Tonsai (a climbers' camp, no ATMs) or hotels on Railay West and Railay East
pros: Climbing by the sea, beaches, DWS
Lots of schools, rental and beginner courses
Multi-pitches with views over the Andaman Sea
You can climb for a month without any transport
cons: Heat and humidity even in the dry season
Polished classic routes
Corroded anchors and old bolts
Monsoon from June to October
railay-tonsai.airport: KBV — Krabi, ~1 h including the boat; HKT — Phuket, ~3 h
famous_lines: Lord of the Thais 7b (Thaiwand Wall, 5 pitches)
school_notes: School and gear rental in Tonsai, DWS trips
The oldest school on Railay, publisher of the local guidebook
Beginner courses, multi-pitches and DWS

geyikbayiri.description: Geyikbayırı is a village in the Taurus foothills 40 km from Antalya and Turkey's main winter sport climbing area. More than 1,300 routes in 40+ sectors of karst limestone, from easy lines to 8c+/9a; the walls face every direction, and there are caves and tufas. A climbing-campground vibe, the sea nearby and lots of Russian-speaking training camps.
geyikbayiri.rating_basis: The main winter sport area of Turkey and the eastern Mediterranean: 1,300+ routes in 40+ sectors, well-developed campgrounds, glowing reviews from Rock+Run, National Geographic and Gripped
geyikbayiri.hazards: Polished holds on the classics, heat on south-facing walls in spring, rockfall
geyikbayiri.crowd_note: Busiest in November and February (slackline festival); on Sundays tourists flock to the market in Akdamlar
geyikbayiri.season: October–April; best October–November and March–April; December–January are the rainiest months; hot in summer
geyikbayiri.transfer: 40 km from Antalya airport: taxi ~€35–40, rental car (can be arranged through the campground) or buses 521/501 from the bus station to Akdamlar and then another ~6 km
geyikbayiri.rock_note: orange-grey karst limestone: tufas, caves, vertical walls; the walls face every direction
geyikbayiri.approach: A single paved road runs along the crags; approaches of 5–15 min, ~30 min to the more distant sectors
geyikbayiri.restrictions: The area lies within a nature park; there are no climbing fees. Routes are equipped with stainless-steel bolts and rebolting is ongoing — buy the guidebook on site at the campgrounds (proceeds go to the routes)
geyikbayiri.guidebook: Official guidebook by Öztürk Kayıkcı (2023), sold at the campgrounds; topos on theCrag
geyikbayiri.stay: Climbers' campgrounds and bungalows by the crags: JoSiTo, Climbers Garden, Kezban, Flying Goat, Peak Guesthouses and others; bungalows ~€20–40, a tent ~€7 a night, breakfasts and dinners available
pros: Sunny and shady sectors for any day
Climbers' campgrounds right by the crags
Cheap direct flights to Antalya
Lots of Russian-speaking training camps and coaches
cons: Too hot in summer
Rain in December–January
Popular classics are polished
school_notes: Coached intensive: transfer from Antalya, apartments, group gear
Coached climbing camps in Geyikbayırı
Training programmes in Geyikbayırı, Citdibi and Olympos
Russian-speaking climbing school for beginners and intermediates

long-dong.description: Long Dong is a set of sea cliffs at the north-eastern tip of Taiwan, facing the Pacific Ocean. Around six hundred routes on very hard quartz sandstone: trad cracks, sport lines and a couple of multi-pitches, with a swim in the sea after climbing. The season is autumn and spring, between the winter monsoon and the summer typhoons.
long-dong.rating_basis: Taiwan's main climbing area: almost 600 routes (G3), 268 described on Mountain Project in 10 sectors; quality trad above the sea an hour from Taipei
long-dong.hazards: Waves and tides on the approaches, typhoons in summer, wasps, corroded bolts, heat on exposed crags
long-dong.crowd_note: At weekends lots of local climbers from Taipei at the sectors by the north car park; empty on weekdays
long-dong.region: New Taipei, north-east coast, Gongliao District
long-dong.season: October–May; best October–November and April; in winter the north-east monsoon brings wind, drizzle and cold; May–June is the “plum rain” season, and summer brings heat and typhoons
long-dong.transfer: ~1 h from Taipei by car (≈35 km) or by bus via Keelung with a change
long-dong.rock_note: very hard quartz sandstone (metaconglomerate) on sea cliffs up to 30 m: cracks and arêtes, with a feel close to granite
long-dong.approach: 5–30 min along coastal trails from three car parks on the coastal highway (north, central, south); access to some walls depends on the tide and swell
long-dong.restrictions: North-east Coast National Scenic Area; the wall by the central approach is closed for nesting peregrine falcons (usually 1 February – 30 June); camping in tents is formally prohibited; don't remove fixed gear or run the rope through it; bolts near the sea corrode
long-dong.guidebook: Rock Climbing Taiwan (Matt Robertson, 2012, partly outdated); Long Dong Trad Climbs (Matt Robertson, 2006); up-to-date topos on Mountain Project and the local Guidebook Plus supplement
long-dong.stay: The Bivy in neighbouring Bitou village, rooms by the north car park, hostels in Jiufen, a paid campground in Fulong
pros: Excellent trad on hard rock
An hour from Taipei
A swim in the sea after climbing
Lots of mid-grade routes
cons: Wind and drizzle in winter, heat and typhoons in summer
Bolts near the sea corrode
Tent camping is formally prohibited
long-dong.airport: TSA — Taipei Songshan, ~1 h; TPE — Taoyuan, ~1.5 h

bishop.description: Bishop is North America's winter bouldering capital, set against the snowy Sierra. The granite highballs of the Buttermilks and the volcanic canyons of the Happy and Sad Boulders offer thousands of problems from V0 to V15 with flat landings and almost guaranteed sun. Nearby are hundreds of sport routes in the Owens River Gorge.
bishop.rating_basis: One of the world's bouldering capitals: on Mountain Project ~1,500 problems in the Buttermilks, Tablelands and Druid Stones alone (~26k area views a month), over 1,800 problems according to Kaya; landmark 8B+–8C problems have been climbed here
bishop.hazards: Tall highballs over rocks (several crash pads needed), sharp granite that shreds skin, strong wind and frost at night in winter, rattlesnakes in the warmer months
bishop.crowd_note: At weekends from December to March Peabody and the Happy Boulders are busy, with queues for the classics; quiet on weekdays and at the more distant blocks
bishop.region: California, Eastern Sierra Nevada, Owens Valley
bishop.season: October–April, best November–March (dry, sunny, excellent friction); on cold days head for the Happy/Sad Boulders (lower and sheltered from the wind), on warm days the Buttermilks; in April–May climb in the mornings and evenings; June–September is too hot (in summer people move to Mammoth and June Lake, an hour's drive away)
bishop.transfer: A car is needed: on Highway 395 ~4.5 h from Los Angeles (400 km), ~3.5 h from Reno, ~4 h from Las Vegas; crash pads, climbing shoes and guidebooks can be rented from Eastside Sports in Bishop
bishop.rock_note: two rock types: coarse-grained granite in the Buttermilks (1,950 m) — highballs, small holds and sharp crystals; volcanic tuff in the Volcanic Tablelands (Happy and Sad Boulders, ~1,300 m) — canyons with pockets, overhangs and flat landings; sport climbing in the nearby Owens River Gorge (tuff, ~1,100 routes)
bishop.approach: 2–15 min from the parking areas: the Buttermilks along the dirt Buttermilk Road (high clearance advisable), Happy and Sad via a short climb into the canyons from Chalk Bluff Road
bishop.restrictions: BLM and Inyo National Forest land: stay on the trails, don't put crash pads on plants, pack out all rubbish and waste (wag bag). In the Buttermilks overnight stays and fires at the Birthday Boulders car park are prohibited. The Pleasant Valley Pit climbers' campground costs $5 per site, no reservations. Before your trip it's worth checking the Bishop Climbing Rangers' weekly conditions report.
bishop.guidebook: Bishop Bouldering (Charlie Barrett) and Bishop Area Rock Climbs (Wolverine Publishing); guidebooks can be rented at Eastside Sports
bishop.stay: Pleasant Valley Pit campground near the Happy/Sad Boulders ($5), budget motels and a hostel in Bishop; on winter weekends there's a “climbers' coffee” with the rangers at the Pit
pros: Thousands of problems at all grades with flat landings
Dry, sunny winters and excellent friction
Two different rock types 20 minutes apart
Cheap campground and crash pad rental in town
Owens River Gorge sport routes nearby
cons: Too hot in summer
Cold nights and wind in the Buttermilks in winter
Car needed, potholed dirt roads
Crowded at weekends
bishop.airport: BIH — Bishop (seasonal flights from Denver and San Francisco from roughly mid-December to March); RNO — Reno, ~3.5 h; LAS — Las Vegas, ~4 h; LAX — Los Angeles, ~4.5 h
famous_lines: Evilution Direct V11 (8A), Grandpa Peabody, Buttermilks
school_notes: Eastern Sierra guide service: climbing and mountaineering
Climbing and mountaineering guides in the Bishop area

hueco-tanks.description: A desert park with caves and overhanging boulders near El Paso — one of the most famous places in world bouldering and the birthplace of the V scale. More than a thousand steep problems on pockets and roofs, ideal dry winters and a strict access system to protect ancient rock art.
hueco-tanks.rating_basis: A cult spot in world bouldering: the V scale was born here; more than 1,000 problems (North Mountain alone has 850 in the Wolverine guidebook), problems by Fred Nicole and Daniel Woods up to V15–V16; National Geographic has listed it among America's best adventures
hueco-tanks.hazards: Cacti and thorns on the approaches, sharp pocket edges, rattlesnakes on warm days, wind and cold nights in winter; after rain the rock becomes fragile — let it dry
hueco-tanks.crowd_note: Visitor numbers are capped by the reservation system, so the boulders are uncrowded — the hard part is getting a North Mountain slot on a weekend between December and March
hueco-tanks.region: Texas, Chihuahuan Desert, 40 km north-east of El Paso
hueco-tanks.season: November–March (best November–February; strong winds in March and early April); October and April depend on the weather; mid-April to September is too hot, with monsoon thunderstorms in summer as well
hueco-tanks.transfer: A car is essential: ~40 min east from El Paso on Montana Ave (US 62/180)
hueco-tanks.rock_note: syenite porphyry — a hard igneous rock similar to granite: steep overhangs, roofs and caves with huecos (scoops and pockets), lots of heel and toe hooks; very few slabs
hueco-tanks.approach: 5–30 min from the park's car park and campground; East Mountain, East Spur and West Mountain only in a guided group
hueco-tanks.restrictions: Strict access: Hueco Tanks is a state historic site with ancient rock art. Self-guided climbing is allowed only on North Mountain — no more than 70 people a day (60 places by advance phone reservation on +1 512 389-8911 up to 90 days ahead, 10 on the day of the visit, with priority for those camping in the park; unconfirmed reservations are released at 10:00). You can book up to 3 consecutive days, then take a day off. East Mountain, East Spur and West Mountain only with a guide (book at least a week ahead). Entry is $7 per adult per day; watching the orientation video once a year is mandatory; the park closes at 18:00 (opens at 8:00 in winter); fires and drones are prohibited.
hueco-tanks.guidebook: Hueco Tanks: North Mountain (Matt Wilder, Jason Kehl; Wolverine Publishing, 2nd ed. 2020) — 850 North Mountain problems plus the “best of” the guided areas
hueco-tanks.stay: Campground inside the park ($12–16 per site; campers get priority for free North Mountain slots), the climber-run Hueco Rock Ranch 1.5 km away (camping and rooms, open November–April), hotels in El Paso (40 min)
pros: Legendary steep bouldering at all levels — from V0 to V15
Dry, sunny winters
Thanks to the visitor cap, the boulders are never crowded
A climbers' camping ranch nearby
cons: Complicated reservation system and mandatory guides for two-thirds of the park
The park closes at 18:00
Wind in March–April, heat from May
Crash pad rental on site isn't guaranteed — better to bring your own
school_notes: Local guide service: access to the guide-only areas (East Mountain, East Spur, West Mountain)
Commercial bouldering guides at Hueco Tanks
Guides for the restricted-access areas

indian-creek.description: A desert canyon in Utah with hundreds of red sandstone walls split by perfectly parallel cracks — the world's benchmark for crack climbing. There's almost no sport climbing here: just trad, lots of same-sized cams and hand-jamming technique. You live in a tent in the desert under the stars.
indian-creek.rating_basis: The world's crack-climbing mecca: ~1,700 routes on Mountain Project (~13k views a month); the classics Supercrack and Incredible Hand Crack feature on lists of the world's best cracks
indian-creek.hazards: Fragile wet sandstone, heat and dehydration, cold nights, rattlesnakes, remoteness from medical help, flash floods in the canyons after downpours
indian-creek.crowd_note: In October and April there are queues at Supercrack Buttress and Donnelly Canyon, and the campgrounds overflow at weekends; the more distant walls are quiet
indian-creek.region: Utah, Bears Ears National Monument, Colorado Plateau (between Moab and Monticello)
indian-creek.season: spring (late March–May) and autumn (September–November), October being the best month; in early autumn seek shade during the day, in late autumn the sunny south-facing walls; cold wind in spring; summer heat above +32 °C and nesting closures, cold in winter
indian-creek.transfer: A car is needed: ~1.5 h from Moab, ~45 min from Monticello, ~5 h from Salt Lake City, ~8 h from Denver and Las Vegas; cams in large numbers (6–16 of the same size) — bring your own or rent in Moab
indian-creek.rock_note: red Wingate sandstone: perfectly parallel vertical cracks of every width — from thin finger cracks to offwidths — on walls 30–60 m high; almost exclusively single-pitch trad
indian-creek.approach: 10–40 min of steep uphill over scree from the dirt parking areas along Route 211; stay on the trails and don't step on the cryptobiotic crust
indian-creek.restrictions: Don't climb on wet sandstone: wait 24–48 hours after rain, otherwise holds break and anchors weaken. Annual raptor nesting closures from 1 March to the end of summer on dozens of walls (Echo, Reservoir Wall, Cat Wall and others — see the BLM map); walls without active nests reopen in late April–May. Don't park or walk on cryptobiotic soil, pack out human waste, don't touch archaeological sites, close gates on private land. The Creek Pasture, Superbowl and Hamburger Rock campgrounds cost $15 a night, no reservations, 14-day maximum.
indian-creek.guidebook: Indian Creek: A Climbing Guide (David Bloom); online — Mountain Project
indian-creek.stay: BLM campgrounds Creek Pasture and Superbowl (tables, toilets, $15), primitive sites at Bridger Jack and Cottonwood; no water — bring your own (a 20-litre jerrycan for two lasts ~4 days); the nearest shops and motels are in Monticello (50 km) and Moab (100 km)
pros: The best parallel cracks in the world
Huge choice of 5.10–5.12 routes
Free or cheap campgrounds among the crags
Dry, sunny climate in spring and autumn
cons: You need a big rack of cams and solid crack technique
Few routes for beginners
No water, shops or phone signal; town is far away
Seasonal raptor closures on many walls
indian-creek.airport: CNY — Moab (Canyonlands Field, expensive flights), ~1.5 h; GJT — Grand Junction, ~3 h; SLC — Salt Lake City, ~5 h

joshua-tree.description: Thousands of granite domes and boulders in the middle of the Mojave Desert — California's top winter climbing destination. Short trad routes on cracks and slabs, topropes for beginners and a huge amount of bouldering with very harsh friction. The rocks stand right by the park's roads and campgrounds.
joshua-tree.rating_basis: About 8,100 routes and problems on Mountain Project (~41k views a month) — one of the largest databases in the US; a classic winter destination for Californian climbers
joshua-tree.hazards: Heat and dehydration (there's almost no water in the park), cold winter nights, rattlesnakes and cacti on the approaches, easy to get lost among identical-looking rocks, sandy “ball bearings” on slabs
joshua-tree.crowd_note: From November to May the campgrounds and the classics in Hidden Valley are packed at weekends; quiet on weekdays and at the more distant domes
joshua-tree.region: California, Mojave Desert, Joshua Tree National Park
joshua-tree.season: October–April; best October–November and February–April (October and March according to Mountain Project); December–January is cool with short days and occasional snow, but excellent friction for bouldering; May to September brings desert heat of +30…+38 °C
joshua-tree.transfer: A car is needed: ~1 h from Palm Springs, ~2.5–3 h from Los Angeles; gear and guides at the Nomad Ventures shop in Joshua Tree village
joshua-tree.rock_note: quartz monzonite: grainy domes and rock “piles” in the desert, cracks, slabs with coarse crystalline texture; very harsh friction, with sand and “ball bearings” underfoot on rarely climbed routes
joshua-tree.approach: Most rocks are 2–15 min from the road and campgrounds (Hidden Valley, Intersection Rock); up to an hour across the desert to the more distant domes
joshua-tree.restrictions: National park entry is $30 per car for 7 days (card only). New bolts and replacing old ones only with a park permit; hangers must be rock-coloured, and using plants for anchors is prohibited. Annual closures for nesting owls and falcons at certain rocks (in 2026: 17 February – 7 June: Right On, Orange Flake, Fat Freddie's Cat, Freak Brothers Dome and others). The park's campgrounds have about 500 sites and fill up quickly in season; most have no water — bring your own.
joshua-tree.guidebook: Joshua Tree Rock Climbs (Randy Vogel) and Joshua Tree Bouldering; online — Mountain Project
joshua-tree.stay: Park campgrounds Hidden Valley (in the heart of the rocks), Ryan, Jumbo Rocks, Indian Cove; BLM sites near the park boundary take the overflow; motels and Airbnbs in Joshua Tree and Twentynine Palms
pros: Huge choice of short routes and problems within walking distance of the car
A great winter destination with dry, sunny weather
Lots of easy routes and schools for beginners
Campgrounds right among the rocks
cons: Few sport routes — trad skills and cams needed
Too hot in summer
Abrasive, grainy rock — wears out skin and ropes
Campgrounds packed at weekends in season
joshua-tree.airport: PSP — Palm Springs, ~1 h; ONT — Ontario, ~2 h; LAX — Los Angeles, ~2.5–3 h
school_notes: Small guide service, half-day and full-day outings
Year-round instruction, owned by AMGA guides
Family-run school, sessions for all levels and for kids, gear included
Courses for all levels

new-river-gorge.description: The deep, forested gorge of the New River in West Virginia, ringed by cliffs of very hard sandstone — one of the main areas on the US East Coast and a national park since 2020. Sport and trad are equally good here: the technical vertical walls of the Endless Wall, the overhangs of Summersville Lake (up to 5.15a) and classic cracks. The hub of climbing life is the town of Fayetteville.
new-river-gorge.rating_basis: One of the largest areas in the eastern US: ~2,400 routes and problems on Mountain Project (~18k views a month), with MP itself citing “more than 3,000 routes”; famous for the quality of its sandstone and technical sport and trad
new-river-gorge.hazards: Ticks, poison ivy and copperheads, wet, muddy trails after rain, sparse bolts on older routes
new-river-gorge.crowd_note: On autumn weekends (especially during the Bridge Day festival in October) the popular Endless Wall and Bridge Buttress are busy; quiet on weekdays
new-river-gorge.region: West Virginia, New River Gorge National Park (near the town of Fayetteville)
new-river-gorge.season: spring (April–May) and autumn (September–October) are the best times, but multi-day rain spells happen; summer is hot and humid — the shady, breezy Summersville Lake crags are the escape; in winter people climb only on sunny days on south-facing walls
new-river-gorge.transfer: A car is needed: ~1 h from Charleston, ~5 h from Washington
new-river-gorge.rock_note: very hard, iron-rich Nuttall sandstone (almost quartzite in places): vertical and overhanging walls of 12–45 m above the river, horizontal breaks, cracks and arêtes; technical climbing, bolts more spaced than at the Red River Gorge
new-river-gorge.approach: 5–30 min along forest trails from the rim of the gorge; at the Endless Wall you descend to the base via ladders
new-river-gorge.restrictions: Most crags lie within New River Gorge National Park (since 2020): fixed draws are prohibited, new routes only with a paid NPS permit, rebolting only with permission via the local NRAC coalition; groups of no more than 15 at Bridge Buttress and 10 at other crags; on single-pitch routes lowering is preferred over rappelling. Summersville Lake is managed by the US Army Corps of Engineers — there are no bolting restrictions there.
new-river-gorge.guidebook: New River Rock (Mike Williams); online — Mountain Project
new-river-gorge.stay: The American Alpine Club (AAC) campground near Lansing with showers and tent platforms ($8–30, book ahead), Chestnut Creek and Ray's, motels and guesthouses in Fayetteville
pros: Top-quality sandstone
Good balance of sport and trad
Shady Summersville Lake crags for summer
Convenient AAC campground and the climbing town of Fayetteville
cons: Few easy routes; the best walls need 6c sport / 6a trad
Frequent multi-day rain spells in spring and autumn
Muggy summers
Fixed draws are prohibited in the national park
new-river-gorge.airport: CRW — Charleston (West Virginia), ~1 h; ROA — Roanoke, ~2.5 h
famous_lines: The Greatest Show on Earth 5.13a (7c+, trad)
Four Sheets to the Wind 5.9+ (5c, trad)
school_notes: Since 1994: beginner courses (1–2 days), intermediate, sport climbing, self-rescue
Half-day and full-day outings, can be combined with rafting

red-river-gorge.description: A forested gorge in Kentucky with thousands of sport routes on solid sandstone — one of North America's top sport climbing destinations. It's famous for the huge overhangs of the Motherlode and Drive-By, long endurance routes and the fact that you can climb under the roofs even in the rain. Climbing life revolves around the campground and pizzeria at Miguel's.
red-river-gorge.rating_basis: One of the best-known sport destinations in the US: ~4,100 routes and problems on Mountain Project (~28k views a month), UKClimbing calls it “world-class”; famous for its overhangs and 7a–8c endurance routes
red-river-gorge.hazards: Ticks, poison ivy and snakes (copperheads, rattlesnakes), slippery sandstone on the approaches after rain, heat and humidity in summer
red-river-gorge.crowd_note: On autumn weekends the Motherlode, Drive-By and Muir Valley are busy and Miguel's is noisy; quieter on weekdays and at the more distant sectors
red-river-gorge.season: March–May and September–November; best April and October–November; summer is hot and very humid (climb early in the morning and in the evening in the shade); winter has good sunny days, but the weather is unstable
red-river-gorge.transfer: By car only: ~1 h from Lexington (80 km via the Mountain Parkway), ~2 h from Louisville and Cincinnati
red-river-gorge.rock_note: dense orange sandstone with “iron” pockets, horizontal breaks and giant overhanging amphitheatres (the Motherlode, Drive-By); long endurance routes of 25–35 m
red-river-gorge.approach: 5–45 min along forest trails from the car parks; some PMRP sectors require a high-clearance vehicle
red-river-gorge.restrictions: Most sport sectors are on private land: at PMRP, MFRP and BRRP (owned by the Red River Gorge Climbers' Coalition) you must sign a liability waiver, overnight parking is prohibited and dogs must be leashed; at Muir Valley — waiver and paid parking (~$15), no dogs; at Graining Fork (Roadside Crag) — a limited number of daily passes. In the Northern Gorge (national forest) backcountry camping requires an inexpensive permit, and fixed draws are not allowed.
red-river-gorge.guidebook: Red River Gorge Rock Climbs South and North (Wolverine Publishing), Best of the Red (Sharp End Books); online guide redriverclimbing.com
red-river-gorge.stay: The legendary climbers' campground at Miguel's Pizza (with a gear shop), Lago Linda's, Land of the Arches with showers, the Sky Bridge Station and Rustic Red hostels, Red River Outdoors cabins
pros: Thousands of sport routes at all grades, especially 6b–8b
Giant overhangs — climbable in the rain
Cheap climbers' campgrounds and the scene at Miguel's
Lots of beginner routes in Muir Valley and the Northern Gorge
cons: Hot and muggy in summer, poor friction
Car needed, sometimes with high clearance
Some sectors are on private land — rules and paid parking
Little bouldering or multi-pitch
red-river-gorge.airport: LEX — Lexington, ~1 h; SDF — Louisville, ~2 h; CVG — Cincinnati, ~2 h
school_notes: The gorge's oldest guide service: half-day and full-day climbing, groups of up to 6
Guides and courses for individuals and groups, book in advance

rifle-mountain-park.description: A narrow limestone canyon in the Colorado mountains — the top summer sport destination for strong climbers in the US. The routes stand right by the road and are long and steep, with a huge concentration of 7c–9a. The good “real” classics start at around 5.11 (6c).
rifle-mountain-park.rating_basis: Mountain Project calls Rifle “the best limestone sport climbing in North America”: ~510 sport routes, one of the largest concentrations of 5.13–5.14 in the US and the area's first 5.15a (Kinder Cakes)
rifle-mountain-park.hazards: Rockfall and breaking holds on new routes, polished holds, summer thunderstorms, long routes — check your rope length and tie a stopper knot
rifle-mountain-park.crowd_note: From May to September the popular walls (Project Wall, Arsenal, Meat Wall) are busy at weekends; the old classics are polished
rifle-mountain-park.region: Colorado, Western Slope of the Rockies, 20 km north of the town of Rifle
rifle-mountain-park.season: May–October; a narrow, shady canyon at ~2,150 m — a summer destination for when the rest of Colorado is too hot; best June–September; spring and late autumn are cold with seepage; in winter the canyon fills with ice (ice climbing)
rifle-mountain-park.transfer: A car is needed: ~1.25 h from Grand Junction (130 km), ~3.5 h from Denver on I-70
rifle-mountain-park.rock_note: blue-grey Leadville limestone in a narrow, shady canyon: steep, long endurance routes on pinches, pockets and flat holds, the Ruckman and Wicked caves; the old classics are heavily polished
rifle-mountain-park.approach: 1–10 min: most sectors are right by the dirt road along the canyon floor
rifle-mountain-park.restrictions: The park belongs to the city of Rifle: entry is $10 per car per day or a season pass; camping ~$20 a night (since 2025), most sites booked 3 months ahead via RoverPass. New routes only with permission; the crags by the fish hatchery in the western part of the canyon are closed to climbing. Climbers are asked to report bats on routes to Climbers for Bat Conservation.
rifle-mountain-park.guidebook: Rifle: A Climber's Guide (Derek Krol); route development is overseen by the Rifle Climbers Coalition
rifle-mountain-park.stay: City campgrounds in the canyon (Little Box, Blue Spruce), Rifle Falls and Rifle Gap state park campgrounds, free camping at The Meadows (4WD needed), motels in the town of Rifle (20 min)
pros: One of North America's best concentrations of hard 7c–9a+ routes
Shade all day — climbable in summer
1–10 min approach from the car
Campground right in the canyon
cons: Almost no routes for beginners and intermediates
Polished old classics
Crowded on summer weekends
Cold and damp in spring and autumn
rifle-mountain-park.airport: GJT — Grand Junction, ~1.25 h; EGE — Eagle/Vail, ~1.25 h; DEN — Denver, ~3.5 h

rmnp-bouldering.description: High-alpine bouldering at 3,000–3,400 m above the lakes of Rocky Mountain National Park — a summer destination for strong boulderers. The banded gneiss of Chaos Canyon and Emerald Lake offers problems mostly in the 7A–8B range and famous lines up to 8C, but you have to hike up to them carrying a crash pad.
rmnp-bouldering.rating_basis: PlanetMountain calls Chaos Canyon a “bouldering mecca”: alpine boulders 7A–8C at 3,000 m, with landmark V14–V15 ascents (Wheel of Chaos, Hypnotized Minds); Mountain Project describes ~200 problems in the main areas
rmnp-bouldering.hazards: Afternoon thunderstorms with lightning, altitude sickness, uneven rocky landings, sudden cold snaps and snow, elk and bears (don't leave food out), remoteness from help
rmnp-bouldering.crowd_note: In July–August the Bear Lake car park fills up by early morning; the Emerald Lake classics are busy at weekends, Upper Chaos is quieter
rmnp-bouldering.region: Colorado, Rocky Mountain National Park, Bear Lake area (near the town of Estes Park)
rmnp-bouldering.season: July–September; in early July some boulders are still under snow, October is cold with possible first snow; in summer there are thunderstorms almost every afternoon — start at dawn; November to June is winter, with snow at ~3,100–3,400 m
rmnp-bouldering.transfer: ~2 h by car from Denver to Estes Park, then 30–40 min to Bear Lake (or the shuttle from the Park & Ride)
rmnp-bouldering.rock_note: banded gneiss and granite in high-alpine canyons: large alpine boulders on moraines and by the lakes, overhangs and arêtes with positive holds, some tall problems over rocks
rmnp-bouldering.approach: 30 min to 2 h from the Bear Lake car park with a crash pad, up the trail to Emerald Lake and over boulders into Chaos Canyon (~250–500 m of ascent)
rmnp-bouldering.restrictions: From 22 May to 19 October 2026, entering the Bear Lake Road corridor between 5:00 and 18:00 requires a timed-entry reservation on Recreation.gov (released on the 1st of the previous month, $2 fee) plus a park entrance pass; from 2026 foreign visitors pay a $100 surcharge per person or buy a $250 non-resident pass. Leaving crash pads in the park is prohibited (they will be confiscated), fans and any motorised equipment are banned in the wilderness area, and you may not move rocks to build landings, break off holds or cut vegetation; waste goes in a wag bag. From 15 February to 31 July off-trail travel above the Loch Vale — Sky Pond trail is closed (raptors), plus a voluntary closure of the Meadow Boulder in Upper Chaos.
rmnp-bouldering.guidebook: RMNP bouldering guidebooks from Mount Julian Press; online — Mountain Project and Kaya
rmnp-bouldering.stay: Park campgrounds (Moraine Park, Glacier Basin — reservations required), motels and cabins in Estes Park (30–40 min to Bear Lake); free shuttles run from the Park & Ride
pros: World-class summer bouldering 7A–8C
Cool temperatures and good friction in July–September
Incredible alpine views and lakes
Can be combined with alpine climbing and trad in the park
cons: Almost no easy problems
Long uphill approach with crash pads, altitude of 3,000+ m
Entry reservations and expensive entry for foreigners
Daily afternoon thunderstorms, short season

smith-rock.description: The Crooked River canyon in the high desert of Central Oregon, where American sport climbing was born in the 1980s. Technical vertical routes on tuff, the legendary Monkey Face tower and basalt cracks in the gorge, from 5.7 to 5.14d.
smith-rock.rating_basis: The birthplace of American sport climbing: more than 1,500 routes on Mountain Project (~19k views a month); the first US 5.14a (To Bolt or Not to Be, 1986) and the first 8c+ (Just Do It) were climbed here
smith-rock.hazards: Ground falls before the first bolt and starts on sloping ground, loose rock on the upper ledges, rattlesnakes, poison ivy by the river, summer heat
smith-rock.crowd_note: On spring and autumn weekends there are queues for the classics on the Dihedrals and Morning Glory Wall, and the main car park fills up by morning
smith-rock.region: Oregon, Central Oregon, Smith Rock State Park (near the village of Terrebonne)
smith-rock.season: March–May and September–November; summer days often top +38 °C (climb early in the morning and in the shady sectors of the gorge); winter brings cold, dry, sunny days; nights are cold year-round
smith-rock.transfer: A car is needed: ~20 min from Redmond airport, ~40 min from Bend, ~2.5–3 h from Portland
smith-rock.rock_note: welded volcanic tuff: technical vertical faces with small edges and pockets, arêtes and dihedrals, the famous Monkey Face; columnar basalt with cracks in the Upper and Lower Gorge
smith-rock.approach: 10–45 min from the main car park across the bridge over the Crooked River to the Dihedrals, Morning Glory and Monkey Face
smith-rock.restrictions: Parking in the park costs $10 per car per day (season pass $30). Seasonal raptor nesting closures, usually from February to early August, affect The Monument, Kiss of the Lepers, Picnic Lunch Wall and part of the Smith Rock Group (current dates at smithrock.com/seasonal-closures). The first bolt is often ~4–5 m up and many routes start from a slope — bring a stick clip. Sleeping in cars and campfires are prohibited at the Bivy campground.
smith-rock.guidebook: Rock Climbing Smith Rock State Park (Alan Watts); online — Mountain Project
smith-rock.stay: Smith Bivy walk-in campground at the park entrance ($12 per person, showers, water, no cars or fires), Skull Hollow campground 13 km away (no water), motels and Airbnbs in Terrebonne, Redmond and Bend
pros: Historic sport classics at all levels
Dry, sunny climate, rain is rare
Cheap climbers' campground at the park entrance
Several accredited schools and guides
cons: Very hot in summer, cold in winter
High first bolts, some old anchors and bold spacing
Seasonal raptor closures on some walls
Lots of people at weekends
smith-rock.airport: RDM — Redmond/Bend, ~20 min; PDX — Portland, ~2.5–3 h
famous_lines: To Bolt or Not to Be 5.14a (8b+), the first 5.14 in the US, Dihedrals
school_notes: Guides with more than 20 years' experience in the park, gear for clients, based at a shop in Terrebonne
AMGA-accredited: instruction, guiding and camps for all ages
Operating in the park since 1983, AMGA-accredited

yosemite-valley.description: The world's most famous climbing valley: the granite walls of El Capitan and Half Dome, where big-wall climbing was born, along with the free ascents of The Nose and the Dawn Wall. The main style is trad on cracks and multi-pitch routes, plus historic bouldering at Camp 4 with the Midnight Lightning problem. In summer the action moves up to high-alpine Tuolumne Meadows in the same park.
yosemite-valley.rating_basis: The historic centre of American climbing; Mountain Project lists ~1,900 routes and problems in the valley and ~3,200 across the national park, with about 46k page views a month; El Capitan and Half Dome appear on every world top list
yosemite-valley.hazards: Rockfall (including major collapses from El Capitan), thunderstorms and sudden bad weather on multi-day walls, heat and dehydration in summer, bears in the campgrounds (store food in metal lockers), long descents after routes
yosemite-valley.crowd_note: In spring and autumn there are queues and “traffic jams” on The Nose, Royal Arches, Nutcracker and other classics; campgrounds and car parks overflow, and in summer park entry may be temporarily closed
yosemite-valley.region: California, Sierra Nevada, Yosemite National Park
yosemite-valley.season: April–June and September–October in the valley; in July–August the valley is hot (+32…+35 °C) — climb early in the morning and in the shade, while most of the action moves to Tuolumne Meadows (2,600 m; the Tioga Pass road is open roughly from late May to October–November); winters are rainy and snowy, but bouldering is good on dry days
yosemite-valley.transfer: A car is essential, or YARTS buses from Merced (Amtrak train) / Fresno; ~1.5–2 h from Fresno, ~4 h from San Francisco
yosemite-valley.rock_note: pale, monolithic granite: perfect cracks of every size, slabs with micro-features, walls up to 1,000 m high (El Capitan, Half Dome)
yosemite-valley.approach: 5–30 min from the road to the base of most walls and to the Swan Slab; 1–3 h to the starts on Half Dome and some other walls; bouldering right in Camp 4 and along the road
yosemite-valley.restrictions: Paid national park entry ($35 per car for 7 days); from 2026 foreign visitors pay a $100 surcharge per person or buy a $250 non-resident America the Beautiful annual pass. Camp 4 is by reservation only on Recreation.gov — dates are released a week ahead at 7:00 Pacific time and go in minutes; other campgrounds are booked months ahead. Bivying on a big wall requires a free climbers' wilderness permit. Each year from 1 March to 15 July some walls are closed for nesting peregrine falcons. New bolts may only be placed with a hand drill, “gardening” cracks is prohibited, all rubbish and waste must be carried off the wall, and tick marks brushed off.
yosemite-valley.guidebook: Yosemite Valley Free Climbs (SuperTopo, Don Reid / Chris McNamara) and Yosemite Big Walls (SuperTopo); for bouldering, Yosemite Valley Bouldering (Matt Wilder)
yosemite-valley.stay: The legendary Camp 4 climbers' campground (book a week ahead), other valley campgrounds (book months ahead), Yosemite Valley Lodge, Curry Village; cheaper motels in El Portal, Mariposa and Groveland (30–60 min)
pros: Legendary big walls and the world's best cracks
Huge choice of multi-pitch classics from 5.7 to 5.14
Historic bouldering at Camp 4
An official school and guides in the park
Stunning scenery and waterfalls for rest days
cons: Few sport routes — trad skills and a rack of cams needed
Very crowded and campgrounds hard to book
Hot in the valley in summer, rain and snow in winter
Expensive entry for foreigners from 2026
yosemite-valley.airport: FAT — Fresno, ~2 h; SFO / OAK — San Francisco, ~4 h
famous_lines: The Nose 5.9 C2 / free 5.14a (8b+), El Capitan
Midnight Lightning V8 (7B), Columbia Boulder, Camp 4
school_notes: The national park's official school: beginner, crack, anchor and multi-pitch courses, a big-wall seminar, guided ascents of Half Dome and El Capitan; some gear for rent, free helmets on courses

cat-ba-lan-ha-bay.description: Cat Ba Island on the edge of Ha Long Bay is Vietnam's main spot for deep-water soloing (DWS): hundreds of lines on the undercut karst islands of Lan Ha Bay. The island itself has sport sectors, the best being Butterfly Valley. For pure sport climbing it's also worth visiting Huu Lung on the mainland, 2 hours from Hanoi.
cat-ba-lan-ha-bay.rating_basis: One of the few DWS areas in the world (230+ lines on 24 crags) plus 200+ sport routes (Mountain Project); but the volume and difficulty are more modest than in Thailand and Laos, and access is regulated
cat-ba-lan-ha-bay.hazards: Shallow water and submerged rocks at low tide (DWS), heat and humidity, typhoons in summer, rusty fixed gear on older routes
cat-ba-lan-ha-bay.crowd_note: Few climbers; tourist crowds only in town and on the bay cruises
cat-ba-lan-ha-bay.region: Haiphong, Cat Ba Island by Ha Long Bay
cat-ba-lan-ha-bay.season: April–May and September–December; DWS June–November (needs a tide above 2.2 m); cool and drizzly in winter, heat and typhoons in summer
cat-ba-lan-ha-bay.transfer: From Hanoi by bus + ferry to Cat Ba town, ~4–4.5 h; Haiphong airport is closer
cat-ba-lan-ha-bay.rock_note: limestone karst islands: towers undercut at the waterline for DWS; on Cat Ba, steep walls with tufas (Butterfly Valley)
cat-ba-lan-ha-bay.approach: On Cat Ba, 10–20 min by scooter from town and a short walk-in; the crags in the bay and all DWS by boat only
cat-ba-lan-ha-bay.restrictions: A UNESCO site controlled by the national park and the military: access to the crags is via a climbing company's pass, a fee to the landowner or a national park fee; DWS only with a licensed guide and boat. The mainland alternative is Huu Lung (Lang Son province): 120+ sport routes 4+…8b, with homestays by the crags
cat-ba-lan-ha-bay.guidebook: Vietnam Rock Climbing Guidebook / Vietnam Climbing (500+ routes: sport, DWS, trad; covers Cat Ba and Huu Lung)
cat-ba-lan-ha-bay.stay: Hotels and hostels in Cat Ba town; scooter rental
pros: World-class DWS in Ha Long Bay
Fairy-tale scenery
Few climbers
cons: Complicated access rules and fees

rocklands.description: Rocklands is a vast field of orange sandstone boulders in the northern Cederberg and one of the planet's top bouldering destinations. More than four thousand problems from easy slabs to 8C+, roofs and pinchy arêtes, San rock art and desert scenery. The season is the southern winter, when it's dry and cool.
rocklands.rating_basis: One of the world's best bouldering areas: 4,300+ problems up to 8C+ (Wikipedia), opened up by Todd Skinner and Fred Nicole in 1996, an annual mecca for the strongest boulderers
rocklands.hazards: Snakes (Cape cobra, adders), baboons, ticks, sharp rock; winter nights can be around freezing
rocklands.crowd_note: In July international teams and film crews gather at the classics, but the field is huge — there are plenty of free boulders
rocklands.region: Western Cape, northern Cederberg, Pakhuis Pass
rocklands.season: April–September (southern winter); best May–August — dry, cool, excellent friction; hot in summer (November–March)
rocklands.transfer: ~3 h by car from Cape Town on the N7 via Clanwilliam (20 min from Rocklands); a car is essential
rocklands.rock_note: dense, bright orange Cederberg quartzitic sandstone: roofs, arêtes, pinches, friction slabs
rocklands.approach: 2–30 min on foot from the farm campgrounds and parking areas along the Pakhuis Pass road; a car is essential
rocklands.restrictions: All sectors (the CapeNature reserve and private farms) only with a valid permit bought online; since 2013 one landowner has closed their land (Tea Garden and the areas from Klein Kliphuis towards Clanwilliam) — trespassers are fined. Don't touch the rock art; brush off chalk and tick marks
rocklands.guidebook: Rocklands Bouldering South Africa (Cordee); online topos on theCrag and 27crags
rocklands.stay: Farm campgrounds and cottages by the rocks: De Pakhuys, Traveller's Rest, Kleinfontein, Eight Day Rain, Kliphuis (CapeNature); book ahead for July
pros: Thousands of problems at every grade
Excellent winter friction
Accommodation and campgrounds right by the boulders
Easy to combine with Cape Town and Waterval Boven
cons: Permit mandatory, some land closed
Impossible without a car
Far from shops (Clanwilliam)

waterval-boven.description: A village by a waterfall on the Elands River, renamed Emgwenya, and South Africa's sport climbing capital. Hundreds of bolted routes on ancient orange quartzite on the crags around the valley, all just minutes from the car. Easy to combine with a trip to Kruger Park or Rocklands.
waterval-boven.rating_basis: South Africa's main sport climbing area: 700+ bolted routes according to the MCSA (1,000+ according to Mountain Project) within 8 km of the village, orange quartzite, grades 5.4–5.14
waterval-boven.hazards: Thunderstorms and lightning in summer, snakes and ticks, sharp quartzite; it's best not to leave valuables in the car
waterval-boven.crowd_note: Crowded only on long weekends and during South African school holidays
waterval-boven.season: March–November; best April–October (dry southern winter, sunny sectors); afternoon thunderstorms in summer
waterval-boven.transfer: ~3 h from Johannesburg on the N4 (≈240 km); ~1 h from Mbombela (Nelspruit)
waterval-boven.rock_note: orange quartzite ~2.3 billion years old: vertical and moderately overhanging, roofs, sharp edges
waterval-boven.approach: All crags are within 8 km of the village: 5–20 min on foot from the parking areas; Wonderland is reached from Tranquilitas farm
waterval-boven.restrictions: No climbing permit needed; no littering or graffiti; some crags are on private farms — park in the designated places
waterval-boven.guidebook: Local Waterval Boven guidebook (PDF), also sold at Roc'n Rope; topos on theCrag and 27crags
waterval-boven.stay: Roc'n Rope Climber's Lodge in the village (dorms and doubles), Orange House for groups; Tranquilitas farm — camping, chalets and safari tents by the Wonderland sectors
pros: Huge choice of routes close to the village
Climbable almost year-round
Cheap accommodation for climbers
Kruger Park nearby for a rest day
cons: Afternoon thunderstorms in summer
Car needed
Little information in Russian
